workouts.notes: A first snatch session using a PVC pipe and an empty bar. The goal is positions and timing, so add weight only when every rep looks the same.

workouts.name: Beginner Clean and Jerk Technique
workouts.notes: Teaches the clean from the hang and the jerk from the rack with light loads. Stay light until the elbows are fast and the dip is straight.

workouts.name: Snatch Day
workouts.notes: A full snatch session for lifters with consistent technique. Work up to the listed sets and add a kilo or two only when no reps are missed.

workouts.name: Clean and Jerk Day
workouts.notes: Heavy cleans and jerks followed by pulls and squats. Percentages for the pull are based on your best clean.

workouts.name: Power and Hang Day
workouts.notes: A lighter, faster day between heavy sessions. Every lift is caught high, so bar speed matters more than load.

workouts.name: Positions and Pulls
workouts.notes: Moderate loads and more reps to build the legs, back, and shoulders that hold the lifts together. Keep rests tight.

workouts.name: Speed Under the Bar
workouts.notes: Drills that take away the pull so the only option is to move fast under the bar. Use light loads and short rests, and stop if the catch gets sloppy.

workouts.name: PVC Mobility Reset
workouts.notes: An easy session with a PVC pipe for rest days. It keeps the overhead and squat positions open without adding fatigue.

workouts.name: Mat Flow Circuit
workouts.notes: The classic abdominal series run back to back with very little rest, so the work stays continuous. Move with control and keep the transitions tight. Add a second lap of the first five moves when it gets easy.

workouts.name: Advanced Control Mat
workouts.notes: The hard end of the mat work: long levers, full roll-ups, and bodyweight supports. Quality over quantity, so stop a set when your lower back lifts or you start to jerk. Earn this session with the foundations one first.

workouts.name: Back Line and Posture
workouts.notes: Balances all the forward-curling work with back extension, glutes, and shoulder support. Keep the stomach lifted on every face-down move. Kicks and side work are per side.

workouts.name: Mat Foundations
workouts.notes: A first Pilates session built from the beginner mat moves. Learn to keep the lower back anchored and the breath steady. Add reps slowly before moving to the flow circuit.

workouts.name: Spine Release
workouts.notes: Gentle spinal movement in every direction: rounding, twisting, and light extension. Keep the effort low and let the breath set the pace.

workouts.name: Easy Walk and Move Circuit
workouts.notes: A gentle, joint-friendly session for days when you want to move without pounding. Keep a pace at which you can still talk; add a round when it feels easy.

workouts.name: Balance and Strength for Older Adults
workouts.notes: A steady session to build leg strength and balance for daily life. Stay close to a sturdy support, move slowly, and aim to do it twice a week; progress by using less hand support.

workouts.name: Shoulder Care
workouts.notes: Light band work for the rotator cuff and upper back. Use a band that lets you finish every rep smoothly; add reps before moving to a thicker band.

workouts.name: Desk Reset
workouts.notes: A ten-minute break for anyone who sits most of the day. Nothing here should feel like a strain; do it once mid-morning and once mid-afternoon.

workouts.name: Full-Body Foam Roll
workouts.notes: A slow pass over the areas that get stiff from training. Keep pressure firm but comfortable and breathe normally; one side per set.

workouts.name: Evening Downshift
workouts.notes: A quiet routine for the end of the day. Hold each stretch gently and let the breathing slow you down.

workouts.name: Foot and Ankle Care
workouts.notes: Easy work for feet, ankles and shins. Good after long days standing or as a warm-up before a walk.

workouts.name: First Run: Run-Walk
workouts.notes: A starter session for new or returning runners: one minute of easy running, four minutes of walking, four times. Repeat it three days a week and only add running time once it feels comfortable.

workouts.name: Incline and Climb
workouts.notes: Low-impact gym cardio that keeps the heart rate up by climbing instead of running. Keep your hands off the rails and raise the incline before the speed.

workouts.name: Hill Strength Session
workouts.notes: Hill repeats are strength work for runners. Run each one hard but even, jog or walk down, and add a repeat every week or two.

workouts.name: Tempo and Strides
workouts.notes: Twenty minutes at a comfortably hard effort, bracketed by drills and strides. If you cannot hold the pace evenly, split the tempo into two blocks with a short jog between.

workouts.name: Long Run with Cadence Work
workouts.notes: The weekly long run at conversation pace, opened with a few minutes of step-rate practice. Extend the long run by a few minutes at a time, not by big jumps.

workouts.name: Recovery Jog and Mobility
workouts.notes: An easy jog and four stretches for the day after a hard run. If the jog does not feel easy, walk it.

workouts.name: Agility Day: Ladders, Cones and Reaction
workouts.notes: Footwork first, then cone patterns, then reacting to a partner. Keep every rep sharp and stop a drill when your feet get sloppy; add a round before adding speed.

workouts.name: Speed Day: Acceleration
workouts.notes: For field and court athletes who want a faster first 20 metres. Rest fully between sprints so every rep is fast; progress by adding one rep, not by cutting rest.

workouts.name: Plyo Day: Jump and Rebound
workouts.notes: Low total contacts, high quality. Start with a landing primer, then go from short rebounds to bigger jumps; add contacts only when every landing is quiet.

workouts.name: Rotational Power
workouts.notes: For throwing, striking and swinging sports. Throws are fast and light, cable work is controlled; raise ball speed before ball weight.

workouts.name: In-Season Maintenance
workouts.notes: One short session a week to hold strength and power during the competitive season without adding fatigue. Keep two reps in reserve on everything.

workouts.name: Landing Mechanics for Beginners
workouts.notes: Learn to land before you learn to jump. Every rep ends in a quiet, balanced hold with knees over toes; move to the next drill only when the current one looks the same every time.

workouts.name: Barbell Density Circuit
workouts.notes: For lifters who want to burn more without leaving the barbell. Keep loads moderate, move with purpose between lifts, and add a set before adding weight.

workouts.name: Squat Builder: Low Bar and Pauses
workouts.notes: A squat-focused day for lifters chasing a bigger competition squat. Add 2.5 kg to the low-bar sets when all five sets of four move cleanly.

workouts.name: Bench Builder: Pause and Lockout
workouts.notes: Builds a competition-style bench with a real pause, then trains the lockout. Progress the paused sets first and keep the accessories smooth.

workouts.name: Deadlift Builder: Floor Speed and Lockout
workouts.notes: For lifters whose deadlift stalls off the floor or at the knees. Keep every pause honest and add load only when the bar stays close.

workouts.name: Weak Point Day: Dead Stops
workouts.notes: An advanced session that removes the bounce from all three lifts. Use it once a week in place of a regular heavy day and progress slowly.

workouts.name: Powerlifter Volume Day
workouts.notes: Higher reps on squat, bench, and hinge variations to hold muscle while leaning out. Keep rests short and leave one or two reps in reserve.

workouts.name: Technique Day: Box and Hinge
workouts.notes: A lighter lower-body day for newer lifters to groove depth and the hip hinge. Raise the load only when every rep looks the same.

workouts.name: Lifter Reset: Hips, Back, Shoulders
workouts.notes: An easy session for the day after heavy squats or deadlifts. Move slowly, breathe, and stop every stretch short of strain.

workouts.name: Gym Strongman Starter
workouts.notes: A first strongman session for any gym: dumbbells and one sandbag, no special implements. Pick loads you can carry without leaning, and add distance or time before weight.

workouts.name: Carry and Drag Medley
workouts.notes: Moderate loads moved for time with short rests: carries, drags and a sled push. Walk tall on every length and stop a set when posture goes, not when grip does.

workouts.name: Overhead Day: Log and Axle
workouts.notes: Heavy pressing with the two main strongman overhead implements. Clean every rep of the first lift, then save the grip and back by pressing the log from the rack.

workouts.name: Moving Day: Yoke and Farmers
workouts.notes: Heavy squats first, then short, heavy runs with the yoke and farmer's handles. Add load only when you can cover the distance without setting the implement down.

workouts.name: Ground to Shoulder: Stones and Tire
workouts.notes: Deadlifts build the pull, then stones, the tire and the sandbag turn it into loading strength. Keep the reps low and crisp, and swap the stone for a sandbag if your gym has none.

workouts.name: Odd-Object Volume
workouts.notes: Moderate loads for more reps with shorter rests to build muscle and work capacity together. Use a sandbag in place of the keg or stone wherever you need to.

workouts.name: Light Carry Reset
workouts.notes: Easy carries and stretches for the day after heavy implements. Loads stay light enough to breathe through the nose the whole time.

workouts.name: Power Flow: Sun Salutation Builder
workouts.notes: A continuous flow that keeps the heart rate up with no jumping. Each Sun Salutation set is three rounds; hold standing poses on each side. Add a round per week as it gets easier.

workouts.name: Standing Strength Series
workouts.notes: Long holds in the big standing poses build leg and hip strength you can feel. Do every hold on both sides and sink a little deeper before you add time.

workouts.name: Balance and Core Flow
workouts.notes: Single-leg balances and core holds that tighten up control without equipment. Balance holds are per side. Progress by lengthening holds before adding sets.

workouts.name: Hip and Hamstring Reset
workouts.notes: A slow lower-body session for the day after heavy legs or a long day of sitting. Stretch holds are per side. Breathe out slowly and never push into pain.

workouts.name: Desk Undo: Shoulders, Spine, and Ankles
workouts.notes: Opens the upper back, shoulders, and ankles that stiffen with desk work. Good as a warm-up before lifting or on its own. Move slowly and stay in a pain-free range.

workouts.name: Evening Wind-Down
workouts.notes: A floor-based session to settle down before bed. Nothing here should feel like effort. Stay longer in any pose that feels good.

workouts.name: Power Flow Burner
workouts.notes: For anyone who wants a sweat without a single jump or weight — strength holds strung into a continuous flow keep your heart rate up the whole time. Progress by adding 10 seconds to each hold before you shorten the rests.

workouts.name: Dynamic Mobility Sweat Circuit
workouts.notes: Mobility work programmed like a conditioning circuit — you drill full ranges of motion while your heart rate climbs, so stiff hips and a calorie burn get handled in one session. Progress by trimming the rests toward 20 seconds.

workouts.name: Yoga Strength: Holds & Balance
workouts.notes: Isometric strength for lifters and yogis alike — long holds, single-leg balance, and pike pressing build shoulders and a midline that carry over to every barbell lift. Progress by extending holds 5 seconds a week before adding reps.

workouts.name: Vinyasa Flow: Foundations
workouts.notes: A repeatable flow day for lifters cutting calories — enough movement to keep the deficit on track without eating into recovery from your strength sessions. Progress by holding each pose one breath longer each week.

workouts.name: Vinyasa Flow: Balance & Hips
workouts.notes: The flow day for people whose squats feel stiff — single-leg balance plus deep hip openers, with just enough work density to count toward the week's activity. Progress by moving from fingertip support to hands-free on the balance holds.

workouts.name: Core + Hip Control
workouts.notes: Anti-extension and anti-rotation core work paired with hip openers — the session that makes your waist look trained and your hips move like they should. Progress the holds before the reps: quality beats quantity here.

workouts.name: Morning Full-Body Wake-Up
workouts.notes: Fifteen unhurried minutes to shake off sleep stiffness before coffee — spine, hips, and shoulders all get a pass. Nothing here should feel like effort; if it does, back off the range.

workouts.name: Desk Reset: Hips + T-Spine
workouts.notes: Built for anyone who sits eight hours a day — every drill targets the two areas a chair locks up: hip flexors and the mid-back. Do it on lunch breaks or after work; consistency matters more than depth.

workouts.name: Hamstring & Posterior Chain Release
workouts.notes: The day-after-deadlifts session — long, easy stretches down the whole back line from calves to lats. Ease into each hold over the first 10 seconds; you should be able to breathe slowly the entire time.

workouts.name: Yin: Long Deep Holds
workouts.notes: Two-minute passive holds that let connective tissue actually let go — the deepest flexibility work in the catalog. Settle to about 70 percent of your max stretch and stay there; sinking deeper happens on its own.

workouts.name: Pre-Sleep Wind-Down
workouts.notes: The last fifteen minutes before bed — slow, floor-based shapes that downshift the nervous system so you fall asleep faster. Dim the lights, breathe out longer than you breathe in, and never push into a stretch.

exercises.name: First Position Plié
instructions: Stand side-on to your support with heels together and toes turned out only as far as your hips allow.
Rest one hand lightly on the support and stand tall through the spine.
Bend your knees out over your toes, keeping your heels down and your torso upright.
Lower as far as you can with the heels on the floor, then press down and straighten slowly.
exercises.formCue: Knees over toes, tall spine, heels down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Forcing the feet wider than the hips can turn so the knees roll inward, or tipping the chest forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a smaller turnout and a shallower bend, with both hands on the support.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the basic barre knee bend and it trains the hips, knees, and feet to line up.

exercises.name: Second Position Plié
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than your hips and toes turned out, one hand resting on your support.
Lengthen your spine and keep your shoulders over your hips.
Bend your knees out over your toes and lower your hips straight down.
Stop when your thighs approach level or your form starts to change.
Press through your whole foot to rise and squeeze your inner thighs at the top.
exercises.formCue: Hips drop straight down between the heels.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the knees fall in front of the toes line, or sticking the hips back and leaning forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Take a narrower stance and a smaller bend, holding the support with both hands.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The wide turned-out stance loads the inner thighs and glutes with little impact.

exercises.name: Relevé
instructions: Stand tall with feet parallel or heels together and one hand on your support.
Press through the balls of your feet and rise smoothly onto them.
Keep your ankles straight, with the weight over the big and second toes.
Pause at the top, then lower your heels slowly to the floor.
exercises.formCue: Rise straight up, ankles stay in line.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rolling out toward the little toes, or dropping down fast.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the support with both hands and rise only part way.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the calves and ankles and sharpens balance on the forefoot.

exercises.name: Plié Pulse
instructions: Set up in a wide turned-out stance with one hand on your support.
Lower into your plié and hold near the bottom.
Pulse up and down a few centimetres, staying low and keeping the knees over the toes.
Keep your torso upright and your breathing steady.
Finish the set, then press slowly to standing.
exercises.formCue: Small range, stay low, stay tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing with a big range, or letting the knees drift inward as the legs tire.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the low position without pulsing, or stay higher in the bend.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Small pulses under tension build muscular endurance without any impact.

exercises.name: Tendu
exercises.musclesWorked: Feet, calves, hip stabilisers, inner thighs
instructions: Stand tall with heels together and one hand on your support.
Slide one foot along the floor to the front, side, or back until only the toes touch.
Keep both knees straight and your hips level and still.
Draw the foot back along the floor to the start, pressing through the ball of the foot.
Repeat in each direction, then switch legs.
exercises.formCue: Brush the floor out and back, hips quiet.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting the foot instead of sliding it, or shifting the hips toward the working leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work in parallel rather than turned out, and hold the support with both hands.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the feet and arches and teaches you to balance on one leg while the other moves.

exercises.name: Arabesque Lift
instructions: Face your support and hold it with both hands, standing tall.
Slide one leg straight back until the toes rest on the floor behind you.
Lift the leg a small way without tipping your chest forward or arching your back.
Pause, lower to tap the toes, and repeat.
Finish all reps, then switch legs.
exercises.formCue: Lift from the glute, keep the chest up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching the lower back or opening the hip to the side to lift higher.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift only a few centimetres and bend the standing knee slightly.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the glutes and trains balance on the standing leg.

exercises.name: Standing Side Leg Lift
instructions: Stand side-on to your support and rest one hand on it.
Stand tall with both hips facing forward.
Lift the outside leg out to the side with the toes pointing forward.
Go only as high as you can without leaning, then lower slowly.
Complete the reps and repeat on the other leg.
exercises.formCue: Body stays tall as the leg goes out.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning away from the lifting leg, or turning the toes up so the hip flexors take over.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift lower and hold the support with both hands.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the outer hip muscles that steady the pelvis when you walk and balance.

exercises.name: Curtsy Lunge Pulse
instructions: Stand tall and step one foot back and across behind the other leg.
Bend both knees and lower with your chest upright and front knee over the front heel.
Stay low and pulse up and down a few centimetres.
Push through the front foot to return to standing.
Finish the set and switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Chest up, front knee over the heel.
exercises.commonMistakes: Twisting the hips and letting the front knee collapse inward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Skip the pulses, take a smaller step, and hold a support for balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The crossed stance puts extra work into the glutes and outer hip of the front leg.

exercises.name: Clamshell
instructions: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent, feet together, and head resting on your lower arm.
Stack your hips one over the other.
Keep your feet touching and lift the top knee without letting your hips roll back.
Pause, then lower the knee slowly.
Finish the reps and turn over for the other side.
exercises.formCue: Feet together, hips stacked, knee opens.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rolling the top hip backward, or opening so far that the pelvis moves.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lie with your back against a wall to stop the hips rolling, and use a smaller range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It targets the outer hip muscles that keep the knee and pelvis steady.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Leg Lift
instructions: Lie on your side with the bottom knee bent for balance and the top leg straight in line with your body.
Stack your hips and shoulders.
Lift the top leg just high enough to feel the outer hip working, toes pointing forward.
Lower slowly without resting between reps.
Complete the set and switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Lead with the heel, hips stacked.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rolling the hips back, or lifting so high that the waist does the work.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lie with your back against a wall and use a smaller lift.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It isolates the outer hip with no load on the spine or knees.

exercises.name: Fire Hydrant
instructions: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Brace your trunk and keep your back flat.
Keep the knee bent and lift one leg out to the side.
Pause briefly without letting your trunk rotate, then lower with control.
Finish the reps and switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Leg moves, trunk stays square to the floor.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning away from the lifting leg, or letting the back sag or twist.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift the knee only a little, or do the Clamshell instead.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the outer hips while the core works to keep the trunk still.

exercises.name: Donkey Kick
instructions: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Brace your trunk so your back stays flat.
Keep the knee bent and lift one leg, pressing the sole of the foot toward the ceiling.
Stop before your lower back starts to arch.
Lower with control, finish the reps, then switch legs.
exercises.formCue: Squeeze the glute, keep the back flat.
exercises.commonMistakes: Kicking too high and arching the lower back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a smaller range, or rest on your forearms.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the glutes on their own with the spine held steady.

exercises.name: Seated March
instructions: Sit upright away from the back of the chair with feet flat on the floor.
Hold the sides of the seat lightly.
Lift one knee as high as is comfortable, keeping the knee bent.
Lower the foot with control and lift the other knee.
Keep alternating at a steady rhythm, sitting tall.
exercises.formCue: Sit tall, lift the knee, place the foot down softly.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning back as the knee lifts, or dropping the foot down hard.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift the heel only, or march more slowly.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It raises the heart rate and works the hips with no balance demand.

exercises.name: Seated Knee Extension
instructions: Sit tall near the front of a sturdy chair with both feet flat on the floor.
Slowly straighten one knee until the leg is level with the floor.
Hold for a moment with the thigh still on the seat.
Lower the foot slowly to the floor.
Finish the reps on one leg, then switch.
exercises.formCue: Straighten slowly, pause, lower slowly.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swinging the leg up, or slumping back as the leg lifts.
exercises.beginnerModification: Straighten only part way, or slide the heel along the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the front of the thigh from a fully supported seat.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
instructions: Lie back on a bench set to roughly 30 to 45 degrees and take a grip a little wider than your shoulders.
Unrack the bar and hold it over your upper chest with your shoulder blades pulled back and down.
Lower the bar under control to your upper chest with your forearms vertical.
Press back up until your arms are straight without letting your shoulders roll forward.
exercises.formCue: Shoulder blades pinned, bar to the collarbone line.
exercises.commonMistakes: Setting the bench too steep so it becomes a shoulder press, and bouncing the bar off the chest.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the incline machine press or light dumbbells until the bar path feels steady.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It loads the upper chest harder than a flat press does.

exercises.name: Decline Barbell Press
exercises.musclesWorked: Lower and mid chest, triceps, front delts
instructions: Hook your feet under the leg brace and lie back on the decline bench.
Grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders and unrack it over your chest.
Lower the bar under control to your lower chest.
Press back up until your arms are straight, then re-rack with a spotter's help if the load is heavy.
exercises.formCue: Feet locked in, bar to the lower chest.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lowering the bar toward the neck and unracking heavy loads without a spotter.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with the decline machine press or a light bar and a spotter.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It lets you press heavy through the lower chest with less shoulder strain for many lifters.

exercises.name: Incline Machine Press
instructions: Set the seat so the handles sit just below your upper chest.
Grip the handles with your elbows out to the sides and your back flat on the pad.
Press the handles up and away until your arms are straight.
Return slowly until you feel a light stretch across the chest, then repeat.
exercises.formCue: Chest up, press on the machine's line.
exercises.commonMistakes: Seat set too low so the shoulders take over, and letting the stack slam between reps.
exercises.beginnerModification: Drop the weight and pause for a second at the stretch on every rep.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A fixed path lets you push the upper chest hard without balancing a bar.

exercises.name: Decline Machine Press
exercises.musclesWorked: Lower and mid chest, triceps, front delts
instructions: Set the seat so the handles line up with your lower chest.
Sit tall with your back on the pad and grip the handles.
Press the handles forward and down until your arms are straight.
Return slowly until your chest is lightly stretched, then repeat.
exercises.formCue: Shoulders down, drive through the palms.
exercises.commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders forward at lockout and cutting the range short.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter load and a three-second lowering phase.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the lower chest hard with a stable, easy setup.

exercises.name: Pec Deck Fly
instructions: Set the seat so your upper arms are level with your shoulders when you hold the pads or handles.
Sit with your back on the pad and your elbows slightly bent.
Bring your arms together in front of your chest in a wide hugging arc.
Open back slowly until you feel a comfortable stretch across the chest, then repeat.
exercises.formCue: Hug a barrel, squeeze the chest.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the arms swing too far back and turning the fly into a press by bending the elbows.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the range and use a load you can pause at the squeeze.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It isolates the chest without the triceps giving out first.

exercises.name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
instructions: Set both pulleys low and stand between them with a handle in each hand.
Take a small step forward and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Sweep your hands up and in until they meet in front of your upper chest.
Lower along the same arc under control and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Scoop up and in, elbows soft.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the elbows to curl the weight and shrugging the shoulders at the top.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work one arm at a time with a light load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The upward arc keeps tension on the upper chest through the whole rep.

exercises.name: High-to-Low Cable Fly
exercises.musclesWorked: Lower and mid chest, front delts
instructions: Set both pulleys high and stand between them with a handle in each hand.
Step forward into a split stance and lean your torso slightly forward.
With a slight elbow bend, bring your hands down and together in front of your hips.
Let your arms travel back up slowly until your chest is stretched, then repeat.
exercises.formCue: Hands meet at the hips, chest tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pressing the handles down with bent elbows and rounding the shoulders forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Reduce the load and pause where the hands meet.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The downward arc lines up with the lower chest fibres.

exercises.name: T-Bar Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, mid back, rear delts, biceps
exercises.equipment: T-bar row station or landmine with handle
instructions: Stand over the bar with your knees slightly bent and hinge forward with a flat back.
Grip the handles and lift the weight clear of the floor.
Pull the handles to your torso, driving your elbows back.
Lower until your arms are straight and your shoulders stretch forward, keeping your back flat.
exercises.formCue: Flat back, elbows to the hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing up with each rep and rounding the lower back as the set gets hard.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the chest-supported version so your lower back is not the limit.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It lets you row heavy on a fixed arc and build back thickness.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, mid back, rear delts, biceps
instructions: Sit at the cable row with your knees slightly bent and hold the handle in one hand.
Let the shoulder reach forward while your torso stays tall.
Pull the handle to the side of your waist and draw the shoulder blade back.
Return until the arm is straight, finish the reps, then switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Elbow to the back pocket.
exercises.commonMistakes: Twisting the whole torso to move the weight and shrugging the shoulder up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower the load and hold the squeeze for one second on every rep.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Training one side at a time gives a longer range and shows up side-to-side gaps.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, teres major, rear delts, biceps
instructions: Grip the bar well outside shoulder width with palms facing away and lock your thighs under the pad.
Start with arms straight and your chest lifted.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and out.
Let the bar rise until your arms are straight and your lats are stretched.
exercises.formCue: Chest to the bar, elbows down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning far back to swing the weight and pulling the bar behind the neck.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter load and a slightly narrower grip.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The wide grip builds the outer lats that give the back its width.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.equipment: Lat pulldown machine, close parallel handle
instructions: Attach a close parallel-grip handle and lock your thighs under the pad.
Start with your arms straight overhead and your chest lifted.
Pull the handle to your upper chest, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Return slowly until your arms are straight and your lats are stretched.
exercises.formCue: Elbows brush the ribs.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rocking back for momentum and stopping short of a full stretch at the top.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower the weight and count two seconds on the way up.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The close grip gives a long range of motion for the lats.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.equipment: Lat pulldown machine, wide parallel-grip bar
instructions: Attach a bar with parallel handles and grip it with your palms facing each other.
Lock your thighs under the pad and start with your arms straight.
Pull the bar to your upper chest with your elbows tracking down in front of your sides.
Return under control to a full stretch.
exercises.formCue: Palms in, chest up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Shrugging at the top and using body swing to finish the rep.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a load you can pause at the chest for one second.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A palms-in grip is often the most comfortable way to load the lats.

exercises.name: Seated Machine Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Mid back, lats, rear delts, biceps
instructions: Set the seat so the handles are level with your lower chest and the chest pad lets you just reach them.
Sit tall with your chest on the pad and grip the handles.
Pull back until your elbows pass your torso and your shoulder blades squeeze together.
Return until your arms are straight and your shoulders reach forward.
exercises.formCue: Chest on the pad, squeeze the blades.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling the chest off the pad and cutting the stretch short.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower the weight and pause at the squeeze.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The chest pad removes the lower back from the lift so the upper back does the work.

exercises.name: Machine Pullover
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, teres major, rear delts, long head of triceps
instructions: Set the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivot and fasten the belt if there is one.
Place your elbows on the pads and hold the bar lightly.
Drive your elbows forward and down until they reach your sides.
Let the arms travel back overhead slowly to a comfortable stretch.
exercises.formCue: Push with the elbows, not the hands.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling with the hands and arching the lower back at the stretch.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the overhead range and use a light load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the lats through a long range without the biceps limiting the set.

exercises.name: Rack Pull
exercises.musclesWorked: Spinal erectors, traps, glutes, hamstrings, grip
instructions: Set the rack pins so the bar rests around knee height.
Stand with the bar against your legs, hinge to grip it and set a flat back.
Stand up by driving your hips forward until you are fully upright.
Lower the bar to the pins under control and reset before the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Flat back, hips through.
exercises.commonMistakes: Loading far more than you can hold with a flat back and dropping the bar onto the pins.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise the pins slightly and use a load you could also lift from the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The short range lets you load the upper back and traps heavily.

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip Barbell Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, mid back, rear delts, biceps
instructions: Hold the bar with a shoulder-width underhand grip.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward with a flat back.
Pull the bar to your waist with your elbows close to your sides.
Lower until your arms are straight without letting your back round.
exercises.formCue: Palms up, bar to the belt.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jerking the torso upright and curling the bar with the wrists.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the chest-supported row or a lighter bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The underhand grip keeps the elbows tight and brings in more lats and biceps.

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.musclesWorked: Front and side delts, triceps, upper traps
instructions: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height.
Sit with your back on the pad and grip the handles.
Press up until your arms are straight overhead.
Lower slowly until your hands are back at shoulder level.
exercises.formCue: Ribs down, press to the ceiling.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching the lower back off the pad and stopping the lowering phase early.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light load and a seat height that feels easy on the shoulders.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A guided path lets you train the delts close to failure safely.

exercises.name: Machine Lateral Raise
instructions: Set the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivots.
Sit with your arms bent and the pads against the outside of your arms.
Raise your arms out to the sides until your upper arms are level with the floor.
Lower slowly and stop just before the weight rests.
exercises.formCue: Lead with the elbows.
exercises.commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up and bouncing out of the bottom.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter load and a two-second pause at the top.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The machine keeps even tension on the side delts through the whole range.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.equipment: Pec deck machine set for reverse fly
instructions: Sit facing the pad and set the seat so your arms are level with your shoulders.
Hold the handles with your chest against the pad and your elbows slightly bent.
Sweep your arms out and back until they are in line with your shoulders.
Return slowly without letting the weight rest.
exercises.formCue: Wide arms, elbows high.
exercises.commonMistakes: Using too much weight and turning it into a row by bending the elbows.
exercises.beginnerModification: Go lighter and stop the arc at shoulder line.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It isolates the rear delts, which pressing and rowing often leave behind.

exercises.name: Upright Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Side delts, front delts, traps, biceps
instructions: Stand tall holding the bar with an overhand grip a little wider than your shoulders.
Pull the bar up along your body with your elbows leading.
Stop when your elbows reach about shoulder height.
Lower under control until your arms are straight.
exercises.formCue: Elbows lead, stop at the shoulders.
exercises.commonMistakes: Using a narrow grip and pulling the elbows well above shoulder height.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a cable or dumbbells with a wider hand position and a shorter range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the side delts and traps together with one heavy pull.

exercises.name: Cable Y Raise
exercises.musclesWorked: Side delts, front delts, lower traps
instructions: Set both pulleys low and take the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left.
Step back slightly and stand tall with your elbows a little bent.
Raise your arms up and out into a Y until your elbows are level with your ears.
Lower slowly along the same path.
exercises.formCue: Reach long, thumbs up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning back to heave the load and shrugging toward the ears.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it one arm at a time with the lightest plate.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The cable keeps tension on the delts at the bottom, where dumbbells go slack.

exercises.name: Cable Reverse Fly
instructions: Set both pulleys at about shoulder height and take the left cable in your right hand and the right in your left.
Step back so your arms are crossed in front of you with elbows slightly bent.
Pull your arms out and back until they are in line with your shoulders.
Return slowly until your hands cross again.
exercises.formCue: Pull apart, keep the elbows up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the elbows to row the weight and arching the lower back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the reverse pec deck so the machine guides the arc.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It loads the rear delts with steady tension and no bench needed.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Sit back on a bench set to about 45 to 60 degrees with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang straight down behind your torso.
Curl the weights, turning your palms up, until your forearms are vertical.
Lower slowly to a full hang and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Elbows stay back, full hang.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the elbows drift forward and lifting the shoulders off the bench.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise the bench angle and use lighter dumbbells.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The arm-behind-body position trains the biceps in a stretched position.

exercises.name: Spider Curl
exercises.equipment: EZ bar or barbell, incline bench
instructions: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with your shoulders near the top.
Hold the bar with a shoulder-width underhand grip and let your arms hang straight down.
Curl the bar up without moving your upper arms.
Lower until your arms are straight and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Upper arms hang still.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swinging the upper arms back and stopping short of full extension.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use dumbbells or a lighter bar and slow the lowering phase.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The bench takes away body swing so the elbow flexors do all the work.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Curl
instructions: Stand tall holding the bar on the angled grips with your palms up.
Keep your elbows at your sides and curl the bar until your forearms are vertical.
Squeeze briefly at the top.
Lower until your arms are straight.
exercises.formCue: Elbows pinned, no lean.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning back to swing the bar and letting the elbows drift forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Stand with your back against a wall and use a lighter bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The angled grip lets you load the biceps with less wrist strain than a straight bar.

exercises.name: Reverse Curl
instructions: Stand tall holding the bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Keep your elbows at your sides and curl the bar until your forearms are vertical.
Keep your wrists straight through the lift.
Lower until your arms are straight.
exercises.formCue: Knuckles up, wrists straight.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the wrists bend back and using a load meant for regular curls.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use an EZ bar and about half your normal curl weight.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The palms-down grip builds the top of the forearm and the brachialis.

exercises.name: Cable Rope Hammer Curl
instructions: Attach a rope to a low pulley and hold an end in each hand with your palms facing each other.
Stand tall with your arms straight and your elbows at your sides.
Curl the rope up until your forearms are vertical.
Lower until your arms are straight.
exercises.formCue: Thumbs up, elbows still.
exercises.commonMistakes: Stepping too close so the cable goes slack and rocking the torso.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower the load and pause at the top.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The cable keeps tension on the arm at the bottom of the curl.

exercises.name: Machine Triceps Dip
instructions: Sit with your back against the pad and fasten the belt if there is one.
Grip the handles with your elbows pointing straight back.
Push the handles down until your arms are straight.
Let the handles rise slowly until your shoulders feel a light stretch.
exercises.formCue: Elbows back, lock it out.
exercises.commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows wide and letting the shoulders shrug up at the top.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the top range and use a lighter stack.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It gives the heavy loading of a dip without having to carry your bodyweight.

exercises.name: Tricep Kickback
instructions: Place one knee and the same-side hand on a bench with your back flat.
Hold a dumbbell in the other hand and lift your upper arm until it is level with the floor.
Straighten your elbow until the whole arm is in line.
Bend the elbow back to the start without dropping the upper arm.
exercises.formCue: Upper arm stays level.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swinging the upper arm and using a weight too heavy to lock out.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a very light dumbbell and pause at full extension.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the triceps hardest at full lockout with very little load on the joints.

exercises.name: JM Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench and unrack the bar with a shoulder-width or slightly narrower grip.
Lower the bar in a straight line toward your upper chest and neck area while your elbows bend and stay fairly high.
Stop when your forearms meet your biceps.
Press the bar back up until your arms are straight.
exercises.formCue: Elbows up, fold and press.
exercises.commonMistakes: Starting too heavy and letting the elbows drop so it turns into a close-grip bench press.
exercises.beginnerModification: Learn the path with an empty bar or use the close-grip bench press.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It blends a press and an extension so the triceps can be loaded heavily.

exercises.name: Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit and rest your forearms on your thighs with your palms up and your wrists just past your knees.
Hold the bar with a narrow underhand grip and let it roll down toward your fingers.
Close your grip and curl your knuckles up as high as you can.
Lower slowly and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Forearms down, move only the wrists.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting the forearms off the thighs and rushing the reps.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light dumbbell one hand at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the inner forearm and grip.

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit and rest your forearms on your thighs with your palms down and your wrists just past your knees.
Hold the bar with an overhand grip.
Raise your knuckles as high as you can.
Lower until your knuckles point toward the floor and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Knuckles to the ceiling.
exercises.commonMistakes: Going too heavy and letting the forearms lift off the thighs.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a very light dumbbell one hand at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the back of the forearm, which most pulling work misses.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
instructions: Lie back on the pad with your shoulders under the shoulder pads and your feet about shoulder-width on the platform.
Straighten your legs and release the safety handles.
Lower by bending your knees and hips as deep as you can control with your back on the pad.
Push through your whole foot until your legs are straight, then re-engage the safeties when done.
exercises.formCue: Back on the pad, knees over toes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the knees cave in and the hips lift off the pad at the bottom.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the depth and use only the sled weight to start.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The back support lets you load the quads hard without balance being the limit.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Squat
instructions: Set the bar at upper-chest height and place it across the back of your shoulders.
Stand with your feet under or slightly in front of the bar and rotate it off the hooks.
Squat by bending your hips and knees until your thighs are about level with the floor.
Stand up until your legs are straight and rotate the bar back onto the hooks when done.
exercises.formCue: Knees follow the toes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Placing the feet so far forward that the lower back rounds, and letting the knees cave in.
exercises.beginnerModification: Squat to a bench set at a comfortable depth.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The guided bar lets you take the quads close to failure without a spotter.

exercises.name: High-Foot Leg Press
instructions: Sit in the leg press and place your feet shoulder-width on the upper part of the platform.
Straighten your legs and release the safeties.
Lower the platform until your hips are deeply bent while your lower back stays on the pad.
Push through your heels until your legs are nearly straight.
exercises.formCue: Hips stay down, drive the heels.
exercises.commonMistakes: Going so deep that the hips roll off the pad and locking the knees hard at the top.
exercises.beginnerModification: Reduce the depth and the load until your lower back stays flat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Research suggests foot position changes muscle activity only modestly, with a higher placement shifting some work toward the glutes under heavy loads.

source.name: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health (systematic review of leg press EMG)

exercises.name: Single-Leg Leg Press
instructions: Sit in the leg press and place one foot in the middle of the platform with the other foot on the floor or held clear.
Straighten the working leg and release the safeties.
Lower until your knee is deeply bent while your hips stay square on the seat.
Push back up until the leg is nearly straight, finish the reps, then switch legs.
exercises.formCue: Hips square, knee tracks the toes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Twisting the hips toward the working leg and loading it like a two-leg press.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with less than half of your two-leg weight and a shorter range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It evens out strength between legs with your back fully supported.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
instructions: Sit with your back on the pad and your knees lined up with the machine's pivot.
Rest your lower legs on the roller and lock the thigh pad down.
Pull the roller down and back by bending your knees as far as you can.
Return slowly until your legs are straight.
exercises.formCue: Hips back, curl the heels under.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hips slide forward and letting the weight snap back up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light load and a three-second return.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Curling with the hips bent trains the hamstrings at a long length.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
instructions: Lie face down with your knees just off the edge of the bench and the roller above your heels.
Hold the handles and keep your hips pressed into the pad.
Curl the roller toward the back of your thighs.
Lower slowly until your legs are straight.
exercises.formCue: Hips down, heels to glutes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting the hips off the pad and using momentum out of the bottom.
exercises.beginnerModification: Reduce the load and work one leg at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It isolates knee flexion, which hinges like the Romanian deadlift do not train.

exercises.name: Hip Abduction Machine
exercises.musclesWorked: Glute medius, glute minimus, upper glutes
instructions: Sit with your back on the pad and the outside of your thighs against the pads.
Hold the handles and sit tall.
Push your legs apart as far as you comfortably can.
Bring them back together slowly without letting the stack rest.
exercises.formCue: Push the knees out, pause.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing through short reps and rocking the torso for momentum.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light load and hold the open position for two seconds.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the side glutes that keep the hips and knees steady.

exercises.name: Hip Adduction Machine
instructions: Sit with your back on the pad and the inside of your thighs against the pads.
Set the start position to a stretch you find comfortable.
Squeeze your legs together until the pads meet.
Open slowly back to the start.
exercises.formCue: Squeeze in, open slow.
exercises.commonMistakes: Setting the start position too wide and letting the pads fly apart.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a narrower start position and a light load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the inner thigh directly, which squats only train in part.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
instructions: Sit with the balls of your feet on the platform and your heels hanging off.
Set the pad on your lower thighs and release the safety.
Lower your heels until your calves are stretched.
Raise your heels as high as you can, pause, and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Full stretch, full squeeze.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing at the bottom and doing short half reps.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light load and pause for two seconds at the bottom.
exercises.whyThisMatters: With the knees bent the deeper calf muscle, the soleus, does most of the work.

exercises.name: Donkey Calf Raise
instructions: Stand with the balls of your feet on the block and your heels hanging off.
Hinge forward, rest your forearms on the support and set the pad on your lower back and hips.
Straighten your knees and lower your heels until your calves are stretched.
Raise your heels as high as you can, then lower slowly.
exercises.formCue: Legs straight, heels all the way down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the knees to help and bouncing out of the stretch.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do the same hinged position with bodyweight only.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The bent-over position puts the calves under a deep stretch.

exercises.name: Leg Press Calf Raise
instructions: Sit in the leg press and straighten your legs with the safeties still engaged where the machine allows.
Slide your feet down so only the balls of your feet are on the lower edge of the platform.
Let your heels sink toward you until your calves are stretched.
Push the platform away by pointing your toes, then lower slowly.
exercises.formCue: Push through the big toe.
exercises.commonMistakes: Unlocking the safeties with the feet barely on the platform and bending the knees to help.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the safeties engaged and use a light load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It loads the calves heavily with no weight on the spine.

exercises.name: Cable Glute Kickback
instructions: Fasten an ankle cuff to a low pulley and attach it to one ankle.
Face the machine, hold the frame and lean forward slightly with the working knee bent.
Drive the leg back by straightening your hip and knee.
Return slowly, finish the reps, then switch legs.
exercises.formCue: Squeeze the glute, keep the back still.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to get the leg higher and swinging the leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it with no cable from a hands-and-knees position.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains one glute at a time with steady cable tension.

exercises.name: 45-Degree Hip Extension
instructions: Set the pad just below your hip crease so you can bend freely at the hips, and hook your heels under the brace.
Cross your arms over your chest or hold a plate there.
Lower by bending only at the hips until you feel a mild stretch in your hamstrings.
Squeeze your glutes to raise your torso until it is in line with your legs, and stop there.
exercises.formCue: Hinge at the hips, finish with the glutes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching past a straight line at the top and bouncing out of the bottom.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use bodyweight and a shorter range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Moving from the hips instead of the spine puts the work on the glutes and hamstrings.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
instructions: Kneel below a high pulley and hold the rope ends beside your head.
Keep your hips still and above your knees.
Curl your ribs toward your hips so your elbows travel toward your thighs.
Return slowly until your torso is tall again.
exercises.formCue: Curl the spine, hips stay put.
exercises.commonMistakes: Sitting the hips back and pulling with the arms.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light load and learn the curl on the floor first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It lets you add load to the abs the way you would to any other muscle.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
instructions: Kneel on a mat and hold the wheel under your shoulders with your arms straight.
Tuck your ribs down and brace your midsection.
Roll the wheel forward as far as you can without your lower back sagging.
Pull the wheel back toward your knees to return.
exercises.formCue: Ribs down, do not let the back sag.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch and rolling out further than you can control.
exercises.beginnerModification: Roll toward a wall that stops the wheel at a short distance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the abs to resist the lower back arching under load.

exercises.name: Decline Sit-Up
instructions: Hook your feet under the pads of a decline bench and sit with your hips bent.
Cross your arms over your chest or hold a plate there.
Lower your torso under control until your shoulders reach the bench.
Curl back up by bending at the waist and hips.
exercises.formCue: Control the way down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Throwing the arms or head forward for momentum and dropping fast.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower the bench angle or lower only halfway.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The slope adds range and resistance to a plain sit-up.

exercises.name: Boxing Stance & Guard
instructions: Stand side-on at roughly 45 degrees with your feet about shoulder-width apart and your weaker-side foot in front.
Soften both knees, share your weight evenly across both feet, and lift the rear heel slightly off the floor.
Bring both fists up with the lead hand near eye level and the rear fist beside your chin, elbows tucked toward your ribs.
Tuck your chin behind the lead shoulder, keep the hands closed but loose, and hold the position while breathing steadily.
exercises.formCue: Chin down, rear heel light.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing tall and square with the chin lifted, or planting both heels flat so the feet cannot move quickly.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold for short blocks in front of a mirror and shake the arms out between holds.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Every punch, step, and defensive move starts from and returns to this position.

exercises.name: Jab
instructions: Set your boxing stance with both hands up and your chin tucked.
Shift a little weight toward the lead leg and turn the trunk slightly as the lead arm travels straight out from the guard.
Rotate the fist so the knuckles face up and the palm faces the floor as the arm reaches full length.
Pull the hand back along the same straight line to your guard while the rear hand stays beside your chin.
exercises.formCue: Straight out, straight back.
exercises.commonMistakes: Drawing the hand back before punching, or letting the rear hand drift away from the chin.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise slowly in front of a mirror from a still stance before adding a step.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The lead straight punch sets range and rhythm for everything else you throw.

exercises.name: Cross
exercises.musclesWorked: Shoulders, chest, triceps, obliques, glutes, calves
instructions: Start in your boxing stance with the lead hand high and the lead elbow covering your ribs.
Turn the rear foot about a quarter turn on the ball of the foot and rotate the hips and trunk toward the lead side.
Extend the rear arm straight to the target, turning the palm down just before full reach.
Bring the hand back along the same path and settle into your stance with the elbow tucked.
exercises.formCue: Turn the hip, then the hand.
exercises.commonMistakes: Throwing with the arm only while the rear heel stays planted, or over-rotating and falling across your front foot.
exercises.beginnerModification: Rehearse the hip and foot turn with hands on your cheeks before adding the arm.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The rear straight teaches you to move force from the floor through the hips into the hand.

exercises.name: Lead Hook
instructions: From your stance, keep the rear hand tight to your chin and load a little weight onto the lead leg.
Lift the lead elbow to about shoulder height with the arm bent close to 90 degrees.
Drive off the front foot, lift the lead heel, and rotate the hips and trunk so the bent arm is carried through in an arc.
Stop the fist at your centre line, then bring it back to the guard by the shortest route.
exercises.formCue: Turn the body, the arm just follows.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling the hand back to wind up, or straightening the arm so the punch turns into a wide swing.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the hip turn with the arm already raised and fixed at 90 degrees.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The hook trains fast trunk rotation around a stable base.

exercises.name: Rear Hook
instructions: From your stance, keep the lead hand up beside your chin.
Rotate the trunk toward the lead side and shift weight onto the lead leg as the rear heel lifts.
Swing the rear arm through with the elbow held near 90 degrees and the knuckles pointing at the target.
Keep your eyes over the top of the arm, then return the hand to the guard by the shortest path.
exercises.formCue: Elbow bent, eyes over the arm.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the arm straighten into a loop, or dropping the lead hand while the rear hand travels.
exercises.beginnerModification: Slow the punch down and stop at the centre line until you can finish balanced.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds rotation from the rear side and balances the lead hook.

exercises.name: Lead Uppercut
instructions: From your stance, bend the knees a little and turn the upper body slightly toward the lead side.
Shift weight onto the lead leg while the rear hand stays high and firm against your chin.
Turn the lead fist so the knuckles point forward and drive it upward with the elbow kept bent.
Finish around chin height, then retract along the same path into your guard.
exercises.formCue: Legs lift the punch.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping the hand low to wind up, or leaning back and lifting the chin as the punch rises.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the small knee dip and rise with both hands glued to your cheeks first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The uppercut links leg drive to a short, compact arm path.

exercises.name: Rear Uppercut
instructions: From your guard, shift weight onto the rear foot and turn the rear palm to face you.
Bend the rear knee slightly and lift the rear heel.
Drive up through the legs and hips and throw a short punch upward with the forearm close to vertical.
Keep your chin behind the lead shoulder, then bring the hand straight back to the guard.
exercises.formCue: Short and up, not across.
exercises.commonMistakes: Winding up before the punch, or driving the fist across the body instead of upward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work it slowly on the spot and stop the fist at chin height.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches upward drive from the hips with the guard still intact.

exercises.name: Jab to the Body
instructions: From your stance, bend the knees until your lead shoulder is level with a target at stomach height.
Keep the back straight, eyes forward, and the rear hand high.
Extend the lead arm straight out with a small hip turn, palm turning down at full reach.
Retract the hand and stand back up into your guard in one motion.
exercises.formCue: Bend the knees, not the waist.
exercises.commonMistakes: Folding at the waist and punching downward, which leaves the head forward and the chin open.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the level change alone as a small squat in stance before adding the punch.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Changing level with the legs adds real leg work to every round.

exercises.name: Lead Hook to the Body
instructions: From your stance, bend the knees until your lead shoulder lines up with a target at rib height.
Keep the rear hand firm against your chin and rotate the trunk slightly toward the lead side.
Shift weight to the lead leg and swing the lead arm through with the elbow bent near 90 degrees.
Return the hand by the shortest path and rise back into your stance.
exercises.formCue: Sit down first, then turn.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping the hand instead of bending the knees, or letting the rear hand fall away from the chin.
exercises.beginnerModification: Throw it slowly in the air and pause in the lowered position to check your guard.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It combines a level change with rotation, which makes rounds more demanding on legs and trunk.

exercises.name: Jab-Cross-Hook Combo
instructions: Start in your stance and throw a straight jab that snaps back to the guard.
Follow with the cross, turning the rear foot and hip so weight moves toward the front leg.
Let that loaded position feed the lead hook, rotating back the other way with the elbow bent.
Finish balanced in your stance with both hands at your chin before repeating.
exercises.formCue: One flow, finish on balance.
exercises.commonMistakes: Throwing three separate punches with pauses, or over-committing to the cross and stumbling into the hook.
exercises.beginnerModification: Drill jab-cross until it is smooth, then add the hook at half speed.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Short combinations teach each punch to set up the body position for the next.

exercises.name: Double Jab-Cross
instructions: From your stance, throw a jab and bring it only part of the way back.
Throw a second jab straight away, with a small forward step if you have room.
Follow with the cross, rotating the rear hip and foot.
Recover both hands to the guard and reset your feet to shoulder width.
exercises.formCue: Quick, quick, turn.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the feet come together on the step, or dropping the jab hand between the two jabs.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise on the spot without the step until the rhythm is steady.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Repeating the lead hand builds shoulder endurance and timing for the rear hand.

exercises.name: Boxing Pivot
exercises.musclesWorked: Calves, quads, glutes, hip rotators, core
instructions: Set your stance with your weight centred and both hands up.
Push off the rear foot and spin on the ball of the lead foot.
Swing the rear foot around behind you so your stance turns about 45 degrees.
Land in the same stance width and repeat, then practise turning the other way.
exercises.formCue: Front foot spins, back foot swings.
exercises.commonMistakes: Crossing the legs or tipping weight forward over the lead knee during the turn.
exercises.beginnerModification: Make smaller turns and pause after each one to check your stance width.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Pivoting changes your angle without giving up balance.

exercises.name: Step-Drag Footwork
instructions: Stand in your boxing stance on the balls of your feet.
To go forward, lift the lead foot slightly, push off the rear foot, and slide the rear foot up once the lead foot lands.
To go back, lift the rear foot slightly, push off the lead foot, and slide the lead foot back to stance width.
Keep the feet shoulder-width apart and your weight shared across both legs throughout.
exercises.formCue: Feet move as a unit.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bringing the feet together, crossing them, or moving flat-footed on the heels.
exercises.beginnerModification: Take small steps along a line on the floor and reset your stance after each one.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Keeping your base while moving is what lets you punch from balance.

exercises.name: Boxing Side Step
instructions: Start in your boxing stance with the knees soft.
To move left in an orthodox stance, lift the lead foot slightly and push off the rear foot, then let the rear foot follow.
To move right, lift the rear foot slightly and push off the lead foot, then let the lead foot follow.
Finish every step at shoulder width with the guard up.
exercises.formCue: Nearest foot goes first.
exercises.commonMistakes: Taking one oversized step that stretches the stance, or letting the feet click together.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use short steps and pause in stance between each one.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Lateral steps take you off a straight line while keeping you ready to work.

exercises.name: Pull Counter
exercises.musclesWorked: Obliques, spinal erectors, glutes, shoulders, calves
instructions: From your guard, shift weight onto the rear leg and lean the upper body back a few centimetres.
Keep both hands up and your chin down as you lean.
Push off the rear foot to bring your weight forward again.
Throw a straight rear hand as you return, then recover to your balanced stance.
exercises.formCue: Small lean, straight back in.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning so far that the head lifts and the base is lost, or dropping the lead hand on the way back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the weight shift back and forward without the punch.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains quick weight transfer between the back and front leg.

exercises.name: Shadow Parry Drill
instructions: Stand in your guard and picture a straight punch coming toward your face.
Turn the body slightly toward the lead side and make a short inward tap with the rear hand, as if deflecting it at the wrist.
Keep the elbow in and stop the hand before it crosses your face.
Return the hand to your chin at once, then answer with a jab.
exercises.formCue: Tiny tap, hand comes home.
exercises.commonMistakes: Reaching out to meet the imaginary punch, or sweeping the hand wide across the face.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the parry alone in a mirror before adding the jab.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Small, economical hand defence keeps the guard in place and frees the other hand.

exercises.name: Duck Under
instructions: Stand in your guard with your eyes forward.
Bend both knees down and slightly inward so your head drops straight below its starting height.
Keep the forearms and elbows covering the body and keep looking ahead.
Drive back up into your stance with the hands still in place.
exercises.formCue: Knees bend, eyes stay up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Folding at the waist and looking at the floor, or tipping the weight onto the front leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Reduce the depth and move slowly until you can stay upright through the trunk.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Ducking with the legs turns defence practice into steady lower-body work.

exercises.name: Speed Bag Rhythm
instructions: Stand square to the bag at about arm's length with the bottom of the bag near eye level.
Hold both hands up close to the bag and strike with small circles instead of back-and-forth swings.
Let the bag rebound three times after each strike before you hit it again.
Work a steady pattern of two strikes with one hand and then two with the other.
exercises.formCue: Small circles, count the rebounds.
exercises.commonMistakes: Holding the hands too far from the bag, or swinging hard and losing the rhythm.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with open hands and one strike at a time until the three-rebound count feels natural.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds shoulder endurance and hand-eye timing.

exercises.name: Double-End Bag Rounds
instructions: Set the bag so the ball sits around head height and take your stance at jab range.
Start with single jabs and time each one as the ball returns to centre.
Add the cross, then simple two and three punch combinations at a steady rhythm.
Keep your feet moving and your guard up between combinations for the whole round.
exercises.formCue: Light hands, time the return.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing flat-footed, or hitting hard so the ball swings out of control.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work only the jab for the first rounds and shorten the round length.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A moving target trains accuracy and timing more than power.

exercises.name: Teep (Push Kick)
exercises.musclesWorked: Hip flexors, quads, glutes, core, calves
instructions: Stand in your stance with hands up and shift your weight onto the back leg.
Lift the lead knee toward your chest.
Push the foot straight forward, driving the hips toward the target and leaning back only slightly.
Pull the knee back in and set the foot down in your stance.
exercises.formCue: Knee up, hips through.
exercises.commonMistakes: Flicking the lower leg without the hip drive, or dropping the hands as the leg lifts.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the knee lift and balance hold, and kick at knee to waist height only.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The push kick builds single-leg balance and hip drive.

exercises.name: Roundhouse Kick
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hip rotators, obliques, quads, calves
instructions: From your stance with fists by your chin, step the base foot slightly out and rise onto the ball of that foot.
Turn the base foot away from the kick as you lift the kicking knee to point at the target.
Rotate the hips over and swing the leg through horizontally, meeting a bag with the shin.
Bring the leg back and return to your stance with the guard up.
exercises.formCue: Pivot the base foot, turn the hip over.
exercises.commonMistakes: Kicking with a flat, unturned base foot, or kicking higher than you can control so the trunk folds.
exercises.beginnerModification: Kick slowly in the air at knee to hip height while holding a wall or chair for balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The roundhouse trains hip rotation and balance on one leg.

exercises.name: Low Kick
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hip rotators, obliques, quads, calves
instructions: Stand in your stance at a range where your shin can reach the lower part of a heavy bag.
Step out slightly and pivot on the ball of the base foot.
Turn the hip and swing the leg through to meet the bag at thigh height with the shin.
Recover the leg to your stance and reset your guard.
exercises.formCue: Same hip turn, lower line.
exercises.commonMistakes: Reaching with the foot instead of the shin, or leaving the base foot planted flat.
exercises.beginnerModification: Rehearse in the air at slow speed before working lightly on a bag.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The low line lets you practise full hip rotation without needing much flexibility.

exercises.name: Switch Kick
exercises.musclesWorked: Calves, glutes, hip rotators, obliques, quads
instructions: Stand in your stance with the guard up.
Step the lead foot back and the rear foot forward in one quick switch, staying close to the floor.
As the new rear foot lands, pivot on the base foot and throw a roundhouse with the leg that started in front.
Bring the leg back and return to your original stance.
exercises.formCue: Quick switch, stay grounded.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jumping both feet high in the air at once, which wastes time and upsets balance.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the stance switch alone, then add a slow knee lift before kicking.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The switch adds quick footwork and coordination to the basic kick.

exercises.name: Straight Knee Strike
instructions: Stand in your stance with hands high, or reach both hands forward as if holding a bag.
Push off the floor with the rear foot and drive that knee forward and up.
Push the hips forward and rise onto the ball of the standing foot as the knee reaches its peak.
Set the foot back down in your stance and reset before the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Hips forward, knee leads.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting the knee without pushing the hips through, or rounding forward over the knee.
exercises.beginnerModification: Slow it down and hold a wall for balance while you learn the hip drive.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Knee strikes work the hip flexors and trunk while challenging single-leg balance.

exercises.name: Shadow Elbow Strike
instructions: Stand in your stance with a high guard and no target in front of you.
Fold one arm so the hand stays near your chest and lift the elbow to shoulder height.
Rotate from the trunk and hips to carry the elbow across in a short horizontal arc.
Keep the other hand against your face, return to the guard, and alternate sides and angles.
exercises.formCue: Turn from the middle, other hand stays home.
exercises.commonMistakes: Over-rotating and losing balance, or dropping the guard hand during the turn.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise slowly facing a mirror, one angle at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Elbow shadow work is compact rotation practice for the trunk and shoulders.

exercises.name: Kick Check
instructions: Stand in your stance with hands up.
Shift your weight onto the back leg.
Lift the lead knee up and turn it slightly outward so the shin faces to the side, with the same-side elbow close above the knee.
Hold for a moment in balance, then set the foot down in your stance.
exercises.formCue: Weight back, shin up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning forward as the leg lifts, or letting the hands drop for balance.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift the knee lower and hold a wall lightly with one hand.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The check is a balance drill that strengthens the standing leg and hip.

exercises.name: Technical Stand-Up
instructions: Sit on the floor with one hand posted behind you and the opposite foot flat on the floor.
Hold the free hand up in front of your face.
Press through the posted hand and foot to lift your hips, then swing the free leg back underneath you.
Plant that foot behind you and stand up into a staggered stance, then sit back down and switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Hand and opposite foot, hips up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Trying to stand without lifting the hips first, or placing the back foot too close to the posted hand.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise only the hip lift and leg swing before standing all the way up.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is a controlled way to get from the floor to your feet with a stable base.

exercises.name: Bridge and Roll
instructions: Lie on your back with your feet flat and your heels close to your hips.
Drive through your feet to lift your hips high.
Turn to look over one shoulder and reach the opposite arm across your body as you bridge onto that shoulder.
Lower back to the start, or roll through to your knees, and repeat on the other side.
exercises.formCue: Hips high, then turn.
exercises.commonMistakes: Turning before the hips are lifted, or pushing through the neck instead of the shoulder.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do straight glute bridges first, then add a small turn onto the shoulder.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds explosive hip extension with rotation.

exercises.name: Penetration Step
instructions: Start in a low athletic stance with knees bent and back flat.
Lower your hips to change level while keeping your chest and head up.
Step forward with the lead leg and let the lead knee glide toward the mat as the hips drive forward.
Bring the trail leg up and through to return to your stance, then repeat down the mat.
exercises.formCue: Level first, then step.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending at the waist with the head down, or stepping so far that the trail leg cannot follow.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a shorter step and keep the knee off the mat until the level change feels smooth.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains a fast level change and forward drive from the legs.

exercises.name: Sit-Through
instructions: Start on your hands and feet with knees bent and hovering just off the floor.
Lift one hand and the opposite foot.
Thread the lifted leg underneath your body and rotate your hips until that hip faces the floor beside you.
Bring the leg back to the start and repeat to the other side.
exercises.formCue: Hips turn, hand stays strong.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hips drop to the floor and rest, or rushing so the supporting shoulder collapses.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start from hands and knees and move slowly through a smaller range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds shoulder stability and rotational hip mobility under bodyweight.

exercises.name: Wrestling Stance and Motion
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, calves, core, upper back
instructions: Take a staggered or square stance with knees bent, hips low, back flat, and hands in front of you.
Move in short steps forward, back, and in a circle without crossing your feet.
Move your feet whenever your hands move so you never reach from a still base.
Every few steps, drop your hips to change level and rise back to your stance.
exercises.formCue: Stay low, feet under you.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing up between steps, or crossing the feet while circling.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work in shorter bursts and hold a higher stance until the legs adapt.
