exercises.whyThisMatters: Holding a low stance while moving builds leg endurance fast.

exercises.name: Archer Push-Up
instructions: Set up in a push-up position with the hands well outside shoulder width and the body in one line.
Lower toward one hand, bending that elbow while the other arm stays long out to the side.
Stop when the chest is just above the floor and the hips are still square.
Press back to the middle through the bent arm and repeat to the other side.
exercises.formCue: Load the bent arm, keep the hips level.
exercises.commonMistakes: Twisting or shifting the hips to cheat the load, and rushing the change of sides.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use regular push-ups until they are solid, then try archers with the hands on a bench.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It puts most of your weight on one arm, which is the bridge between two-arm and one-arm pressing.

exercises.name: One-Arm Push-Up
exercises.musclesWorked: Chest, triceps, front delts, lats, obliques, glutes
instructions: Take a push-up position with the feet wider than the hips and one hand under the shoulder, the other off the floor.
Tighten everything from grip to glutes to quads before you move.
Lower under control with the shoulder packed down and the trunk turning as little as possible.
Press the floor away to a straight arm without letting the plank break.
exercises.formCue: Whole body tight, then lower.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag or rotate, shrugging the working shoulder, and the feet rolling inward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise the working hand on a bar or bench and lower the height over weeks.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds heavy pressing strength and cross-body trunk control with no equipment.

exercises.name: Elevated One-Arm Push-Up
exercises.equipment: Bar in a rack, bench or sturdy box
instructions: Place one hand on a fixed bar or bench and walk the feet back into a wide-stance plank.
Put the free hand behind the back or along the thigh and tense the whole body.
Lower the chest toward the hand with the shoulders as level as you can keep them.
Press back to a straight arm, then finish all reps before switching sides.
exercises.formCue: Same tension as the floor version, just a kinder angle.
exercises.commonMistakes: Picking a height that is too low and twisting to finish the rep.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with the hand at hip height and only lower it when every rep stays square.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It lets you practise the exact one-arm pattern at a load you can own.

exercises.name: Planche Lean
exercises.musclesWorked: Front delts, serratus, biceps tendon area, wrists, core
instructions: Start in a straight-arm plank with the fingers forward or turned slightly out.
Lock the elbows with the elbow pits facing forward and press the shoulders down away from the ears.
Lean forward until the shoulders travel past the wrists and hold.
Rock back to the plank before the elbows bend or the hips drop.
exercises.formCue: Arms locked, lean from the ankles.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the elbows as the lean gets hard, and skipping wrist preparation.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lean only a few centimetres and build time before adding distance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the straight-arm shoulder strength every planche step depends on.

exercises.name: Frog Stand
instructions: Squat down and plant the hands shoulder width apart with the elbows bent out to make a shelf.
Rest the knees on the arms just above the elbows.
Tip forward slowly until the toes get light, then let them leave the floor.
Look slightly ahead, breathe evenly and hold, then tip back onto the feet.
exercises.formCue: Tip forward slowly, eyes ahead of the hands.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jumping into the balance instead of leaning into it, and holding the breath.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the toes on the floor, or rest the forehead on a folded towel while you find the lean.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the wrists and shoulders to carry your full weight before harder hand balances.

exercises.name: Tuck Planche
exercises.musclesWorked: Front delts, serratus, chest, core, wrists
instructions: From a frog stand or a seated start on parallettes, lock the arms straight.
Lean the shoulders ahead of the hands and press the floor away to round the upper back.
Pull the knees to the chest and lift the feet and knees clear of the arms.
Hold with the hips near shoulder height, then set the feet down with control.
exercises.formCue: Lean, lock, push the floor away.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bent elbows, and rushing here before the wrists and shoulders are ready.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the frog stand, then take one knee off the arm at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the first real planche hold and a strong test of straight-arm pressing.

exercises.name: Ring Push-Up
instructions: Set the rings low and take a plank with a hand in each ring, arms straight.
Keep the body in one line from head to heels.
Lower the chest between the rings while keeping them close to the ribs.
Press to full lockout without letting the rings swing or drift apart.
exercises.formCue: Quiet rings, straight body.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rings drifting wide and hips sagging as the set goes on.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise the rings so the body is more upright, or use regular push-ups.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The unstable handles make the shoulders and trunk work harder than the floor version.

exercises.name: Feet-Elevated Inverted Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Mid back, lats, rear delts, biceps
exercises.equipment: Fixed bar and bench or box
instructions: Lie under a fixed bar, take a wide overhand grip and rest the heels on a bench.
Hang with straight arms and a straight body.
Pull the chest to the bar and draw the shoulders back at the top.
Lower until the arms are straight.
exercises.formCue: Chest high, body stiff.
exercises.commonMistakes: Hips dropping and the chin reaching for the bar instead of the chest.
exercises.beginnerModification: Put the feet on the floor, or bend the knees.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Raising the feet makes the row close to a full bodyweight horizontal pull.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Pull-Up
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, teres major, rear delts, biceps, forearms
instructions: Grip the bar overhand, hands clearly wider than the shoulders.
Hang with the arms and shoulders fully extended.
Pull until the chin is over the bar.
Lower all the way to a straight-arm hang.
exercises.formCue: Elbows down to the ribs.
exercises.commonMistakes: Going so wide that the range gets short, and stopping before a full hang.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a band, or do slow lowering reps with this grip.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It shifts more of the pull to the lats and upper back.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
instructions: Take the parallel handles with the palms facing each other.
Hang with the arms and shoulders fully extended.
Pull until the neck reaches the height of the hands.
Lower to a full hang under control.
exercises.formCue: Chest up, elbows to the hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Kicking the legs and stopping short at the bottom.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a band or a foot on a box to take some weight.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The palms-in grip is often the most comfortable way to pull heavy for elbows and shoulders.

exercises.name: L Pull-Up
instructions: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip.
Lift the straight legs until they are level with the hips and hold them there.
Pull the chin over the bar without letting the legs drop or swing.
Lower to a full hang with the legs still held in the L.
exercises.formCue: Legs frozen, pull strict.
exercises.commonMistakes: Legs dropping as you pull, and using a swing to start the rep.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold a tucked-knee position during the pull-up.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Holding the L removes all momentum and trains the trunk while you pull.

exercises.name: Ring Support Hold
instructions: Grip the rings and press or jump to straight arms above them.
Lock the elbows and pull the shoulders down away from the ears.
Turn the rings out slightly so the palms face forward.
Hold the rings still against the sides, then step down before the arms bend.
exercises.formCue: Arms locked, rings still.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bent elbows, shrugged shoulders and rings shaking away from the body.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the toes on a box to take some weight.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A steady support is the base for every dip and muscle-up on rings.

exercises.name: False Grip Hang
instructions: Set the rings so the heel of each hand sits on top of the ring, wrist bent over it.
Wrap the fingers and let the ring rest across the base of the palm.
Hang with the wrists still bent, feet on the floor at first if needed.
Come down before the grip slips back into the fingers.
exercises.formCue: Wrist over the ring.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the ring slide into the fingers, and holding too long too soon.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the feet on the floor in a ring-row position and hold the grip there.
exercises.whyThisMatters: This grip is what lets you move from the pull to the dip in a strict muscle-up.

exercises.name: Strict Ring Muscle-Up
instructions: Hang from the rings in a false grip.
Pull smoothly and as high as you can, bringing the rings to the chest.
Lean the chest forward over the hands and bring the elbows back to move above the rings.
Press out of the dip to locked arms with the rings turned slightly out.
exercises.formCue: Pull high, lean through, press.
exercises.commonMistakes: Losing the false grip, and trying it before strict pull-ups and dips are solid.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the transition with the feet on the floor under low rings.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It links a pull and a press into one skill that gets you on top of the rings.

exercises.name: Pistol Squat
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, hip flexors, ankles, core
instructions: Stand on one leg with the other leg held out in front and the arms forward for balance.
Sit back slightly and bend the standing knee, letting it track over the toes with the heel down.
Lower until the hip crease is below the knee.
Drive through the whole foot to stand without the free leg touching the floor.
exercises.formCue: Heel down, knee over toes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rocking onto the toes, the knee caving in, and the free foot touching down.
exercises.beginnerModification: Squat to a box, hold a support, or let the free heel rest lightly on the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds single-leg strength, balance and ankle range together.

exercises.name: Box Pistol Squat
instructions: Stand on one leg in front of a box or bench with the other leg held forward.
Sit back and down under control until you touch the box.
Keep the standing knee in line with the foot.
Stand up on the same leg without rocking for momentum.
exercises.formCue: Touch the box, do not drop onto it.
exercises.commonMistakes: Falling the last few centimetres and bouncing back up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a higher box and lower it over time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The box sets a depth you can control while single-leg strength catches up.

exercises.name: Assisted Pistol Squat
instructions: Hold a rack upright or other fixed support at chest height.
Stand on one leg with the other leg held in front.
Lower as deep as you can control, using the hands only as much as needed.
Stand up through the whole foot, keeping the pull from the arms light.
exercises.formCue: Legs do the work, hands just guide.
exercises.commonMistakes: Hauling yourself up with the arms and letting the heel lift.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the depth and add range as control improves.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It lets you practise the full pistol path before you have the strength to do it free.

exercises.name: Shrimp Squat
instructions: Stand on one leg and bend the other knee so that foot is behind you.
Reach the arms forward and keep the weight over the middle of the standing foot.
Lower slowly until the back knee touches the floor softly behind the standing heel.
Stand back up without pushing off the back foot.
exercises.formCue: Weight on the midfoot, knee kisses the floor.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping the back knee hard and pushing off the rear toes.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower the knee to a pad or stack of mats to shorten the range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds one-leg strength and scales more easily than the pistol.

exercises.name: L-Sit
exercises.musclesWorked: Abs, hip flexors, quads, triceps, shoulders
instructions: Sit with the legs straight and the hands flat beside the hips, or grip parallettes.
Press down hard and push the shoulders away from the ears.
Lift the hips and both straight legs off the floor.
Hold with the knees locked and chest tall, then lower with control.
exercises.formCue: Push down, shoulders low, knees locked.
exercises.commonMistakes: Shrugged shoulders, a rounded back and bent knees.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold a tuck with the knees bent, or keep one foot on the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the trunk and hip flexors hard while the arms support the body.

exercises.name: Tuck L-Sit
instructions: Sit between the hands or parallettes with the knees bent.
Press down and push the shoulders away from the ears until the hips lift.
Pull the knees toward the chest so both feet leave the floor.
Hold with a tall chest, then set the feet down.
exercises.formCue: Press tall, knees in.
exercises.commonMistakes: Sinking into the shoulders and leaning back to lift the feet.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift one foot at a time while the other stays down.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the support strength and compression needed for the full L-sit.

exercises.name: Tuck Front Lever
instructions: Hang from a bar or rings with straight arms.
Pull the knees tight to the chest and lean back, pressing the hands down toward the hips.
Raise the hips until the back is roughly level with the floor.
Hold with the arms locked, or lower slowly into the position from above, then return to the hang.
exercises.formCue: Straight arms, push the bar to the hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the elbows and letting the hips hang low.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do slow lowering reps from an inverted tuck before holding.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the first front lever step and builds straight-arm pulling strength.

exercises.name: Advanced Tuck Front Lever
instructions: Start in a tuck front lever with the arms straight.
Open the hips so the knees move away from the chest and the back flattens.
Keep the hips level with the shoulders.
Hold for a short time, then tuck back in and lower to the hang.
exercises.formCue: Flat back, hips at shoulder height.
exercises.commonMistakes: Opening the tuck further than you can hold, so the hips drop.
exercises.beginnerModification: Go back to the tight tuck or use slow lowering reps.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Moving the knees away lengthens the lever and loads the lats more.

exercises.name: Tuck Back Lever
exercises.musclesWorked: Shoulders, chest, biceps, lower back, glutes
instructions: Hang from the rings, tuck the knees and roll backward between the arms until inverted.
Keep the knees tucked and the arms straight.
Lower the hips slowly behind you until the back is level with the floor, chest facing down.
Hold briefly, then pull back to the inverted tuck and roll out.
exercises.formCue: Lower slowly, arms long.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping in fast, and forcing the range when the shoulders are not ready.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work on shoulder extension flexibility and lower only part of the way.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the shoulders in extension and the muscles along the back of the body.

exercises.name: Chest-to-Wall Handstand
instructions: Start in a plank with the feet against a wall.
Walk the feet up the wall and the hands in until you are near vertical, chest facing the wall.
Stack wrists, shoulders and hips, push tall through the shoulders and keep the body tight.
Hold while breathing steadily, then walk back down before you tire.
exercises.formCue: Push tall, stack the joints.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching the back and walking in closer than you can safely exit from.
exercises.beginnerModification: Stop at a shallower angle with the hands further from the wall.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Facing the wall teaches a straight handstand line and builds time upside down.

exercises.name: Handstand Kick-Up
instructions: Stand facing a wall, place the hands shoulder width apart a short distance from it and lock the arms.
Step into a short lunge and swing the back leg up while the front leg pushes off lightly.
Let the lead heel touch the wall softly, with the legs still split.
Bring the legs together, hold, then step down one leg at a time.
exercises.formCue: Kick soft enough to barely touch.
exercises.commonMistakes: Kicking too hard and bending the arms on the way up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise small kicks that only reach halfway.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A controlled entry is what makes handstand practice repeatable and safe.

exercises.name: Freestanding Handstand
instructions: Kick up gently in clear space with the arms locked and hands shoulder width apart.
Pause with the legs split, then close them into one straight line.
Balance by pressing through the fingers when you tip over and through the heel of the hand when you fall back.
Step down, or turn out sideways like a cartwheel if you overbalance.
exercises.formCue: Fingers are the brakes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Kicking too hard, and practising before you have a safe way to bail.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work near a wall and float the heels off it for a second at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It develops shoulder strength, balance and body awareness in one skill.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
instructions: Hang from a high bar with an overhand grip a little wider than the shoulders.
Keep the knees straight and the body still.
Raise the legs by bending at the hips until they are at least level with the hips.
Lower them slowly to the hang without swinging.
exercises.formCue: Lift slow, lower slower.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swinging to throw the legs up and dropping them on the way down.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bend the knees and do hanging knee raises.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the abs and hip flexors through a long range while training grip.

exercises.name: Seated Climb
instructions: Add resistance or pick a gear that slows your cadence but still lets the pedals turn smoothly.
Stay in the saddle with the hands relaxed on the bars and the elbows slightly bent.
Keep the upper body still and the head up while the legs drive an even, round pedal stroke.
Hold a steady cadence, shifting to an easier gear before it turns into a grind.
exercises.formCue: Still shoulders, smooth circles.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rocking the upper body and gripping the bars hard, or grinding a gear that is too big.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use less resistance and keep each climb to 2 or 3 minutes.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Seated climbing is the efficient way to hold power for long efforts.

exercises.name: Standing Climb
instructions: Add a gear or a little resistance just before you leave the saddle.
Rise smoothly and keep the hips back over the saddle rather than far forward over the bars.
Let the bike move slightly under you while the pedal stroke stays smooth.
Sit back down, ease the resistance and return to a steady seated cadence.
exercises.formCue: Add a gear, then stand.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing in a gear that is too light so the legs spin out, or throwing the body weight over the front wheel.
exercises.beginnerModification: Stand for 10 to 15 seconds at a time with moderate resistance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Standing gives a short burst of extra force for steep sections and a break for the seated muscles.

exercises.name: Low-Cadence Climb
instructions: Warm up for at least 10 minutes at an easy spin.
Choose a resistance that drops your cadence about 10 rpm below your normal climbing rhythm.
Stay seated and push through the whole pedal circle for about 8 minutes with steady breathing.
Spin easily for several minutes and repeat up to three times.
exercises.formCue: Heavy gear, smooth pressure.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rocking the hips and pulling on the bars to force the gear over, or doing it without a proper warm-up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten each effort to 3 or 4 minutes and drop the cadence only slightly.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Pushing a bigger gear builds the leg strength that makes normal climbing gears feel lighter.

exercises.name: Spin-Ups
instructions: Set a light resistance and pedal at a comfortable cadence.
Over about 30 seconds, raise the cadence steadily until it is as fast as you can hold without bouncing.
Hold that leg speed briefly with the hips still on the saddle.
Let the cadence come back down and spin easily for 1 to 2 minutes before the next one.
exercises.formCue: Fast legs, quiet hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing on the saddle, or adding resistance so it becomes a strength effort.
exercises.beginnerModification: Stop the build as soon as the hips start to bounce and hold just below that cadence.
exercises.whyThisMatters: High leg speed at low load smooths the pedal stroke and coordination.

exercises.name: Cadence Change Drill
instructions: Sit with the sit bones on the widest part of the saddle and set a moderate resistance.
Pedal for 1 minute at 80 rpm, 1 minute at 90 rpm and 1 minute at 100 rpm.
Change the order of the three cadences on the next block without changing resistance.
Spin easily for 60 seconds between blocks.
exercises.formCue: Full circles at every speed.
exercises.commonMistakes: Stamping on the downstroke only, or easing the resistance right off to hit the faster cadences.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use two cadences, 80 and 90 rpm, and a lighter resistance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Switching leg speed on demand teaches control of the pedal stroke across the range.

exercises.name: Sweet-Spot Interval
instructions: Warm up for 10 to 15 minutes, building gradually from easy to moderate.
Settle at an effort just below threshold, hard but steady, with breathing deep and controlled.
Hold that effort and a steady cadence for the full interval, building toward 20 minutes.
Spin easily for 5 minutes, repeat once, then cool down.
exercises.formCue: Hard, but you could go longer.
exercises.commonMistakes: Starting above the target and fading, or letting the effort drift down to an easy ride.
exercises.beginnerModification: Ride intervals of 8 to 10 minutes and add time over several weeks.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Long efforts just under threshold give a lot of aerobic training for a manageable recovery cost.

exercises.name: Bike Sprint Interval
instructions: Warm up thoroughly, including two or three short hard efforts.
From a steady roll, add resistance and sprint at full effort for 15 to 30 seconds with cadence above 90 rpm.
Keep the upper body firm and the pedal stroke as smooth as you can at speed.
Spin very easily until you are ready to match the quality of the first sprint, then go again.
exercises.formCue: Every sprint at full quality.
exercises.commonMistakes: Cutting the recovery so the sprints become medium efforts, or sprinting cold.
exercises.beginnerModification: Sprint seated for 10 seconds with long, easy recoveries.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Short all-out efforts build top-end power and the ability to repeat it.

exercises.name: Arms-and-Body Rowing Drill
instructions: Sit tall at the finish position with the legs straight and the handle drawn in below the ribs.
Keeping the legs flat, extend the arms first and then swing the body forward from the hips.
Swing the body back and then draw the arms in, in that order.
Row this way for a minute or two, then add the legs and row full strokes with the same sequence.
exercises.formCue: Arms away, then body over.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the knees before the hands have passed them, or pulling with the arms before the body swings.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with arms only, then add the body swing once that is smooth.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Isolating the upper half of the stroke fixes the order of movement on the recovery.

exercises.name: Legs-Only Rowing Drill
instructions: Sit at the catch with shins near vertical, arms straight and the body leaning forward from the hips.
Push with the legs while the arms stay straight and the body keeps its forward angle.
Stop when the legs are almost flat, without leaning back or bending the arms.
Slide forward under control and repeat, then build back to full strokes.
exercises.formCue: Legs push, arms hang.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the seat shoot back ahead of the handle, or opening the back early.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a low damper setting and move slowly through each push.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the legs to start the drive, which is where most of the stroke's power comes from.

exercises.name: Rowing Pause Drill
instructions: Row full strokes at a low stroke rate.
On each recovery, stop for a second once the arms are straight and the body has swung forward, before the knees bend.
Check that the hands are past the knees, then slide forward to the catch and take the next stroke.
After a few minutes, remove the pause and keep the same order of movement.
exercises.formCue: Pause, check, then slide.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rushing through the pause, or sliding forward before the hands have cleared the knees.
exercises.beginnerModification: Pause on every second or third stroke instead of every stroke.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A deliberate stop makes you feel the correct sequence before blending it into one motion.

exercises.name: Rowing Rhythm Count
instructions: Row at a low stroke rate with light to moderate pressure.
Count one as you drive back quickly with the legs, body and arms.
Count two, three and four as you move forward slowly through the recovery.
Keep the count going so the drive stays quick and the recovery stays unhurried.
exercises.formCue: Quick drive, slow slide.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rushing forward on the slide so the drive and recovery take the same time.
exercises.beginnerModification: Say the count out loud and row with very light pressure.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A slower recovery gives a moment of rest every stroke, which is what makes long rows sustainable.

exercises.name: Rowing Steady State
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, lats, upper back, core
instructions: Warm up with 5 minutes of easy rowing.
Settle at a stroke rate in the mid 20s and an effort you could hold a conversation through.
Keep the same split and rate for the whole piece, with legs, then body, then arms on each drive.
Finish with a few minutes of light rowing.
exercises.formCue: Same rate, same split.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the stroke rate climb as you tire while each stroke gets shorter and weaker.
exercises.beginnerModification: Break the session into 5-minute blocks with a minute of easy paddling between them.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Long, even rowing builds aerobic fitness and gives hundreds of strokes of technique practice.

exercises.name: Rowing Rate Ladder
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, lats, upper back, core
instructions: Warm up, then start rowing at a low stroke rate with firm pressure.
After a set time, such as 2 to 3 minutes, raise the rate by two strokes per minute.
Keep stepping the rate up at each change while holding the same stroke length and sequence.
Come back down the same steps, then row lightly to cool down.
exercises.formCue: Rate goes up, length stays.
exercises.commonMistakes: Shortening the stroke to hit the higher rates, or speeding up the slide instead of the drive.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use only three steps and keep the top rate within a comfortable range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Changing rate on command teaches you to hold good strokes as the tempo rises.

exercises.name: Negative-Split Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, lats, upper back, core
instructions: Row easily for a few minutes and note the 500-metre split you can hold comfortably.
Divide the piece into equal blocks and row the first block at that comfortable split.
Make each following block slightly faster, pushing harder with the legs rather than rushing the slide.
Row the last block at a strong effort, then paddle lightly to recover.
exercises.formCue: Finish faster than you started.
exercises.commonMistakes: Going out too fast so later blocks slow down, or raising the stroke rate without adding leg drive.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use only two blocks, the second a little quicker than the first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Building pace through a piece teaches pacing control and a strong finish.

exercises.name: Freestyle Catch-Up Drill
instructions: Push off and swim freestyle with a steady kick.
Leave the leading arm stretched out in front of its shoulder while the other arm takes a full stroke.
Bring the recovering hand forward to meet the leading hand before the next arm starts its pull.
Keep the hands in line with the shoulders rather than crossing the centre line.
exercises.formCue: One arm waits for the other.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hands cross in front of the head, or letting the kick stop while the arm waits.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold a kickboard out front and swap hands on the board with each stroke.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Slowing the stroke down fixes hand entry and timing at the front of the stroke.

exercises.name: One-Arm Freestyle Drill
instructions: Push off with one arm resting by the side and the other ready to stroke.
Swim freestyle with the working arm only, keeping a steady kick.
Breathe on every stroke toward the side of the resting arm.
Rotate the body to both sides, then switch arms on the next length.
exercises.formCue: Rotate both ways, even with one arm.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swimming flat with no body rotation, or lifting the head forward to breathe.
exercises.beginnerModification: Wear fins so the kick holds the body position while you learn the rotation.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It exposes a flat body position and trains rotation and breath timing.

exercises.name: Swim Kick Set
exercises.musclesWorked: Hip flexors, glutes, quads, hamstrings, core
instructions: Push off in a long line on the front, side or back with the arms still.
Kick from the hips with a small, quick flutter, letting the knees and ankles stay loose.
Point the toes backward and keep the kick narrow.
Kick one length, rest briefly and repeat, changing between side, front and back.
exercises.formCue: Small kick, from the hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Kicking from the knees with big bends, or arching the back to hold the head up on a board.
exercises.beginnerModification: Kick on the back with fins so breathing is easy and the body stays level.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A narrow hip-driven kick holds the body level, which makes every stroke easier.

exercises.name: Pull Buoy Set
instructions: Place a pull buoy between the thighs and push off with the legs still.
After each hand enters, let the hand drop down and in while the elbow bends and points out to the side.
Press straight back against the water, speeding the hand up through the pull.
Finish just past the hip and bring the arm forward relaxed.
exercises.formCue: Elbow high, press straight back.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pressing down on the water with a straight arm, or dropping the elbow at the start of the pull.
exercises.beginnerModification: Swim short repeats of one length with plenty of rest and an easy stroke rate.
exercises.whyThisMatters: With the legs supported, all attention can go to how the arms hold and move water.

exercises.name: Freestyle Breathing Drill
instructions: Stand in shallow water and practise bobs, breathing out steadily underwater and in quickly at the surface.
Push off and swim easy freestyle, breathing out through the nose and mouth the whole time the face is down.
To breathe, turn the head with the body's rotation and keep one goggle in the water.
Take a quick breath, return the face to the water and carry on the stroke without a pause.
exercises.formCue: Breathe out under, turn to breathe in.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting the head forward, which sinks the hips, or holding the breath underwater.
exercises.beginnerModification: Kick on the side with the bottom arm extended and practise turning the face in and out of the water.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Calm, low breathing keeps the body level and lets you swim further for less effort.

exercises.name: Backstroke
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, shoulders, triceps, core, hip flexors
instructions: Lie on the back near the surface with the head still, ears in the water and hips high.
Kick from the hips with the legs close together, ankles loose and knees only slightly bent.
Lift one arm out thumb first, keep it straight overhead and enter the water little finger first.
Catch the water, push through to the thigh and breathe in a steady rhythm with the arm cycle.
exercises.formCue: Head still, hips up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Carrying the head too high so the hips sink, or pulling hard the instant the hand enters.
exercises.beginnerModification: Kick on the back with arms by the sides, then add one arm at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the back of the shoulders and lets you breathe freely, which balances a lot of freestyle.

exercises.name: Breaststroke
instructions: Start in a long glide, face down, with the body close to level and arms extended.
Sweep the hands out and down with the elbows high, then in toward the chest as the shoulders rise and you breathe in.
Draw the heels toward the seat, turn the feet out and kick round and back until the legs come together.
Reach the arms forward and glide in a straight line, breathing out, before the next stroke.
exercises.formCue: Pull, kick, glide.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling the hands too wide and too far back, or kicking while the arms are still pulling.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the kick on its own with a board, then add one pull to every two kicks.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The glide makes it a sustainable stroke, and the legs do most of the work.

exercises.name: Basic Step
instructions: Stand close to the platform, within about a foot of it, facing the long side.
Step up with the lead foot and place the whole foot on the platform.
Step up with the other foot so both feet are on top.
Step down with the lead foot and then the other, letting each heel reach the floor.
exercises.formCue: Up, up, down, down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the heel hang off the back edge, or stepping down far away from the platform.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the lowest platform height, or march the same pattern on the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The four-count basic is the base pattern for every other step move.

exercises.name: V-Step on the Step
instructions: Stand behind the centre of the platform with your feet together.
Step the lead foot up to the far corner on its own side.
Step the other foot up to the opposite corner so your feet are wide on top.
Step the lead foot back down to the centre and bring the other foot down beside it.
exercises.formCue: Out, out, in, in.
exercises.commonMistakes: Landing with only the toes on the platform, or letting the knees drop inward in the wide position.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do the same wide-then-narrow pattern on the floor first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The wide placement brings the outer hips into ordinary stepping.

exercises.name: Over the Top
instructions: Stand side-on to the platform with the near foot beside it.
Step the near foot up onto the middle of the platform.
Bring the other foot up, then step the first foot down on the far side.
Bring the trailing foot down beside it and repeat in the other direction.
exercises.formCue: Up and over, land close.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jumping across and landing far from the platform, or twisting the knee of the planted foot.
exercises.beginnerModification: Step up and return to the same side until the sideways step feels secure.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Travelling across the platform adds lateral work to step training.

exercises.name: Step Knee Lift
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, hip flexors, core, calves
instructions: Stand close to the platform and step the lead foot up with the whole foot on top.
Lift the other knee to about hip height while standing tall on the platform leg.
Lower that foot back to the floor.
Step the lead foot down, then repeat with the other foot leading.
exercises.formCue: Stand tall, then lift.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning back to raise the knee, or pushing off hard from the floor instead of standing up through the top leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Replace the knee lift with a light toe tap on the platform.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It adds a single-leg balance moment to each step cycle.

exercises.name: Repeater Knee
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, quads, hip flexors, calves, core
instructions: Step the lead foot onto the platform near one corner and keep it there.
Lift the other knee, then tap that foot lightly back on the floor.
Repeat the knee lift three times in a row, keeping your weight over the platform leg.
Step down, then start the next set with the other foot leading.
exercises.formCue: Weight stays on top.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing off the floor foot between lifts, or letting the platform knee cave inward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do a single knee lift each time instead of three.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Holding one leg on the platform for several counts builds leg endurance.

exercises.name: Aerobic March
instructions: Stand tall with your feet under your hips.
March on the spot with one foot meeting the floor on each beat.
Swing your arms naturally in opposition to your legs.
Vary it by travelling forward, back, or to the side, or by lifting the knees higher.
exercises.formCue: One foot per beat.
exercises.commonMistakes: Slumping through the trunk, or stamping heavily instead of placing the feet.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the knees low and march at half tempo.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The march is the low-impact base that most aerobic routines are built on.

source.name: City College of San Francisco, Physical Education (aerobic exercise handout)

exercises.name: V-Step
instructions: Stand with your feet together.
Step the lead foot forward and out on a diagonal.
Step the other foot forward and out so your feet are wide.
Step the lead foot back to the start and bring the other foot in beside it.
exercises.formCue: Out, out, in, in.
exercises.commonMistakes: Turning the pattern into a narrow shuffle, or locking the knees in the wide position.
exercises.beginnerModification: Make the V smaller and slow the tempo.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It adds forward and sideways travel to a simple walking pattern.

exercises.name: Mambo
instructions: Stand with your feet together and knees soft.
Step the lead foot forward and shift your weight onto it.
Shift your weight back onto the rear foot.
Step the lead foot back behind you, shift onto it, then return your weight to the other foot and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Rock forward, rock back.
exercises.commonMistakes: Taking steps so long that the trunk tips, or keeping the hips stiff.
exercises.beginnerModification: Take smaller steps and leave the arms at your sides.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The mambo teaches smooth weight transfer between the front and back foot.

exercises.name: Rock-Step Cha-Cha
instructions: Stand with your feet together.
Step one foot back and rock your weight onto it.
Transfer your weight forward onto the front foot again.
Take three small quick steps on the spot, then repeat starting with the other foot.
exercises.formCue: Rock, replace, quick-quick-quick.
exercises.commonMistakes: Making the three quick steps too large, or losing the beat between the rock and the triple step.
exercises.beginnerModification: Replace the three quick steps with two marches.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Mixing slow and quick steps builds rhythm and light footwork.

exercises.name: Box Step
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Step the lead foot across in front of the other foot.
Step the other foot straight back.
Step the lead foot out to the side, then bring the feet together to finish the square.
exercises.formCue: Across, back, side, together.
exercises.commonMistakes: Twisting the knee of the planted foot on the cross step, or rushing so the square collapses.
exercises.beginnerModification: Walk through the four placements slowly without music first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The four-point pattern trains coordination and changes of direction.

exercises.name: Chasse Step
instructions: Stand tall with knees soft.
Step one foot out to the side.
Bring the other foot in to meet it with a quick closing step.
Step the first foot out to the side again, then repeat in the other direction.
exercises.formCue: Side, close, side.
exercises.commonMistakes: Crossing the feet, or bouncing high instead of gliding.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do a plain step touch until the three-step rhythm feels comfortable.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A quick three-step travel raises the heart rate without jumping.

exercises.name: Pivot Turn
instructions: Stand with your feet together.
Step one foot forward and place your weight on the balls of both feet.
Turn 180 degrees toward the back foot, rotating on the balls of the feet.
Shift your weight onto the new front foot, then repeat to return to the start.
exercises.formCue: Step, turn on the balls of the feet.
exercises.commonMistakes: Turning with the heels planted, which twists the knees, or looking down and losing balance.
exercises.beginnerModification: Swap the turn for a four-count march until you are ready to add it.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Turning adds a change of direction and a balance challenge to simple choreography.

exercises.name: Low-Impact Jack
instructions: Stand with your feet together and arms at your sides.
Tap one foot out to the side while raising both arms out and overhead.
Bring the foot back in as the arms lower.
Repeat on the other side and keep alternating at a steady pace.
exercises.formCue: Tap out, arms up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears, or leaning away from the tapping foot.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise the arms only to shoulder height.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It keeps the pattern of a jumping jack while one foot stays on the floor.

exercises.name: Step Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet a little wider than your hips.
Step onto one foot and shift your weight over it.
Bend the other knee to bring that heel toward your glute.
Set the foot down wide and repeat on the other side.
exercises.formCue: Shift, then curl the heel up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Tipping the chest forward, or swinging the leg instead of bending the knee.
exercises.beginnerModification: Tap the toe behind you instead of curling the heel up.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the back of the legs inside a low-impact side-to-side pattern.

source.name: City College of San Francisco, Physical Education (aerobic exercise handout)

exercises.name: Alternating Knee Lift
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step onto one foot and lift the other knee to about hip height.
Lower that foot and step onto it.
Lift the opposite knee and continue alternating in time.
exercises.formCue: Tall spine, knee to hip height.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning back as the knee rises, or dropping the chest toward the knee.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift the knee lower, or tap the toe in front instead.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Knee lifts raise the heart rate while one foot always stays grounded.

exercises.name: Cross-Step Touch
instructions: Stand with your feet together and knees soft.
Step to the side with one foot.
Cross the other foot in front and touch the toe to the floor.
Step that foot back out to its own side and cross-touch with the first foot.
exercises.formCue: Step wide, touch across.
exercises.commonMistakes: Putting weight on the crossing foot, or twisting the knees instead of turning from the hips.
exercises.beginnerModification: Touch the foot beside the standing foot instead of crossing.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The crossing touch adds hip movement and coordination to a basic side step.

exercises.name: Dance Hip Circles
exercises.musclesWorked: Obliques, glutes, hip rotators, lower back
instructions: Stand with your feet a little wider than your hips and knees soft.
Push your hips to one side, then to the back, the other side, and the front.
Join the four points into one smooth circle.
Complete several circles, then reverse the direction.
exercises.formCue: Knees soft, circle from the hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Locking the knees, or swaying the shoulders instead of moving the hips.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do only the side-to-side shifts before linking the full circle.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Controlled hip circles loosen the hips and trunk for dance work.

exercises.name: Side-to-Side Rock
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than your hips and knees soft.
Shift your weight onto one foot and let the other heel lift.
Shift smoothly across to the other foot.
Keep rocking at a slow, even tempo while letting your breathing settle.
exercises.formCue: Slow shift, easy breath.
exercises.commonMistakes: Stopping suddenly after hard work instead of slowing down gradually, or locking the knees.
exercises.beginnerModification: Narrow the stance and make the shift smaller.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Simple rhythmic movement brings the heart rate down gradually before stretching.

exercises.name: Air Squat
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes turned out slightly.
Send the hips back and down while the chest stays tall and the knees follow the toes.
Lower until the hip crease drops below the top of the knees with the heels flat.
Drive through the whole foot and stand until hips and knees are fully straight.
exercises.formCue: Hip crease below the knee, then stand all the way up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Cutting the depth short, or letting the knees cave in and the heels lift as the weight shifts to the toes.
exercises.beginnerModification: Squat to a box or bench set just below knee height and stand from there.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A full-depth, fully-locked-out squat is the standard every loaded squat and thruster is built on.

exercises.name: Barbell Thruster
instructions: Hold the bar in the front rack with a full grip just outside the shoulders and elbows up in front of the bar.
Squat until the hip crease is below the knees while the chest and elbows stay high.
Stand up hard and let the drive from the legs lift the bar off the shoulders.
Press only after the hips and knees are straight, and lock the bar out over the middle of the foot.
Bring the bar back to the shoulders before you start the next squat.
exercises.formCue: Legs first, arms last.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pressing before the legs have finished extending, or starting the next squat before the bar is back on the shoulders.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use dumbbells or an empty bar and squat to a ball or box to learn the depth.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the legs and arms to share one lift, which makes it one of the most demanding conditioning movements with a barbell.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift High Pull
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, traps, upper back, shoulders
instructions: Stand wider than shoulder width with the bar over midfoot and grip it with both hands inside the knees.
Set a flat back with the chest up and the arms straight.
Push the floor away and keep the bar close until the hips and knees are fully extended.
Shrug, then pull the elbows high and out until the bar reaches about collarbone height.
Lower in reverse order: arms straighten first, then the hips and knees bend.
exercises.formCue: Stand tall first, then elbows high and outside.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the arms before the hips open, or rounding the lower back off the floor.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a single light kettlebell and stop the pull at chest height.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the hips-then-arms sequence that every clean, snatch and medicine-ball clean depends on.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Clean
instructions: Stand over the ball with feet shoulder-width apart, squat down with the chest up and place a palm on each side of the ball.
Stand up with straight arms until the hips and knees are fully open.
Shrug hard, then drop under the ball right away and turn the hands beneath it.
Catch it at the shoulders in the bottom of a squat with the elbows up.
Stand to full height before lowering the ball for the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Jump, shrug, drop under.
exercises.commonMistakes: Curling the ball up with the arms, or pulling before the hips have fully opened.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a very light ball and catch in a shallow squat until the timing is smooth.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the pull-under of the clean with a load that is safe to miss.

exercises.name: Kipping Pull-Up
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, biceps, shoulders, abs, hip flexors
instructions: Hang with arms straight, hands just outside the shoulders and the shoulders pulled slightly away from the ears.
Swing from the shoulders between an arched position with the chest forward and a hollow position with the feet forward.
As the body rises out of the hollow, pull with the arms until the chin clears the bar.
Push away from the bar at the top and fall back into the arch to load the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Swing from the shoulders, then pull late.
exercises.commonMistakes: Driving the swing with the legs instead of the shoulders, or dropping from the top with loose shoulders.
exercises.beginnerModification: Build strict pull-ups first, then practise kip swings alone without the pull.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Using the whole body lets you do more pulling work in less time once strict strength is in place.

exercises.name: Chest-to-Bar Pull-Up
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, rhomboids, rear delts, biceps, abs
instructions: Hang with straight arms and start a controlled kip swing from the shoulders.
Out of the hollow position, drive the hips up and pull the elbows down and back.
Keep pulling until the chest touches the bar below the collarbone.
Push away from the bar and return to a full hang before the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Pull the bar to your sternum, elbows behind you.
exercises.commonMistakes: Stopping at chin height, or reaching with the chin and neck instead of pulling the elbows back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do strict or kipping pull-ups to the chin, or ring rows pulled all the way to the chest.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The longer pull builds the height and upper-back strength that bar muscle-ups need.

exercises.name: Kipping Bar Muscle-Up
instructions: Hang with straight arms and build a strong kip swing from arch to hollow.
From the back of the swing, drive the hips toward the bar while pulling it down toward the waist with straight-ish arms.
As the hips rise, sit the chest fast over the bar so the shoulders end up above the hands.
Press out to straight arms in the support position.
Lower with control and push away from the bar to re-enter the swing.
exercises.formCue: Hips to the bar, then chest over fast.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling with bent arms too early so the hips never rise, or landing on one elbow at a time.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work strict pull-ups, chest-to-bar pull-ups and bar dips, and practise the turnover by jumping from a box.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It links a pull and a dip into one movement that takes you from hanging below the bar to supported above it.

exercises.name: Toes-to-Bar
instructions: Hang with straight arms and start a small kip swing from arch to hollow.
As you move into the hollow, press down on the bar with the lats and lift both feet together.
Touch both feet to the bar at the same time between the hands.
Pull the feet back and down while the chest moves forward into the arch, ready for the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Push the bar down, bring the toes up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the legs drop loosely so the swing gets wild, or bending the arms to reach the bar.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do hanging knee raises, or alternate one leg at a time toward the bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the trunk and lats to work with a hanging grip, which carries over to every bar gymnastics skill.

exercises.name: Strict Toes-to-Bar
instructions: Hang completely still with straight arms and legs together.
Press into the bar with straight arms and lift the legs as straight as your flexibility allows.
Curl the hips up until both feet touch the bar.
Lower slowly to a dead hang without swinging.
exercises.formCue: No swing, straight arms, legs together.
exercises.commonMistakes: Using a swing to start the rep, or bending the arms to shorten the distance.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise straight legs to hip height only, or do strict hanging knee raises.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Taking the swing away builds the trunk strength and control that make the kipping version safe.

exercises.name: Knees-to-Elbows
instructions: Hang from the bar with straight arms and the shoulders active.
Press down on the bar and pull the knees up toward the chest.
Keep curling the hips until the knees touch the elbows.
Lower with control to a full hang before the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Curl the hips, knees meet elbows.
exercises.commonMistakes: Stopping at hip height, or swinging so much that momentum does the work.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise the knees to hip or chest height and build range over time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the bridge between a basic knee raise and toes-to-bar.

exercises.name: Single-Under
instructions: Hold a handle in each hand with elbows close to the ribs and hands slightly in front of the hips.
Turn the rope from the wrists, not the shoulders.
Jump just high enough for the rope to pass once, with a tall body and a soft bend in the knees.
Land on the balls of the feet and keep an even rhythm.
exercises.formCue: Small jump, quiet feet, wrists turn the rope.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jumping too high with a double bounce, or letting the hands drift wide so the rope shortens and trips.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the jump without a rope, tapping the thighs once per jump for timing.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A relaxed, efficient single bounce is the base that double-unders are built on.

exercises.name: Wall Walk
instructions: Lie face down with the feet against the wall and the hands under the shoulders.
Press up and walk the feet up the wall while walking the hands back toward it.
Keep the ribs down and the body tight until the chest is close to the wall.
Walk the hands out and the feet down under control until the chest is back on the floor.
exercises.formCue: Tight middle, small hand steps.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the lower back sag as the feet climb, or rushing the way down and dropping off the wall.
exercises.beginnerModification: Walk only part of the way up, stopping when the hips are above the shoulders.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It introduces being upside down while hands, feet and wall keep you supported.

exercises.name: Strict Handstand Push-Up
exercises.musclesWorked: Shoulders, triceps, upper chest, traps, abs
instructions: Kick up to a handstand against the wall with hands just outside shoulder width and fingers turned out slightly.
Squeeze the glutes and abs so the body stays in one line.
Lower slowly until the top of the head touches the mat lightly in front of the hands, forming a triangle with the hands.
Press straight back up to locked elbows without resting on the head.
exercises.formCue: Head and hands make a triangle, lower like a feather.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping onto the head, or placing the head in line with the hands so the elbows flare and the press stalls.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do pike push-ups with the feet on a box so the hips sit over the shoulders.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds overhead pressing strength and balance with nothing but bodyweight.

exercises.name: Kipping Handstand Push-Up
instructions: Lower under control from the handstand to the head-and-hands triangle, keeping most of the weight on the hands.
Slide the hips against the wall and draw the knees down toward the chest.
Kick both feet straight up toward the ceiling.
Press hard through the hands as the legs extend and finish with locked elbows and a straight body.
exercises.formCue: Knees down, kick up, press.
exercises.commonMistakes: Crashing onto the head on the way down, or pressing before the leg drive so the kip adds nothing.
exercises.beginnerModification: Earn several slow strict reps first, and until then use box pike push-ups.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The leg drive lets you keep pressing overhead when strict strength alone would run out.

exercises.name: Box Step-Over
instructions: Stand facing the box with feet about hip-width apart.
Place one whole foot on top and drive through it to stand up on the box.
Step the other foot onto the box, then step down on the far side one foot at a time.
Turn around and repeat, leading with the other leg.
exercises.formCue: Whole foot on the box, push with the top leg.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pushing off the floor with the back leg, or letting the lead knee cave inward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a low step and hold nothing in the hands.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It gives single-leg strength and conditioning without the impact of jumping.

exercises.name: Burpee Box Jump-Over
instructions: Stand next to or facing the box and drop to the floor until chest and thighs touch.
Push up and bring both feet under the hips.
Jump onto or over the box and land softly with bent knees.
Step or hop down on the far side, turn, and start the next burpee there.
exercises.formCue: Chest down, feet under you, then jump.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jumping while still off balance from the burpee, or landing with stiff legs.
exercises.beginnerModification: Step back and up in the burpee and step over a lower box.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It pairs getting off the floor with a jump, a hard test of conditioning and coordination under fatigue.

exercises.name: Bar-Facing Burpee
instructions: Stand facing a loaded barbell on the floor, square to it.
Drop down with the hands inside the plates until chest and thighs touch the floor.
Push up and bring the feet back under the hips.
Jump over the bar from two feet, land on two feet, then turn to face the bar again.
exercises.formCue: Face the bar, two feet up, two feet down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Drifting sideways to the bar, or stepping over one leg at a time when a two-foot jump is the standard.
exercises.beginnerModification: Step back and up in the burpee and step over the bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The fixed line to jump keeps every rep honest when you are tired.

exercises.name: Rope Climb
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, biceps, forearms, abs, hip flexors
instructions: Reach high on the rope with both hands and let it run down the outside of one leg.
Lift the knees, wrap the rope under that foot and over the top of the other, and clamp it between the feet.
Stand up on the clamp while reaching the hands higher.
Repeat the knees-up, clamp and stand until you reach the top.
Come down hand under hand while easing the foot clamp, never sliding.
exercises.formCue: Clamp with the feet, stand with the legs.
exercises.commonMistakes: Hauling with the arms alone because the foot lock slips, or sliding down and burning the hands and shins.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the foot lock from a seated box, or lower to lying and pull back to standing on the rope.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A secure foot lock turns the climb into leg work and saves the grip.

exercises.name: GHD Sit-Up
instructions: Sit on the glute-ham developer with the feet locked in and the hips just past the edge of the pad.
Lean back under control with a slight bend in the knees and the abs braced.
Go only as far as you can keep the lower back from over-arching.
Straighten the knees sharply and sit up until the hands reach the foot pads.
exercises.formCue: Brace going back, snap the knees to come up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Doing too many reps too soon, or relaxing the abs at the bottom so the lower back hangs.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower only to parallel with the floor and keep the volume low for the first weeks.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the hip flexors through a long range while the abs learn to hold the spine steady.

exercises.name: GHD Hip Extension
instructions: Lock the feet in face down with the hip crease clear of the pad so the hips can bend freely.
Brace and set a flat, neutral back.
Fold at the hips and lower the torso while the back stays flat.
Squeeze the glutes and hamstrings to rise until the body is in one straight line.
exercises.formCue: Flat back, hinge only at the hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding and unrounding the spine instead of hinging, or over-arching past a straight line at the top.
exercises.beginnerModification: Cross the arms on the chest and shorten the range, or do a bodyweight good-morning on the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The hips do the work while the trunk holds still, the same demand as a deadlift.

exercises.name: Overhead Walking Lunge
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, shoulders, upper back, trunk
instructions: Press the weight overhead and lock the elbows with the arms beside the ears.
Step forward and lower until the back knee touches the floor lightly.
Keep the torso upright and the weight stacked over the shoulders and hips.
Drive through the front heel to stand and step straight into the next lunge.
exercises.formCue: Arms locked, ribs down, knee kisses the floor.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the elbows soften and the weight drift forward, or leaning the chest toward the front knee.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold one light dumbbell overhead with both hands, or lunge with no load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Holding a load overhead while the legs work shows up any weak link in shoulder and trunk stability.

exercises.name: Ring Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, rhomboids, rear delts, biceps, abs
instructions: Hold the rings with straight arms and lean back with the body in one line from head to heels.
Walk the feet forward to make it harder or back to make it easier.
Pull the chest to the rings with the elbows close to the ribs.
Lower until the arms are straight without letting the hips sag.
exercises.formCue: Body like a plank, chest to the rings.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping or thrusting the hips, or stopping the pull short of the chest.
exercises.beginnerModification: Stand more upright with the feet further back.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The angle is adjustable in seconds, so it builds pulling strength at any level.

exercises.name: Ring Dip
instructions: Hold a steady support on the rings with arms locked and the rings close to the hips.
Lower under control with the elbows tracking back and the rings kept near the body.
Go down until the shoulders are below the elbows.
Press back up to a full lockout and steady the rings before the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Rings tight to the body, finish locked out.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the rings drift wide, or cutting the depth and the lockout short.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the top support for time, or keep the feet on the floor or a band to take some weight.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The unstable rings make the shoulders control the whole range, building strength a fixed bar does not ask for.

exercises.name: Lateral Cone Jump
instructions: Stand just beside a low cone with feet hip-width apart, shoulders down and midsection braced.
Sit the hips back into a short quarter squat with the chest lifted and the back flat.
Without pausing, jump up and sideways over the cone with both feet leaving and staying level together.
Land softly on the middle of both feet, let the hips drop back to absorb the landing, then jump back the other way.
exercises.formCue: Land quiet, hips back.
exercises.commonMistakes: Landing stiff-legged with the knees caving in, or rushing reps before each landing is under control.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hop side to side over a line on the floor and pause to reset between each hop.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains you to produce and absorb force sideways, which straight-ahead jumping never covers.

exercises.name: Lateral Bound
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hip abductors and adductors, quads, calves
instructions: Stand with feet close together, knees and hips slightly bent, and lift one foot just off the floor.
Push off the standing leg and jump as far to the side as you can control.
Land on the opposite foot with the knee bent and the other foot held off the ground.
Hold the landing for a moment until you are steady, then bound back the other way.
exercises.formCue: Stick the landing before you go again.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the landing knee collapse inward, or bouncing straight out of a landing you never controlled.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the distance and tap the trailing foot down for balance on each landing.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Single-leg landings build the hip control that protects knees when you change direction.

exercises.name: Battle Rope Alternating Wave
exercises.musclesWorked: Shoulders, forearms, upper back, core, legs
instructions: Face the anchor holding one rope end in each hand, feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent and back straight.
Lean the torso slightly forward from the hips and brace the midsection.
Raise one hand to about shoulder height while the other drops to waist height, then switch quickly.
Keep the arms trading places at a steady rhythm so each wave travels the full length of the rope.
exercises.formCue: Fast hands, quiet torso.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing bolt upright with locked knees, or letting the waves shrink as the arms tire instead of ending the interval.
exercises.beginnerModification: Step closer to the anchor for more slack, make smaller waves and work in 10 to 15 second bursts.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It drives the heart rate up hard with almost no impact on the legs.

exercises.name: Battle Rope Double Wave
instructions: Face the anchor with one rope end in each hand, feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft and back straight.
Lean slightly forward from the hips and brace the midsection.
Lift both hands together to about shoulder height, then drive them down to waist height.
Repeat at a quick, even tempo so both ropes ripple to the anchor side by side.
exercises.formCue: Both hands move as one.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back to chase bigger waves, or shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a shorter or thinner rope and keep the waves small and rhythmic.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Moving both arms together loads the trunk and hips more than the alternating version.

exercises.name: Battle Rope Slam
instructions: Face the anchor with a rope end in each hand, feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Lift both rope ends up to head height or just above, rising tall through the hips.
Drive both arms down hard and fast so the rope hits the floor in front of you, letting the hips sit back as it lands.
Stand tall again and repeat with full effort on every rep.
exercises.formCue: Tall, then slam it down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Slamming with the arms only and no hip action, or rounding the back at the bottom of each rep.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift the rope only to chest height and slam at about half effort until the rhythm feels natural.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A full-body power effort you can repeat at top intensity without a hard landing.

exercises.name: Air Bike Sprint
instructions: Set the seat so your knee keeps a slight bend at the bottom of the pedal stroke, then pedal easily for a few minutes to warm up.
Start the interval by pushing and pulling the handles while driving the pedals, building to full effort within a few strokes.
Hold that effort for the whole interval, usually 10 to 30 seconds, keeping the pedal stroke smooth.
Spin very lightly through the rest period before the next sprint.
exercises.formCue: Push and pull the handles, legs follow.
exercises.commonMistakes: Going so hard on the first sprint that the remaining rounds collapse, or bouncing in the saddle with a choppy stroke.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work at a hard but repeatable effort for 15 seconds and rest for 45 seconds.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Resistance rises with your effort, so it delivers true sprint work with no impact.

exercises.name: SkiErg Double-Pole
instructions: Stand facing the machine with feet about shoulder-width apart and take the handles with hands slightly above eye level and elbows bent.
Start the pull by crunching the trunk forward and driving the handles down, letting the knees bend a comfortable amount.
Finish with the hands passing beside the thighs and the arms nearly straight.
Stand back up tall as the arms return along the same narrow path to the start.
exercises.formCue: Crunch down, stand up tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping into a deep squat on every stroke, or swinging the arms wide on the way back up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Slow the stroke rate and use a low damper setting while you learn the timing.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the pulling muscles and trunk for conditioning while the legs get a break from impact.

exercises.name: Shuttle Run
instructions: Mark a start line and three or four lines at increasing distances, such as the lines of a basketball court.
Sprint from the start to the nearest line, touch it with a foot, and sprint back to the start.
Go straight out to the next line and back, and continue until you have reached the farthest line.
Walk for 60 to 90 seconds before the next round.
exercises.formCue: Sink the hips into every turn.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing tall through the turns, or pacing the early lengths so slowly that it stops being a sprint.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use two lines a short distance apart and run at a strong stride instead of a full sprint.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Repeated stops and restarts build conditioning that steady running does not.

exercises.name: Stair Sprint
instructions: Warm up with a few minutes of easy stair walking and light jogging up the steps.
Run up the flight touching every step, staying on the balls of the feet with the eyes forward.
Lean slightly forward and pump the arms to drive the knees up.
Walk back down under control as your recovery, then repeat.
exercises.formCue: Eyes up, arms drive.
exercises.commonMistakes: Running back down the stairs, or staring at the feet and folding at the waist.
exercises.beginnerModification: Walk briskly up the stairs, or pick a flight that takes about 10 seconds to climb.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Each step is a small single-leg push, so it builds leg power and fitness together.

exercises.name: Lateral Stair Run
instructions: Stand side-on to the bottom of the stairs with knees soft and one hand near the rail.
Step the top foot up one stair and bring the bottom foot up to join it.
Keep moving sideways up the flight with quick, light steps and the hips facing the rail.
Walk down normally, then repeat facing the other way.
exercises.formCue: Stay side-on, quick feet.
exercises.commonMistakes: Crossing the feet before the pattern is learned, or turning the hips to face up the stairs.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it at walking speed with a hand on the rail.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the outer hips that forward stair running misses.

exercises.name: Rotational Jack
instructions: Stand tall with feet together and arms by the sides.
Jump the feet out into a wide squat while turning the trunk and reaching one hand toward the floor and the other toward the ceiling.
Jump the feet back together and return to standing.
Repeat, turning and reaching to the other side.
exercises.formCue: Sit into the squat, then reach.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending from the lower back to touch the floor instead of sitting the hips down.
exercises.beginnerModification: Step out to the wide squat one foot at a time instead of jumping.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It adds a squat and a twist to the jumping jack, so more muscle works in the same time.

exercises.name: Lunge Mountain Climber
instructions: Start in a high plank with hands under the shoulders and the body in a straight line.
Step or jump one foot up to land outside the hand on the same side.
Switch legs in one movement so the other foot lands outside its hand.
Keep alternating while the shoulders stay over the wrists.
exercises.formCue: Foot to the outside of the hand.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hips pike up or the shoulders drift behind the hands as the feet switch.
exercises.beginnerModification: Step each foot forward and back one at a time rather than jumping the switch.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The longer stride opens the hips while the shoulders and trunk hold the plank.

exercises.name: Plank Knee Drive
instructions: Set up in a high plank with hands under the shoulders and feet about hip-width apart.
Draw one knee toward the chest without letting the hips rise.
Return the foot to the floor and set the plank again.
Repeat with the other knee and keep alternating at a controlled pace.
exercises.formCue: Hips level, knee to chest.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing the hips up and down, or rushing until the plank position falls apart.
exercises.beginnerModification: Place the hands on a bench or step to take load off the shoulders.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the plank position under movement before you add speed.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge Power Knee
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot back and lower into a lunge with the front foot flat.
Push through the front foot and drive the back knee forward and up to hip height as you stand.
Step the same leg straight back into the next rep, and finish all reps before switching sides.
exercises.formCue: Drive the knee, stand tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pushing off the back foot instead of the front leg, or leaning the trunk back as the knee comes up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Pause with both feet together between the lunge and the knee lift.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It joins a strength move to a fast knee drive, which trains the legs the way running uses them.

exercises.name: Kneeling Ball Slam
instructions: Kneel tall on a mat with the knees hip-width apart and hold a slam ball in both hands.
Reach the ball overhead with arms long and hips fully extended.
Throw the hips back toward the heels and slam the ball into the floor in front of the knees.
Collect the ball and rise back to tall kneeling for the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Hips back as the ball goes down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Slamming with the arms alone, or arching the lower back when reaching overhead.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter ball and slow the tempo, resetting fully between reps.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Taking the legs out teaches the hip and trunk action of the slam before you stand up.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Clean
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, upper back, forearms, core
instructions: Set the bell in front of you, hinge and hike it back between the legs like a swing.
Drive the hips and keep the elbow close to the ribs so the bell travels up, not out.
Loosen the grip and slide the hand around the handle so the bell rolls onto the forearm.
Finish in the rack with the wrist straight and forearm vertical, then drop it back into the next hike.
exercises.formCue: Elbow glued to the ribs, bell goes up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Casting the bell away from the body so it bangs the forearm, and gripping too hard to let it roll.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise low swings and a two-hand clean before going to one hand.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A clean rack is the starting point for kettlebell presses, squats and carries.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Clean and Press
instructions: Stand hip width apart with one bell and swing it back between the legs with a flat back.
Drive the hips, pull the bell up close and drop the elbow to the ribs to catch it at the shoulder.
Pause in the rack, then press the bell overhead to a straight arm.
Pull the elbow back down to the rack and let the bell swing back for the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Clean it quiet, then press.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pressing from a loose rack and leaning back to finish.
exercises.beginnerModification: Split it up: do sets of cleans, then sets of presses.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains a hip-driven pull and an overhead press in one repeatable rep.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Snatch
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, upper back, shoulders, grip
instructions: Hinge with a slight knee bend and swing the bell back until the forearm meets the inner thigh.
Extend the hips and legs hard with the arm still straight.
Shrug and pull the bell close to the body, and near head height punch the hand through the handle.
Finish with the arm locked overhead and the bell resting softly on the forearm, hips and knees straight.
exercises.formCue: Hips first, then punch through.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the arm early, letting the bell swing wide, and catching with a bent elbow.
exercises.beginnerModification: Build it from deadlifts, swings and the clean and press before snatching.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It takes a load from low to overhead in one move, building power and conditioning.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Overhead Press
instructions: Stand hip width apart with the bell racked at the shoulder, resting on the forearm, elbow near the ribs.
Brace the trunk and squeeze the handle.
Press the arm straight overhead.
Pull the elbow back down to the ribs to return to the rack.
exercises.formCue: Straight wrist, elbow under the bell.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the wrist bend back and leaning away from the bell.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter bell, or press from a half-kneeling position.
exercises.whyThisMatters: One-arm pressing builds shoulder strength while the trunk resists the offset load.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Bottoms-Up Press
instructions: Hold a light bell upside down by the handle at shoulder height, base pointing at the ceiling.
Stand with the same-side foot slightly forward and crush the handle.
Press the arm straight overhead while keeping the bell balanced.
Pull the elbow back to the ribs under control.
exercises.formCue: Crush the handle, move slowly.
exercises.commonMistakes: Going too heavy and letting the bell tip onto the forearm.
