exercises.beginnerModification: Just hold the bottoms-up position at shoulder height, or walk with it.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The unstable bell forces a strong grip and a straight, stacked pressing path.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Push Press
instructions: Bring two bells to the shoulders with the elbows close to the ribs and the wrists firm.
Stand tall with the feet shoulder width apart.
Dip a little at the knees and hips, then drive hard through the floor.
Use that drive to punch both arms straight overhead, then pull the elbows down to the rack.
exercises.formCue: Short dip, fast drive.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dipping forward onto the toes and pressing before the legs finish.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use one bell at a time, or a strict press with lighter bells.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Leg drive lets you move more weight overhead than a strict press.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Jerk
instructions: Rack two bells at the shoulders with the elbows close to the ribs and the wrists firm.
Dip slightly at the knees and hips with a tall back.
Drive up hard, then split the feet front and back as you punch both arms straight.
Stand up with the feet back under the hips, then pull the elbows down to the rack.
exercises.formCue: Drive up, drop under, lock out.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pressing the bells out slowly instead of getting under them, and a short unstable split.
exercises.beginnerModification: Learn the double push press first and practise the footwork with no weight.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains power and timing by getting the body under a heavy overhead load.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Swing
instructions: Stand shoulder width apart and hold the bell in one hand, palm down, with a firm grip.
Keep the back flat and sink into the hips to send the bell back between the legs.
Snap the hips forward to float the bell to about chest height, letting the free arm move with it.
Let the bell fall back between the legs and hinge again.
exercises.formCue: Hips throw it, the arm just guides.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting with the shoulder and letting the trunk twist toward the bell.
exercises.beginnerModification: Own the two-hand swing first, then use a lighter bell.
exercises.whyThisMatters: One hand on the bell adds grip work and makes the trunk resist rotation.

exercises.name: Kettlebell High Windmill
instructions: Stand with the feet wider than the shoulders and press one bell straight overhead.
Keep that arm vertical and your eyes on the bell.
Sink back into the hip under the bell and let the free hand slide down the inside of the opposite leg.
Push the hips forward to stand tall again with the arm still locked.
exercises.formCue: Hip back, eyes on the bell.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending sideways through the spine instead of hinging, and a soft overhead elbow.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with the low windmill or use no weight.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds shoulder stability overhead while the hips and trunk move underneath.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Low Windmill
instructions: Stand with the feet wider than the shoulders, bell hanging in one hand in front of the thigh.
Reach the other arm straight overhead and look at that hand.
Sink back into the hips and lower the bell down the inside of the leg.
Drive through the legs and push the hips forward to stand.
exercises.formCue: Sit into the hip, top arm stays vertical.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the back to reach lower.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it with no weight and a shorter range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the windmill hinge with the load held low, where it is easier to control.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Front Squat
instructions: Clean two bells to the rack in front of the shoulders and set the feet in your squat stance.
Brace and keep the elbows in and the chest tall.
Bend the knees and hips and lower until the thighs are just past parallel.
Drive up to full hip and knee extension.
exercises.formCue: Tall chest, bells stay close.
exercises.commonMistakes: Elbows flaring so the bells pull you forward, and the upper back rounding.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use one bell held as a goblet squat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The front-loaded bells train the legs and demand a strong, upright trunk.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Figure Eight
instructions: Stand wider than shoulder width and sit into a squat with a flat back, bell in one hand.
Pass the bell between the legs from front to back into the other hand.
Bring it around the outside of that leg to the front.
Pass it back through to the first hand and keep tracing the eight.
exercises.formCue: Stay low, back flat.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the back and standing up between passes.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light bell and move slowly.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds grip, coordination and trunk control while the legs hold a squat.

exercises.name: Half Turkish Get-Up
instructions: Lie on your back with the bell pressed above one shoulder, that knee bent and the other leg out at an angle.
Keep your eyes on the bell and roll up onto the opposite elbow, then onto the hand.
Push through the planted foot to lift the hips off the floor.
Pause, then reverse each step back to the floor.
exercises.formCue: Eyes on the bell, arm vertical.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rushing the steps and letting the overhead arm drift.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise with no weight, or balance a shoe on the fist.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the first half of the get-up, where shoulder stability and trunk strength are learned.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Pull-Over Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent and feet flat, holding the bell by the sides of the handle past your head.
With the arms long, pull the bell over until it is above the chest.
Crunch up, lifting the shoulder blades off the floor.
Lower the back down, then return the bell overhead.
exercises.formCue: Ribs down as the bell goes back.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching the lower back when the bell is overhead.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light bell, or do the pull-over without the crunch.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the abs and lats together and teaches rib control with the arms overhead.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Single-Arm Overhead Squat
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, shoulders, upper back, core
instructions: Press one bell overhead and lock the arm, feet about shoulder width apart.
Keep your eyes on the bell.
Push the hips back and squat, letting the free arm reach toward the floor as the trunk turns slightly toward the bell side.
Drive through both feet to stand with the arm still locked.
exercises.formCue: Locked arm, eyes up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the overhead arm bend or drift forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use no weight, or squat with the bell in the rack.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It tests shoulder stability, hip mobility and trunk control together.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, mid back, rear delts, biceps
exercises.equipment: Kettlebell and a chair or bench
instructions: Stand in a split stance with the bell by the back foot and the free hand on a chair or bench.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and grip the bell.
Pull the elbow up and back, keeping it close to the ribs and the chest still.
Lower the bell under control until the arm is straight.
exercises.formCue: Elbow to the hip, chest still.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the back and yanking the bell with a twist of the trunk.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter bell and a higher support.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the back one side at a time and shows up left-right differences.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, mid back, rear delts, lower back, hamstrings
instructions: Stand hip width apart with two bells between the feet.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and soft knees, and grip both handles.
Hold the hinge and pull both elbows back.
Lower the bells with control without standing up.
exercises.formCue: Hold the hinge, row to the hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the back and bouncing the torso to move the weight.
exercises.beginnerModification: Row one bell at a time with a hand on a support.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the upper back while the hips and lower back hold a hinge.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Suitcase Deadlift
instructions: Stand shoulder width apart with the bell on the floor outside one foot.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back, bend the knees and grip the handle.
Push through the feet and stand tall without leaning toward or away from the bell.
Hinge back down the same way and set the bell on the floor.
exercises.formCue: Shoulders level, stand tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning to the side as you lift.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise the bell on a low step to shorten the reach.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The one-sided load makes the trunk work to keep you upright while you hinge.

exercises.name: American Kettlebell Swing
instructions: Set up as for a two-hand swing and hike the bell back between the legs.
Drive the hips and legs so their force carries the bell upward.
Let the bell travel all the way overhead with the arms straight and the trunk held rigid.
Guide it back down the same path into the next hinge.
exercises.formCue: Hips drive, midline stays tight.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching the lower back at the top and pulling with the arms.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the chest-height swing until the overhead position is comfortable.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The longer path means more work per rep than the chest-height swing.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Clean
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, upper back
instructions: Squat down to dumbbells beside the ankles, palms facing in, shoulders over the weights and back tight.
Stand by extending the hips and knees, keeping the dumbbells close.
As they pass the knees, finish the leg drive and shrug hard.
Pull the elbows under and catch the dumbbells at the shoulders with the knees slightly bent, then stand.
exercises.formCue: Legs first, then elbows through.
exercises.commonMistakes: Curling the weights up with the arms and letting them drift away from the body.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start from the hang with the dumbbells at mid-thigh.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains fast hip and leg extension with simple equipment.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand tall with the dumbbells in front of the thighs, knees slightly bent and back straight.
Push the hips back and slide the weights down close to the legs.
Stop when you feel a strong stretch in the back of the legs and the back is still flat.
Push through the heels and bring the hips forward to stand.
exercises.formCue: Hips back, weights close.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the back to reach lower and turning it into a squat.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the range or use lighter dumbbells.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the hamstrings and glutes and grooves a clean hip hinge.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Split Squat
instructions: Stand in a long split stance with a dumbbell in each hand at the sides.
Lower by bending the front knee and hip, letting the back heel rise.
Stop when the back knee is just above the floor.
Push through the front foot to stand, and finish all reps before switching legs.
exercises.formCue: Straight down, straight up.
exercises.commonMistakes: A stance that is too short and the front knee caving in.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it with no weight and hold a support for balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It loads one leg at a time with a stable base, good for strength and balance.

exercises.name: Renegade Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, mid back, core, shoulders, triceps
instructions: Take a push-up position with each hand on a dumbbell under the shoulder and the feet about shoulder width apart.
Press into both dumbbells and keep the body straight.
Row one dumbbell toward the chest with the elbow close to the ribs while the feet press into the floor.
Lower it slowly, then row the other side.
exercises.formCue: Hips square to the floor.
exercises.commonMistakes: Hips rotating open on each row and the lower back sagging.
exercises.beginnerModification: Widen the feet, drop to the knees, or use lighter dumbbells.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the back and the trunk at once by making you resist rotation.

exercises.name: Man-Maker
exercises.musclesWorked: Chest, back, shoulders, quads, glutes, core
instructions: Start in a high plank gripping two dumbbells, feet hip width or wider, and do one push-up.
Row one dumbbell, then the other, without rocking the hips.
Step or jump the feet up to a squat stance and clean the dumbbells to the shoulders.
Squat, stand and press overhead, then lower the weights to the floor and return to the plank.
exercises.formCue: Smooth, not rushed.
exercises.commonMistakes: Twisting during the rows and losing the back position when picking the weights up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use light dumbbells, step instead of jumping, or drop the push-up.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strings a push, a pull, a squat and a press into one demanding conditioning rep.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
instructions: Sit on the floor with the dumbbells in the hip crease, then lie back and bring them to the chest.
Press them to straight arms and set the feet flat with the knees bent.
Lower slowly until the upper arms rest lightly on the floor.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.formCue: Soft touch on the floor, then press.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping the elbows onto the floor and bouncing out of the bottom.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use lighter dumbbells or press one arm at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It lets you press without a bench, and the floor limits how far the shoulders travel.

exercises.name: Arnold Z Press
instructions: Sit on the floor with the legs straight out and the torso upright.
Hold the dumbbells at shoulder height with the palms facing you.
Press overhead while turning the palms to face forward, and lock out fully.
Lower under control, turning the palms back toward you.
exercises.formCue: Sit tall, no leaning back.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning back as the weights go up and rounding the lower back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Sit on a low pad, bend the knees slightly, or use lighter dumbbells.
exercises.whyThisMatters: With no back support and no leg drive, the shoulders and trunk do all the work.

exercises.name: Zottman Curl
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight and palms facing forward.
Curl the weights up with the palms up and the elbows at your sides.
At the top, turn the palms to face down.
Lower slowly with the palms down, then turn them forward again at the bottom.
exercises.formCue: Palms up to lift, palms down to lower.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swinging the weights and rushing the lowering half.
exercises.beginnerModification: Go lighter, or curl one arm at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the biceps on the way up and the forearms on the way down.

exercises.name: Snatch
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, shoulders, upper back
instructions: Set the feet about hip width with toes turned out, take a wide grip, and start with the bar over the balls of the feet and the shoulders above the bar.
Push through the whole foot and keep the same back angle until the bar passes the knees.
Extend the hips and legs hard while the bar stays close to the body.
Pull the elbows up and out, move the feet to your squat stance, and drop under the bar.
Lock the bar overhead in a full squat, then stand up under control.
exercises.formCue: Bar close, finish tall, punch up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the arms early, or letting the bar swing away from the body.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with a dowel or empty bar and learn the power snatch from the hang first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the first competition lift and trains speed, power, and mobility in one movement.

exercises.name: Power Snatch
instructions: Set up as for the snatch with a wide grip, the bar over the balls of the feet, and the shoulders above the bar.
Push through the whole foot and hold your back angle until the bar passes the knees.
Extend the hips hard with the bar close, then pull the elbows up and out.
Move the feet out and receive the bar locked out overhead in a partial squat with the thighs above parallel.
Stand up under control.
exercises.formCue: Finish the pull, then punch and stop high.
exercises.commonMistakes: Cutting the leg drive short to rush under the bar, or pressing the bar out with soft elbows.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a dowel or empty bar from the hang at mid-thigh.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Catching high demands a strong, fast pull and is easier to learn than the full snatch.

exercises.name: Hang Snatch
instructions: Deadlift the bar to standing with a snatch grip.
Lower it under control to the hang position you are training, balanced over the whole foot.
Push through the floor, then extend the hips hard with the bar close to the body.
Pull the elbows up and out, move the feet, and drop into a full squat under the bar.
Lock the bar overhead firmly and stand.
exercises.formCue: Shoulders over the bar, then finish tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swinging the bar out from the hips, or pulling with the arms before the legs finish.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the hang power snatch with an empty bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Starting from the hang isolates the final extension and the pull under the bar.

exercises.name: Hang Power Snatch
instructions: Deadlift the bar to standing with a snatch grip.
Lower it under control to the hang position, with the shoulders over the bar.
Push through the floor and extend the hips hard.
Pull the elbows up and out and receive the bar locked out overhead above a parallel squat.
Stand up and lower the bar under control.
exercises.formCue: Legs first, arms last.
exercises.commonMistakes: Using the arms to lift the bar, or catching with bent elbows.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practice with a dowel, starting from mid-thigh.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the simplest way to learn the snatch extension and overhead catch.

exercises.name: Muscle Snatch
instructions: Start as for the snatch and push through the whole foot until the bar is above the knees.
Extend the hips with the bar close, then shrug and pull the elbows up and out.
Keep the legs straight and turn the bar over as the elbows reach shoulder height.
Punch straight up to lockout with the bar over the back of the neck.
exercises.formCue: Elbows high, then turn it over and punch.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping the elbows before the turnover, or bending the knees again to get under the bar.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a dowel or empty bar and start from the hang.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches and strengthens the upper-body turnover of the snatch.

exercises.name: Tall Snatch
instructions: Stand tall with a snatch grip, the bar at arm's length, and the feet in your pulling stance.
Lift the feet and pull the elbows up and out at the same moment.
Turn the bar over and punch up as you drop into a squat, aiming to lock out as the feet land.
Hold the bottom with the bar secure overhead, then stand.
exercises.formCue: Pull yourself down, fast.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dipping the knees or leaning to get the bar moving first, or pressing the bar out slowly.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a PVC pipe and receive in a partial squat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It isolates the pull under the bar and builds speed and confidence in the catch.

exercises.name: Block Snatch
instructions: Set the bar on blocks and take the same position you would pass through in a snatch at that height.
Balance over the whole foot, then push hard with the legs with the bar close.
Extend the hips fully once the bar passes the knees.
Pull the elbows up and out, move the feet, and receive the bar overhead in a squat.
Stand, then return the bar to the blocks.
exercises.formCue: Set your position, then go.
exercises.commonMistakes: Starting with the shoulders behind the bar, or rushing the pull because there is no run-up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the hang snatch from the same height with a lighter load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: With no stretch or momentum to help, it builds a fast, strong start from a fixed position.

exercises.name: Snatch Pull
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, quads, traps, upper back
instructions: Set the snatch start position with the heels about hip width, the bar over the balls of the feet, and the shoulders above the bar.
Push through the whole foot and keep the bar close to the legs past the knees.
Open the hips and drive up with the legs as hard as you can.
Shrug and let the elbows bend slightly to keep the bar against the body, then return it to the floor.
exercises.formCue: Legs all the way, bar against the body.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling with the arms early, or letting the bar drift away from the body at the top.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with the snatch deadlift to learn the positions at slow speed.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the strength and timing of the snatch extension with loads at or above the full lift.

exercises.name: Snatch High Pull
exercises.musclesWorked: Traps, upper back, shoulders, glutes, hamstrings
instructions: Set the snatch start position and push with the legs through the whole foot.
Keep the bar close until mid-thigh, then open the hips and drive up hard.
After the legs finish, shrug and pull the elbows up and out with the bar against the body.
Stay tall with the trunk vertical at the top, then lower the bar.
exercises.formCue: Elbows up and out, stay tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning forward to meet the bar, or pulling with the arms before the legs finish.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light bar from the hang at mid-thigh.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It links the leg drive to the arm action that starts the pull under the bar.

exercises.name: Snatch Deadlift
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, quads, upper back, grip
instructions: Take a snatch-width grip with the heels about hip width, the bar over the balls of the feet, and the shoulders above the bar.
Set the back flat and push through the whole foot.
Keep the bar close and hold the same back angle until the bar reaches the thigh.
Extend the hips to stand tall, then lower the bar.
exercises.formCue: Same back angle to the knees.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hips rise faster than the shoulders, or losing the flat upper back with the wide grip.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use straps and a lighter load, or pull from low blocks.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds strength and posture in the exact positions of the snatch pull.

exercises.name: Overhead Squat
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, shoulders, upper back, trunk
instructions: Hold the bar overhead with a snatch grip, elbows locked, shoulder blades squeezed together, and the bar over the base of the neck.
Set the feet in your squat stance and brace the trunk.
Squat to full depth at a controlled speed, balanced over the whole foot.
Keep pushing up into the bar as you stand.
exercises.formCue: Push up on the bar the whole time.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the bar drift forward of the base of the neck, or the elbows softening at the bottom.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the PVC overhead squat and only go as deep as you can hold the bar in place.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the strength, balance, and mobility needed to receive a snatch.

exercises.name: PVC Overhead Squat
instructions: Hold a PVC pipe overhead with a wide grip and locked elbows, over the base of the neck.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together and set your squat stance.
Squat slowly as deep as you can while the pipe stays in place and the weight stays over the whole foot.
Push up into the pipe and stand.
exercises.formCue: Reach up into the pipe as you sit.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the pipe drift forward, or rising onto the toes.
exercises.beginnerModification: Squat to a box, or widen the grip until the position holds.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Daily practice with no load is the simplest way to build the snatch receiving position.

exercises.name: Snatch Balance
instructions: Stand with the bar behind the neck, a snatch grip, the shoulder blades set tight, and the feet in your pulling stance.
Dip at the knees with the trunk upright and drive up just enough to unweight the bar.
Punch the arms up hard as you move the feet out and drop into an overhead squat.
Hold the bottom until the bar is steady, then stand.
exercises.formCue: Punch under, do not push the bar up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Driving the bar high and pressing it out, instead of moving fast under it.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the pressing snatch balance with an empty bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds speed, timing, and confidence for the catch of the snatch.

exercises.name: Pressing Snatch Balance
instructions: Stand with the bar behind the neck, a snatch grip, and the feet in your squat stance.
Start pressing the bar and squatting down at the same time, at a controlled speed.
Time it so the elbows lock just as you reach the bottom of the squat.
Make sure the bar is steady overhead, then stand.
exercises.formCue: Press yourself down under the bar.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pressing the bar up first and then squatting, or stopping short of full depth.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a PVC pipe and squat only as deep as you can keep the bar over the base of the neck.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the receiving position and overhead mobility at slow speed.

exercises.name: Snatch Push Press
instructions: Stand with the bar behind the neck, a snatch grip, and the shoulder blades set tight.
Dip at the knees with the trunk upright and drive hard through the floor.
As the bar leaves the shoulders, press fast into a firm lockout.
Hold a moment overhead, then lower the bar to the shoulders and reset.
exercises.formCue: Dip straight, drive, lock it hard.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning forward in the dip, or finishing with soft elbows.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use an empty bar or PVC pipe.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the overhead strength and stability that holds a snatch in place.

exercises.name: Press in Snatch
instructions: With a snatch grip and the bar behind the neck, sit into the bottom of a squat.
Press the bar to full lockout without any help from the legs.
Keep the shoulder blades squeezed and the chest up while the bar is overhead.
Lower the bar under control to the upper back and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Stay down, chest up, press.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rising out of the squat to help the press, or letting the bar drop onto the neck.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a PVC pipe, or do the pressing snatch balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds mobility, stability, and strength in the snatch receiving position.

exercises.name: PVC Pass-Through
instructions: Hold a PVC pipe in front of the hips with a wide overhand grip and straight arms.
Raise the pipe in a wide arc up and over the head without bending the elbows.
Continue the arc until the pipe rests behind the hips, then bring it back the same way.
Narrow the grip a little at a time only while the movement stays smooth and comfortable.
exercises.formCue: Arms long, slow arc.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the elbows to get through, or forcing a grip that is too narrow.
exercises.beginnerModification: Take a wider grip, or use a band so the hands can move apart.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It warms up the shoulders for the snatch and every overhead position.

exercises.name: Clean
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, upper back
instructions: Set the feet about hip width with toes turned out, grip just outside the legs, and start with the bar over the balls of the feet.
Push through the whole foot and hold your back angle until the bar passes the knees.
Extend the hips hard with the bar close, brushing the upper thigh.
Pull the elbows up, move the feet out, and whip the elbows around to rack the bar on the shoulders in a full squat.
Drive straight up out of the squat and stand.
exercises.formCue: Bar close, fast elbows.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the bar crash onto the shoulders with slow elbows, or jumping forward to chase a bar that swung out.
exercises.beginnerModification: Learn the hang power clean first, then add the front squat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the first half of the clean and jerk and builds total-body power.

exercises.name: Power Clean
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, quads, traps, upper back
instructions: Set up with the feet about hip width, the bar over the balls of the feet, the shoulders above the bar, and the back flat.
Push through the whole foot and hold your back angle until the bar passes the knees.
Extend the hips hard with the bar close to the body.
Pull the elbows up, move the feet out, and whip the elbows around to rack the bar with the thighs above parallel.
Stand up fully.
exercises.formCue: Finish the legs, then fast elbows.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling with the arms early, or catching with the elbows low and the bar in the hands.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the hang power clean with an empty bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the most widely used lift for building power from the floor.

exercises.name: Hang Clean
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, quads, traps, upper back
instructions: Deadlift the bar to standing with a clean grip.
Lower it under control to the hang position you are training, balanced over the whole foot.
Push with the legs, then extend the hips hard with the bar close.
Pull the elbows up, move the feet, and rack the bar on the shoulders as you sit into a full squat.
Drive up out of the bottom right away and stand.
exercises.formCue: Extend, then pull under and sit.
exercises.commonMistakes: Catching high and then riding the bar down, instead of pulling under into the squat.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the hang power clean followed by a separate front squat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Starting from the hang trains the final extension and a fast pull under the bar.

exercises.name: Muscle Clean
instructions: Start as for the clean and push through the whole foot until the bar is above the knees.
Extend the hips with the bar close to the body.
Keep the legs straight and pushing into the floor as you shrug and pull the elbows up and out.
Bring the elbows around and set the bar smoothly on the shoulders without bending the knees again.
exercises.formCue: Elbows high, then around.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dipping under the bar, or letting the bar loop away from the body.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use an empty bar from the hang.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the arm path of the clean turnover and strengthens it.

exercises.name: Tall Clean
instructions: Stand tall with a clean grip, the bar at arm's length, and the feet in your pulling stance.
Lift the feet and pull the elbows up and out at the same moment.
Bring the elbows around fast and rack the bar as you drop into a squat.
Sit into the bottom smoothly, then stand right away.
exercises.formCue: Pull down and whip the elbows.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dipping or swinging the bar to start it moving, or receiving with the elbows low.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use an empty bar and receive in a partial squat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It isolates the pull under the bar and builds a quick, precise turnover.

exercises.name: Block Clean
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, quads, traps, upper back
instructions: Set the bar on blocks and take the same position you would pass through in a clean at that height.
Push through the floor and hold your back angle until the bar passes the knees.
Extend the hips hard with the bar close, brushing the upper thigh.
Pull the elbows high, move into your squat stance, and whip the elbows around to rack the bar.
Drive up out of the squat, then return the bar to the blocks.
exercises.formCue: Tight start, full finish.
exercises.commonMistakes: Starting loose because the bar is already raised, or cutting the extension short.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the hang clean from the same height with a lighter load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: With no momentum from the floor, it builds speed and force in the top of the pull.

exercises.name: Clean Pull
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, quads, traps, spinal erectors
instructions: Set the clean start position with the heels about hip width, the bar over the balls of the feet, the shoulders above the bar, and the back flat.
Push through the whole foot and keep the bar close with the same back angle past the knees.
At mid-thigh, open the hips and drive up as hard as you can.
Shrug with slightly bent elbows to keep the bar tight to the body, then return to flat feet as the bar comes down.
exercises.formCue: Push the floor, finish tall, shrug.
exercises.commonMistakes: Yanking the bar off the floor, or bending the arms before the legs have finished.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with the clean deadlift to learn the positions slowly.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds pulling strength and timing for the clean with loads at or above the full lift.

exercises.name: Clean Deadlift
instructions: Set the clean start position with the heels about hip width, the bar over the balls of the feet, and the shoulders above the bar.
Push through the whole foot with the chest up and the bar close to the legs.
Hold the same back angle until the bar passes the knees.
Extend the hips and legs to stand tall, then lower the bar under control.
exercises.formCue: Chest up, knees back, bar close.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hips shoot up first, or pulling it like a powerlifting deadlift with the shoulders behind the bar.
exercises.beginnerModification: Pull from low blocks with a light load until the start position is comfortable.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the exact posture and bar path of the first part of the clean.

exercises.name: Clean and Jerk
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, shoulders, triceps
instructions: Clean the bar from the floor to the shoulders and stand up fully.
Reset the grip and breath, with the bar resting on the shoulders and the trunk upright.
Dip by bending only the knees, a short distance, then drive straight up hard.
Punch the bar overhead as the feet move into a split and the elbows lock.
Hold the bar steady, bring the feet back in line, and then lower it.
exercises.formCue: Stand tall, reset, then dip and drive straight.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rushing the jerk before the clean is settled, or dipping forward onto the toes.
exercises.beginnerModification: Train the power clean and push press as separate lifts first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the second competition lift and puts the most weight overhead of any movement.

exercises.name: Split Jerk
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, shoulders, triceps, upper back
instructions: Stand with the heels about hip width and the bar racked on the shoulders, elbows down and slightly in front of the bar.
Dip by bending only the knees with the trunk vertical, a short distance, and brake hard.
Drive straight up with the legs and push the bar up and slightly back.
Move the feet quickly into a split as you punch the elbows to lockout.
Hold the bar steady, then step the front foot back and the rear foot in.
exercises.formCue: Dip straight, drive, punch and split.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dipping forward so the bar goes out front, or a short, narrow split that leaves no base.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practice the footwork with a PVC pipe, then use the jerk balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The split gives the widest base for receiving heavy weights overhead.

exercises.name: Push Jerk
instructions: Rack the bar between the throat and the top of the shoulders, with the elbows slightly in front of the bar.
Dip by bending only the knees with the trunk vertical, then drive up hard.
As the legs finish, push the bar up and slightly back and punch the elbows to lockout.
Bend the knees again to receive the bar in a partial squat with the feet staying on the floor, then stand.
exercises.formCue: Drive, then push yourself under.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pressing the bar out slowly instead of dropping under it, or dipping with the chest forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the push press until the dip and drive are consistent.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Feet that stay planted teach a balanced, complete leg drive.

exercises.name: Power Jerk
instructions: Stand with the heels about hip width and the bar racked on the shoulders, elbows down and slightly forward.
Dip by bending only the knees with the trunk vertical, and brake hard.
Drive up hard with the legs and push the bar overhead.
Move the feet quickly out to your squat stance and punch the elbows to lockout in a partial squat.
Steady the bar, then stand.
exercises.formCue: Straight dip, hard drive, fast feet.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jumping forward or back, or catching with soft elbows.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the push jerk, where the feet stay on the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It demands a high, straight drive and is a simple way to train the jerk.

exercises.name: Jerk Dip Squat
instructions: Stand in your jerk stance with the bar in the jerk rack position and brace as you would for a jerk.
Dip by bending the knees at a controlled speed with the trunk upright.
Keep tension in the legs and stay balanced over the whole foot.
Change direction smoothly and stand back up without an explosive drive.
exercises.formCue: Straight down, straight up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the chest tip forward, or the weight shifting to the toes.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use an empty bar and hold a short pause at the bottom of the dip.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the dip position so the bar travels straight in the jerk.

exercises.name: Jerk Balance
exercises.equipment: Barbell or PVC pipe, squat rack
instructions: Rack the bar on the shoulders and stand in a short split, about one foot-length shorter than your full split.
Balance the weight evenly between both feet.
Dip straight down and drive straight up.
Step the front foot forward into the full split as you punch the bar to lockout, keeping the trunk upright.
Steady the bar, then recover the feet.
exercises.formCue: Step through, do not dive the chest.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning the chest forward, or putting most of the weight on the front leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a PVC pipe or empty bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches you to move under the bar into a balanced split.

exercises.name: Rolling Like a Ball
instructions: Sit near the front of the mat, hug your shins, and open your knees to shoulder width.
Round your spine, tuck your chin toward your chest, and lift your feet to balance behind your sitting bones.
Breathe in and roll back as far as your shoulder blades, keeping the same round shape.
Breathe out and roll up to the balance without letting your feet touch the floor.
exercises.formCue: Stay a ball: heels close, chin tucked.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rolling onto the neck or head, and throwing the legs or head to get back up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold behind the thighs with a looser shape, or just practise the balance without rolling.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the abdominals to hold a rounded spine and control momentum.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back, hug both knees in, and curl your head and shoulders off the mat.
Keep one knee in and reach the other leg out to about 45 degrees.
Place the outside hand on the ankle and the inside hand on the knee of the bent leg.
Switch legs smoothly, drawing each knee in as the other leg reaches long.
Keep your lower back on the mat and your trunk still for the whole set.
exercises.formCue: Trunk still, legs trade places.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rocking the torso side to side, or letting the head drop and the neck take the strain.
exercises.beginnerModification: Reach the straight leg higher toward the ceiling, or rest your head on the mat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the trunk to stay stable while the legs move.

exercises.name: Double-Leg Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back, hug both knees to your chest, and curl your head and shoulders up.
Breathe in and reach your arms back by your ears and both legs out on a high diagonal.
Keep your lower back on the mat and your head and shoulders lifted.
Breathe out, circle your arms around, and hug your knees back in.
Repeat without lowering your head between reps.
exercises.formCue: Reach long, hug tight, back stays down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch as the legs reach, or dropping the head back with the arms.
exercises.beginnerModification: Reach the legs straight up instead of out, or move only the arms and then only the legs.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the abdominal strength to hold the trunk steady against long levers.

exercises.name: Single Straight-Leg Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back, curl your head and shoulders up, and reach both legs toward the ceiling.
Hold behind the calf or thigh of one leg and lower the other leg toward the mat.
Draw the top leg toward you with two small pulses.
Switch legs in a scissor action, keeping both knees as straight as you can.
Keep your elbows wide and your trunk still throughout.
exercises.formCue: Legs scissor, trunk does not rock.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing the torso with each pulse, or rounding the shoulders forward to reach the leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold behind the thigh, soften the knees, and keep the lower leg higher off the mat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the abdominals while giving the hamstrings an active stretch.

exercises.name: Double Straight-Leg Stretch
exercises.musclesWorked: Lower abdominals, hip flexors, inner thighs
instructions: Lie on your back with hands layered behind your head, elbows wide, and head and shoulders curled up.
Reach both legs straight up and squeeze them together.
Lower both legs only as far as your lower back stays on the mat.
Lift the legs back to vertical with a little more emphasis on the way up.
Keep your chest lifted and neck relaxed for every rep.
exercises.formCue: Lower slow, lift with intent, back stays down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch off the mat, or losing the shoulder lift as the legs lower.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bend the knees slightly, lower only a short way, and place your hands under your hips.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It loads the lower abdominals hard while the trunk learns to resist arching.

exercises.name: Criss-Cross
instructions: Lie on your back with hands behind your head, elbows wide, and knees bent over your hips.
Curl your head and shoulders up and reach one leg out on a diagonal.
Rotate your ribcage toward the bent knee, lifting the back of the opposite shoulder off the mat.
Hold the twist for a beat, then switch sides as you change legs.
Keep your hips still and your elbows open the whole time.
exercises.formCue: Twist the ribs, not the elbows.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling on the neck and flapping the elbows instead of rotating the trunk, or rocking the hips.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep both feet on the floor with knees bent and twist the upper body only.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds rotational strength in the obliques with the pelvis held steady.

exercises.name: Spine Stretch Forward
instructions: Sit tall with legs straight, a little wider than your hips, and feet flexed.
Reach your arms forward at shoulder height.
Breathe out, nod your chin, and round forward one segment at a time while pulling your stomach back.
Reach forward as if curving over a big ball, keeping your hips where they are.
Breathe in and stack your spine back up to tall sitting.
exercises.formCue: Round up and over, belly pulls back.
exercises.commonMistakes: Starting slumped, or hinging flat from the hips instead of rounding the spine.
exercises.beginnerModification: Sit on a folded blanket or bend your knees so you can start upright.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the spine to move one segment at a time and stretches the back of the body.

exercises.name: Open-Leg Rocker
exercises.musclesWorked: Abdominals, hip flexors, hamstrings, spinal erectors
instructions: Sit just behind your sitting bones, hold your ankles, and straighten your legs into a V at shoulder width.
Keep your lower back gently rounded and your chest lifted.
Tilt your pelvis under to start rolling back and roll only as far as your shoulder blades.
Roll back up using your abdominals and pause in the balance.
Keep your arms straight and the shape the same in both directions.
exercises.formCue: The pelvis starts the roll, not the head.
exercises.commonMistakes: Throwing the head back to start, or rolling onto the neck.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold behind your calves or thighs with bent knees, or just hold the V balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It combines balance, hamstring length, and abdominal control in one rolling movement.

exercises.name: Corkscrew
exercises.musclesWorked: Abdominals, obliques, hip flexors, inner thighs
instructions: Lie on your back with arms long by your sides, palms pressing down, and both legs straight up and squeezed together.
Keep your whole spine on the mat and your shoulders wide.
Circle both legs as one: over to one side, down and around, and up the other side.
Pause at the top, then reverse the circle.
Keep the circle small enough that your lower back and hips stay still.
exercises.formCue: Legs glued together, small circle, quiet hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Making the circle so big that the lower back arches or the hips roll off the mat.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bend the knees a little, make a plate-sized circle, and put your hands under your hips.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the trunk to stay anchored while the legs move through rotation.

exercises.name: Saw
exercises.musclesWorked: Obliques, spinal erectors, hamstrings, upper back
instructions: Sit tall with legs straight and a little wider than the mat, feet flexed, and arms out to the sides.
Rotate your trunk to one side while both sitting bones stay down.
Reach the front hand toward the outside of the opposite foot as the back arm reaches behind you.
Round forward over the leg and breathe out fully.
Roll up, untwist to the centre, and repeat to the other side.
exercises.formCue: Both hips stay heavy as you twist and reach.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the opposite hip lift or slide forward, or collapsing the chest instead of rotating.
exercises.beginnerModification: Sit on a folded blanket and bend the knees slightly.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It pairs spinal rotation with a hamstring stretch and trains a full breath out.

exercises.name: Swan Prep
exercises.musclesWorked: Spinal erectors, glutes, upper back, triceps
instructions: Lie face down with hands under your shoulders, elbows close to your sides, and legs together.
Lift your stomach lightly off the mat and press your hip bones down.
Lift your head and chest using your upper back, with only light pressure in the hands.
Press into your hands to rise a little higher while your neck stays long.
Lower slowly, lengthening forward as you go.
exercises.formCue: Chest reaches forward and up, belly lifted.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pushing up with the arms and hinging in the lower back, or throwing the head back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep your forearms on the mat and lift only a few centimetres.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds upper-back extension strength to balance all the forward-rounding work.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Kick
instructions: Lie face down and prop yourself on your forearms with elbows under your shoulders.
Press your elbows down, lift your chest, and pull your stomach up off the mat.
Kick one heel toward your seat with two quick pulses.
Straighten that leg to the mat and kick the other heel.
Keep your hips and trunk completely still as the legs alternate.
exercises.formCue: Chest proud, hips pinned, heel to seat.
exercises.commonMistakes: Sinking between the shoulders, or letting the hips rock with each kick.
exercises.beginnerModification: Rest your forehead on stacked hands and kick once per side.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the hamstrings and upper back while opening the front of the thighs.

exercises.name: Double-Leg Kick
exercises.musclesWorked: Spinal erectors, glutes, hamstrings, rear shoulders
instructions: Lie face down with one cheek on the mat and hands clasped high on your back, elbows relaxed down.
Kick both heels toward your seat three times.
Straighten your legs to the mat as you reach your clasped hands toward your heels and lift your chest.
Keep your stomach lifted and your neck long at the top.
Lower, turn your head to the other cheek, and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Reach the hands to the heels and let the chest follow.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the stomach sag so the lower back pinches, or craning the neck up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the hands by your hips instead of clasped, and lift the chest only slightly.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It opens the chest and shoulders while strengthening the whole back line.

exercises.name: Teaser
exercises.musclesWorked: Abdominals, hip flexors, quads, spinal erectors
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs together on a 45 degree diagonal and arms reaching overhead.
Bring your arms forward, lift your head, and roll up one segment at a time.
Finish in a V with your fingers reaching toward your toes and your chest open.
Hold for a breath with your legs still.
Roll down slowly through the lower back first, keeping the legs where they are.
exercises.formCue: Legs stay still, the spine does the moving.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jerking up with momentum, letting the legs drop, or hinging with a stiff arched back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use Teaser Prep with the knees bent and feet on the floor, or one leg extended.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the benchmark of Pilates control: strength, balance, and spinal articulation together.

exercises.name: Leg Pull Back
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, rear shoulders, triceps, core
instructions: Sit with legs straight and hands on the mat behind your hips, fingers pointing forward or out.
Press down through your hands and heels and lift your hips until your body is one straight line.
Keep your hips level and kick one straight leg up toward the ceiling.
Lower it with control and switch legs.
Finish the set, then lower your hips slowly to the mat.
exercises.formCue: Hips stay high and level as the leg lifts.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hips drop as the leg kicks, or sinking into the shoulders and wrists.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the reverse plank without the kicks, or bend the knees into a tabletop.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the back of the body and opens the chest and shoulders.

exercises.name: Seal
instructions: Sit with knees bent and open and heels together.
Thread your hands between your legs and hold the outsides of your ankles.
Lift your feet and balance just behind your sitting bones with a rounded spine.
Roll back to your shoulder blades, then roll up and find the balance again.
Add three small foot claps at the back and at the front once the roll is smooth.
exercises.formCue: Round and roll, pause in the balance.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rolling onto the neck, or using a kick of the legs to get back up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Leave out the claps and hold behind the thighs.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It loosens the back at the end of a mat session and keeps the balance sharp.

exercises.name: Pilates Side Bend
exercises.musclesWorked: Obliques, shoulders, outer hips, inner thighs
instructions: Sit on one hip with knees bent, top foot just in front of the bottom foot, and your bottom hand on the mat under your shoulder.
Press into your hand and feet and lift your hips as you straighten your legs.
Reach your top arm overhead so your body makes a long arc.
Keep the supporting shoulder away from your ear and your chest open.
Lower your hips with control to just above the mat and repeat before switching sides.
exercises.formCue: Push the floor away and lift from the underside of the waist.
exercises.commonMistakes: Sinking into the wrist and shoulder, or letting the top shoulder roll forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the bottom knee on the mat, or work from the forearm.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds side-body and shoulder strength with control through a full range.

exercises.name: Neck Pull
exercises.musclesWorked: Abdominals, hip flexors, spinal erectors, hamstrings
instructions: Lie on your back with legs straight and hip-width apart, feet flexed, and hands layered behind your head.
Keep your elbows wide, curl your head and chest up, and roll forward over your legs.
Stack your spine up to sit tall, pressing your head lightly back into your hands.
Lean back in one straight line as far as you can control.
Round your lower back and roll down to the mat one segment at a time.
exercises.formCue: Elbows wide, legs heavy, no tugging on the head.
exercises.commonMistakes: Yanking on the neck to get up, or letting the feet lift off the mat.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bend the knees slightly, or do a Roll-Up with the arms reaching forward.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is a harder Roll-Up that demands full abdominal control with no help from the arms.

exercises.name: Foam Roll Calves
instructions: Sit on the floor with the roller under one calf and your hands behind you.
Lift your hips slightly so your weight rests on the roller.
Roll slowly from just below the knee toward the ankle, pausing on tender spots.
Work for one to two minutes, then switch legs.
exercises.formCue: Slow and steady. Breathe on the tender spots.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rolling fast back and forth, or pressing so hard you tense up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep your hips on the floor and both feet relaxed to reduce the pressure.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A couple of minutes of slow rolling can ease the feeling of tight calves before or after training.

exercises.name: Foam Roll Quads
instructions: Lie face down on your forearms with the roller under the front of one thigh.
Keep your trunk braced so your lower back does not sag.
Roll slowly between the top of the knee and the hip crease.
Stop on a tender spot for 30 to 45 seconds, then move on and switch legs.
exercises.formCue: Firm but tolerable. Never sharp.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rolling over the kneecap, or holding your breath against the pressure.
exercises.beginnerModification: Roll both thighs at once to spread your weight.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is a simple way to ease stiff quads around training.

source.name: NASM, Foam Rolling and Self-Myofascial Release: The Trainer's Application Guide

exercises.name: Foam Roll Outer Thigh
instructions: Lie on your side with the roller under the outer thigh, just below the hip.
Cross the top leg over and place that foot on the floor to take some weight.
Roll slowly along the outer thigh, stopping above the knee.
Keep the pressure moderate, pause briefly on tender areas, then switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Use the top foot to take weight off.
exercises.commonMistakes: Grinding hard on the side of the knee or the hip bone.
exercises.beginnerModification: Put more weight through the supporting foot and hand, or use a softer roller.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Gentle work on the muscles of the outer thigh can make the hip and knee feel freer.

source.name: NASM, Foam Rolling and Self-Myofascial Release: The Trainer's Application Guide

exercises.name: Foam Roll Glutes
instructions: Sit on the roller with your hands on the floor behind you.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee and lean toward the hip of the crossed leg.
Roll slowly over the back of that hip to find a tender spot.
Hold there for 30 to 45 seconds while breathing normally, then switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Lean in, find the spot, breathe.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rolling quickly, or pressing into pain that shoots down the leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep both feet on the floor and do not cross the leg.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It gives the back of the hip some relief after long sitting or heavy leg work.

source.name: NASM, Foam Rolling and Self-Myofascial Release: The Trainer's Application Guide

exercises.name: Foam Roll Upper Back
exercises.musclesWorked: Thoracic spine muscles, rhomboids, mid traps
instructions: Lie on your back with the roller across your mid back, knees bent and feet flat.
Support your head with your hands and lift your hips slightly.
Use your feet to roll slowly between the bottom of the shoulder blades and the top of the shoulders.
Pause at a stiff segment and gently ease back over the roller as you breathe out.
exercises.formCue: Ribs down, roll the upper back only.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rolling onto the lower back or neck, or flaring the ribs to force the arch.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep your hips on the floor and just lean back over the roller without rolling.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is a useful reset for an upper back that has been bent over a desk.

source.name: NASM, Foam Rolling and Self-Myofascial Release: The Trainer's Application Guide

exercises.name: Foam Roll Lats
instructions: Lie on your side with the roller just below your armpit and the bottom arm reaching overhead.
Use your top hand and feet on the floor for support.
Roll slowly from the armpit toward the lower ribs.
Pause on tight spots, work for one to two minutes, then switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Thumb up, roll slow.
exercises.commonMistakes: Too much pressure, or rolling onto the ribs at the front.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it standing with the roller or a ball against a wall.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Easing the lats can make reaching overhead feel smoother.

exercises.name: Foam Roll Adductors
instructions: Lie face down on your forearms with one knee bent out to the side.
Place the roller under the inner thigh of that leg, at a right angle to it.
Roll slowly between the groin and the inside of the knee.
Pause on tender spots, work for one to two minutes, then switch legs.
exercises.formCue: Small, slow passes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rolling too fast or pressing right into the groin crease.
exercises.beginnerModification: Take more weight on your forearms and the other leg.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The inner thigh is easy to forget and often feels tight after squats and side-to-side work.

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and your head supported.
Rest one hand on your upper chest and the other just below your ribs.
Breathe in slowly through your nose so the lower hand rises while the chest hand stays still.
Breathe out slowly through pursed lips as your belly falls, and repeat for a few minutes.
exercises.formCue: Belly rises, chest stays quiet.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting the chest and shoulders, or forcing big breaths.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise for one minute at a time and build up.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Slow belly breathing is a simple way to bring effort and heart rate down after training.

exercises.name: Box Breathing
instructions: Sit or lie comfortably and breathe all the way out.
Breathe in through your nose for a count of four.
Hold gently for a count of four.
Breathe out for a count of four, hold for four, and repeat for three or four rounds.
exercises.formCue: Four in, four hold, four out, four hold.
exercises.commonMistakes: Straining on the holds or counting too slowly for comfort.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a count of three, or skip the holds.
exercises.whyThisMatters: An even counted breath gives the mind one simple thing to follow while the body settles.

exercises.name: Band External Rotation
instructions: Anchor a light band at elbow height and stand side-on to it.
Hold the band in the far hand with the elbow bent to 90 degrees and tucked to your side.
Rotate the forearm outward, keeping the elbow against your ribs.
Pause, then return slowly to the start.
exercises.formCue: Elbow glued to the ribs.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the elbow drift away from the body, or using a band that is too heavy.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it without a band, or lying on your side with a very light weight.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the small rotator cuff muscles that keep the shoulder steady.

source.name: AAOS OrthoInfo, Rotator Cuff and Shoulder Conditioning Program

exercises.name: Shoulder Pendulum
instructions: Lean forward with one hand resting on a table.
Let the other arm hang straight down and relaxed.
Gently swing the arm forward and back, then side to side.
Finish with small circles in each direction, then switch arms.
exercises.formCue: Let the arm hang heavy.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the back or using shoulder muscles to drive a big swing.
exercises.beginnerModification: Make the swings smaller.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is a gentle way to move the shoulder without loading it.

source.name: AAOS OrthoInfo, Rotator Cuff and Shoulder Conditioning Program

exercises.name: Single-Leg Stand
instructions: Stand facing a wall with your fingertips resting on it.
Lift one foot off the floor, keeping your hips level.
Keep a slight bend in the standing knee and hold for 5 to 10 seconds.
Lower the foot and repeat on the other side.
exercises.formCue: Hips level, soft knee, eyes forward.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning the trunk to the side or locking the standing knee.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the toes of the lifted foot resting lightly on the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Standing steady on one leg is the base of walking, stairs and catching yourself from a trip.

exercises.name: Tandem Stance
instructions: Stand tall beside a support.
Place one foot directly in front of the other so the heel touches the toes.
Look ahead and hold the position for 10 seconds.
Switch the front foot and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Feet on a tightrope, eyes up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Looking down at the feet or gripping the support hard.
exercises.beginnerModification: Leave a small gap between the feet, or stand with them slightly offset.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A narrow stance trains side-to-side steadiness with very little risk.

source.name: Otago Exercise Programme (Royal Orthopaedic Hospital NHS)

exercises.name: Heel-to-Toe Walk
instructions: Stand tall next to a wall.
Place one heel on the floor directly in front of the toes of the other foot.
Step the back foot through and place it heel to toe in front.
Keep looking forward and take at least five steps.
exercises.formCue: Look ahead, not at your feet.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rushing the steps or stepping wide to stay balanced.
exercises.beginnerModification: Run your fingers along the wall as you walk.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the narrow-base balance needed for steady walking.

exercises.name: Sideways Walk
instructions: Stand with feet together and knees slightly bent.
Step one foot out to the side in a slow, controlled way.
Bring the other foot in to join it without dropping your hips.
Take 10 steps one way, then 10 steps back.
exercises.formCue: Slow steps, level hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swaying the trunk or letting the feet turn out.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it facing a kitchen counter with your hands resting on it.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Controlled side steps strengthen the hips that keep you steady when you move sideways.

exercises.name: Sit-to-Stand
instructions: Sit toward the front of a chair with feet hip-width apart.
Lean slightly forward, looking straight ahead.
Stand up slowly using your legs rather than your arms.
Stand fully upright, then sit back down slowly.
exercises.formCue: Nose over toes, then stand.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping back into the chair or pushing mostly with the hands.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a higher seat or push lightly on the armrests.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Getting out of a chair without help is a basic test of leg strength for daily life.

exercises.name: Supported Mini Squat
instructions: Stand behind a chair with your hands resting on it and feet hip-width apart.
Bend your knees a comfortable amount, keeping them over your toes.
Keep your back straight and heels down.
Stand back up by squeezing your buttocks, and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Small bend, knees over toes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning forward onto the chair or letting the knees fall inward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bend only a few centimetres.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A short-range squat builds leg strength with support close at hand.

exercises.name: Supported Heel Raise
instructions: Stand tall with your hands resting on the back of a chair.
Lift both heels off the floor as far as is comfortable.
Move slowly and stay upright without leaning forward.
Lower the heels with control and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Rise slow, lower slower.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing, or rolling out onto the outer edges of the feet.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it seated, lifting the heels one at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Strong calves help with walking, stairs and balance.

exercises.name: Low Step-Up
exercises.equipment: Low step with a rail or wall
instructions: Stand facing a low step with a hand on a rail or wall.
Step up with one foot and place the whole foot on the step.
Bring the other foot up to join it.
Step back down slowly, one foot at a time, and repeat leading with the other leg.
exercises.formCue: Whole foot on the step. Slow on the way down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling up with the arm or dropping down quickly.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lower step and keep a firm hold of the rail.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It practises stair climbing in a controlled way.

exercises.name: Marching in Place
instructions: Stand tall with elbows bent and hands relaxed.
March on the spot, lifting each knee to a comfortable height.
Swing your arms in time with your steps.
Add a few steps forward and back as you keep the rhythm.
exercises.formCue: Tall posture, steady rhythm.
exercises.commonMistakes: Stamping the feet or slouching.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold a support and lift the knees only a little.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A few minutes of marching raises body temperature gently before exercise.

source.name: NHS, How to warm up before exercising

exercises.name: Neck Rotation
instructions: Sit upright with your shoulders relaxed and down.
Turn your head slowly toward one shoulder as far as is comfortable.
Hold for a few seconds and return to the centre.
Repeat to the other side, three times each way.
exercises.formCue: Turn, do not tilt.
exercises.commonMistakes: Forcing the range or letting the shoulders turn with the head.
exercises.beginnerModification: Turn through a smaller range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It keeps the neck moving freely, which helps with tasks like checking over your shoulder.

exercises.name: Neck Side Stretch
instructions: Sit upright and look straight ahead.
Hold one shoulder down with the opposite hand.
Slowly tilt your head away from that shoulder until you feel a gentle stretch.
Hold for a few seconds, return to the centre, and repeat on the other side.
exercises.formCue: Ear toward shoulder, shoulder stays down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling on the head or letting the held shoulder hike up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Tilt only a little and skip the shoulder hold.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It eases the side of the neck after long periods of sitting.

exercises.name: Standing Toe Raise
instructions: Stand tall holding a support with feet hip-width apart.
Rock back gently onto your heels and lift the fronts of both feet.
Keep your knees soft and your hips over your heels.
Lower the toes slowly and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Toes to shins, hips stay stacked.
exercises.commonMistakes: Sticking the hips back or leaning on the support.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it seated, lifting the toes with heels on the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Strong shin muscles lift the toes clear of the ground with each step.

source.name: Otago Exercise Programme (Royal Orthopaedic Hospital NHS)

exercises.name: Heel Walk
instructions: Stand tall beside a counter or rail.
Lift your toes so your weight is on your heels.
Walk 10 small steps on your heels, looking ahead.
Lower your feet, turn around, and walk back the same way.
exercises.formCue: Toes up, small steps.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending forward at the hips or taking long strides.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep a hand on the support the whole way.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It combines shin strength with balance in a walking pattern.

source.name: Otago Exercise Programme (Royal Orthopaedic Hospital NHS)

exercises.name: Ankle Alphabet
exercises.musclesWorked: Ankle joint, calf and shin muscles
instructions: Sit on a chair or bench high enough that one foot can hang free.
Lead with the big toe and trace the letters of the alphabet in the air.
Keep the movement small and coming from the ankle, not the knee or hip.
Finish the alphabet, then switch feet.
exercises.formCue: Draw with the big toe. Shin stays still.
exercises.commonMistakes: Moving the whole leg instead of the ankle.
exercises.beginnerModification: Trace half the alphabet, or just point and pull the foot ten times.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It takes the ankle through every direction it moves, which helps keep it mobile.

source.name: AAOS OrthoInfo, Foot and Ankle Conditioning Program

exercises.name: Foot Arch Roll
exercises.equipment: Golf ball or small massage ball, chair
instructions: Sit on a stable chair with both feet on the floor.
Place a small ball under the arch of one foot.
Roll the ball slowly back and forth from heel to ball of the foot for up to two minutes.
Switch feet.
exercises.formCue: Light pressure, slow rolls.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing on the ball with full weight.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a softer or larger ball.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A short roll under the arch can make the feet feel looser after a long day standing.

source.name: AAOS OrthoInfo, Foot and Ankle Conditioning Program

exercises.name: B-Skip
instructions: Stand tall with the chest up and eyes forward.
Skip off one foot while lifting the opposite knee to hip height, as in an A-skip.
Extend the lifted leg forward, then sweep it down and back so the foot lands under the hips.
Alternate legs and travel forward for 20 to 30 metres with relaxed, opposite arm swing.
exercises.formCue: Knee up, reach, paw back.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning back as the leg extends, or kicking straight out from the floor without lifting the knee first.
exercises.beginnerModification: Walk through the pattern as a march before adding the skip.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It rehearses pulling the foot back under the body, which is the answer to overstriding.

exercises.name: Ankling Drill
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Take very short steps forward, rolling each foot down from the toe so the heel barely touches the ground.
Keep the knees low and the steps quick and springy.
Learn the pattern slowly, then raise the step rate over 10 to 20 metres.
exercises.formCue: Small steps, springy ankles.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting the knees high, or letting the heels drop heavily on each step.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it at walking speed until the foot action feels smooth.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the foot and ankle to load and release quickly, which every running step needs.

exercises.name: Strides
instructions: After an easy run, find a flat stretch of roughly 80 to 100 metres.
Build speed smoothly over the first third until you are running fast but relaxed, well short of an all-out sprint.
Hold that speed with tall posture and quick steps, then ease down gradually.
Walk or jog easily for 60 to 90 seconds and repeat 4 to 8 times.
exercises.formCue: Fast and relaxed, never straining.
exercises.commonMistakes: Turning them into flat-out sprints, or reaching the foot out in front to lengthen the step.
exercises.beginnerModification: Run 4 shorter strides at a comfortably quick pace with a full walk back.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A few short accelerations keep fast running mechanics sharp without adding fatigue.

exercises.name: Hill Repeats
instructions: Warm up with at least 10 minutes of easy running and find a steady hill.
Run up the hill at a hard, controlled effort, judging it by feel rather than pace.
Keep the steps short and the trunk tall, with a slight lean from the ankles.
Jog or walk slowly back down to recover, then repeat.
exercises.formCue: Short steps, tall chest.
exercises.commonMistakes: Sprinting the first repeat and fading on the rest, or bending at the waist as the hill bites.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a gentle slope, shorten each effort to 30 seconds and walk down.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Hills build running strength and fitness at lower speed and lower impact than flat sprints.

exercises.name: Tempo Run
instructions: Jog easily for 10 minutes to warm up.
Raise the pace to comfortably hard, an effort where you can say a few words but not hold a conversation.
Hold that effort evenly for 20 to 30 minutes.
Finish with 5 to 10 minutes of easy jogging.
exercises.formCue: Comfortably hard, and even.
exercises.commonMistakes: Starting too fast and slowing through the second half, or running it like a race.
exercises.beginnerModification: Split the hard running into blocks of 5 to 10 minutes with 2 minutes of easy jogging between them.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Sustained work near threshold raises the pace you can hold before fatigue builds.

exercises.name: Fartlek Run
instructions: Warm up with 10 minutes of easy running.
Pick a landmark or a time and run faster until you reach it.
Drop back to an easy jog until your breathing settles.
Keep mixing faster and easier stretches of different lengths by feel, then cool down with easy running.
exercises.formCue: Surge, settle, repeat.
exercises.commonMistakes: Making every surge an all-out sprint, or stopping to walk instead of jogging between efforts.
exercises.beginnerModification: Alternate 1 minute a little quicker with 2 minutes very easy.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Unstructured pace changes train you to shift speed and recover while still moving.

exercises.name: Long Slow Run
instructions: Plan a route or time that is longer than any other run in your week.
Start at an easy pace where you can talk in full sentences.
Hold that easy effort the whole way and let pace drop on hills.
Finish feeling you could have continued, then walk for a few minutes.
exercises.formCue: Slow enough to chat.
exercises.commonMistakes: Running it at a medium-hard effort, or extending the distance by a big jump from one week to the next.
exercises.beginnerModification: Add walk breaks every few minutes and keep the total time modest.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Time on feet at low intensity builds the aerobic base everything else sits on.

exercises.name: Cadence Drill
instructions: During an easy run, count your steps for one minute to find your usual step rate.
Set a metronome about 5 percent faster than that number.
Run for 1 minute matching your steps to the beat, keeping the same speed by taking shorter, lighter steps.
Jog normally for 1 to 2 minutes and repeat several times.
exercises.formCue: Quicker feet, same speed.
exercises.commonMistakes: Speeding up instead of shortening the step, or jumping to a much higher rate in one go.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the faster rhythm for 30 seconds at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A slightly quicker step rate shortens the stride and softens each landing.

exercises.name: Easy Recovery Run
instructions: Start at a gentle jog, slower than feels necessary.
Keep the effort low enough to breathe through the nose or talk freely.
Stay relaxed and tall with short, light steps for about 20 to 30 minutes.
Take a walk break if your form starts to get heavy or sloppy.
exercises.formCue: Easy means easy.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the pace creep up into a moderate run, which turns a recovery day into another training day.
exercises.beginnerModification: Alternate a few minutes of jogging with a minute of walking.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Gentle running between hard days keeps the habit and the blood flow without adding stress.

exercises.name: Run-Walk Intervals
instructions: Walk briskly for 5 minutes to warm up.
Run at an easy pace for 1 minute.
Walk for 4 minutes to recover.
Repeat the run and walk four times, then walk for 5 minutes to cool down.
exercises.formCue: Easy run, real walk.
exercises.commonMistakes: Running the minute too fast, or adding running time before the current session feels comfortable.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the run to 30 seconds and keep the walks the same.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Walk breaks let you build up to running a little at a time instead of all at once.

exercises.name: Track Repeats
instructions: Warm up with 10 to 15 minutes of easy running and a few strides.
Run a set distance, such as 400 metres, at a hard pace you can repeat.
Jog or walk for about as long as the hard effort took.
Repeat for the planned number of efforts, aiming for the same time on each, then cool down.
exercises.formCue: Same pace, first rep to last.
exercises.commonMistakes: Running the first repeats too fast and falling apart, or cutting the recovery short.
exercises.beginnerModification: Halve the distance of each repeat and walk the full recovery.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Hard, measured efforts with planned rest let you spend more total time near top aerobic effort.

exercises.name: Incline Treadmill Walk
instructions: Start the belt flat at a comfortable walk for a few minutes.
Raise the incline to a moderate grade and set a speed you can hold without gripping the rails.
Walk tall with the arms swinging freely and the whole foot pushing through each step.
Lower the incline and walk flat for a few minutes to finish.
exercises.formCue: Hands off the rails.
exercises.commonMistakes: Holding the handles and leaning back, which takes the work away from the legs.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lower incline and slower speed, and rest a hand lightly on the rail only for balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The grade raises the heart rate and works the hips hard at walking speed.

exercises.name: Elliptical Trainer
instructions: Step onto the pedals, hold the moving handles and start striding at a low resistance.
Stand upright with the shoulders over the hips.
Push and pull the handles in time with the legs so the stride feels like a smooth run.
Raise the resistance until the effort matches the session, and slow gradually before stepping off.
exercises.formCue: Stand tall, full strides.
