exercises.commonMistakes: Slouching over the console, or letting momentum carry the pedals at a resistance that is too low.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the fixed handles and keep the resistance light for short sessions.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It gives a running-style effort for arms and legs with very little impact.

exercises.name: Stair Climber
instructions: Step on, start at a slow speed and find a steady rhythm.
Stand upright with the hands resting lightly on the rails for balance only.
Place the whole foot on each step and lift the feet clear as the steps turn.
Raise the speed gradually and build the length of the session over several weeks.
exercises.formCue: Light hands, tall body.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning heavily on the rails or hunching over them, which takes load off the legs.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a slow speed for a few minutes at a time with flat walking between bouts.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Steady climbing is demanding cardio that also builds hip and thigh endurance.

exercises.name: Power Walk
instructions: Stand tall with the eyes on the horizon, chest lifted and midsection lightly braced.
Bend the elbows to roughly a right angle and swing the arms forward and back from the shoulders.
Land on the heel and roll through to push off the toes.
Pick up speed by taking quicker steps rather than longer ones.
exercises.formCue: Tall posture, quick steps.
exercises.commonMistakes: Overreaching with the front foot, or looking down and rounding the shoulders.
exercises.beginnerModification: Alternate a few minutes of brisk walking with a few minutes at a normal pace.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Brisk walking with good form is cardio almost anyone can do daily and recover from.

exercises.name: Agility Ladder Icky Shuffle
instructions: Stand to the left of the first square in an athletic stance with hips and knees slightly bent.
Step the right foot into the square, then the left foot in beside it.
Step the right foot out to the right of the ladder, then bring the left foot forward into the next square.
Follow with the right foot in, step the left foot out to the left, and keep the in-in-out rhythm zig-zagging up the ladder.
exercises.formCue: In, in, out. Stay on the balls of your feet.
exercises.commonMistakes: Staring at the feet and standing tall, or rushing the pattern before the rhythm is clean.
exercises.beginnerModification: Walk the pattern slowly and say the steps out loud until it is automatic, then add speed.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains fast, coordinated weight shifts from side to side while still moving forward.

exercises.name: Agility Ladder Lateral Shuffle
instructions: Stand side-on at one end of the ladder with both feet in the first square, knees soft and chest over toes.
Shift your weight to the trailing leg and step the lead foot into the next square.
Bring the trailing foot in to join it without crossing your feet.
Travel the full ladder, then return leading with the other foot.
exercises.formCue: Hips low, feet quick, never cross.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bobbing up and down with each step, or letting the feet click together and cross.
exercises.beginnerModification: Slow to a walk and use one foot contact per square before adding the second.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Quick lateral steps from a low stance are the base of defending and changing direction.

exercises.name: L-Drill
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, hamstrings, calves, hip stabilisers
instructions: Set three cones in an L shape with about 5 yards between each cone.
Sprint from the first cone to the second, touch the line, and sprint back to the first.
Sprint back to the second cone, round it tightly, and weave around the inside of the third cone.
Round the third cone, come back around the second, and finish through the first cone.
exercises.formCue: Short choppy steps into the cone, lean, then go.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing up tall at the cones and taking wide looping turns.
exercises.beginnerModification: Jog the route at half speed until the path is memorised, then build pace.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It rehearses braking, tight turning and re-accelerating in one short effort.

source.name: NSCA, Developing Agility and Quickness (Human Kinetics excerpt)

exercises.name: Falling Start
instructions: Stand tall with feet under your hips and eyes straight ahead.
Keep your body in one straight line and let yourself tip forward from the ankles.
At the point where you must step, drive one knee forward hard and punch the opposite arm.
Push the ground back behind you and accelerate for 10 to 20 metres, rising gradually.
exercises.formCue: Fall as a plank, then drive.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending at the waist instead of leaning as one line, or stepping out too early.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start from a staggered stance with a smaller lean and run at three-quarter speed.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the forward body lean and first-step drive that acceleration depends on.

source.name: Human Kinetics, Three Drills for Developing Starts and Initial Acceleration

exercises.name: Resisted Sled Sprint
instructions: Attach the harness to a lightly loaded sled and walk forward until the strap is tight.
Set a staggered stance with a forward lean from the ankles.
Drive out and sprint 10 to 20 metres, pushing the ground back with each step.
Keep the same lean and arm action you would use in an unloaded start, then walk back and rest fully.
exercises.formCue: Lean and push. Same shape as a free sprint.
exercises.commonMistakes: Loading the sled so heavy that the stride turns into a grind and posture breaks.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a very light sled or sprint up a gentle slope instead.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A light towing load builds the horizontal push used in the first steps of a sprint.

source.name: NSCA Coach, Sled Resisted Sprint Training

exercises.name: Sprint and Stop
instructions: Place two cones 10 to 15 metres apart.
Accelerate from the first cone at a controlled, fast pace.
As you near the second cone, lower your hips and shorten your steps, bending at the ankles, knees and hips on each contact.
Come to a balanced stop at the cone in an athletic stance and hold for two seconds.
exercises.formCue: Sink the hips, chop the steps, own the stop.
exercises.commonMistakes: Braking with stiff, upright legs or leaning back on the heels.
exercises.beginnerModification: Run at half speed and allow more steps to slow down.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Being able to brake under control comes before every cut and change of direction.

source.name: NSCA, Effective Deceleration Technique for Court and Field Sports

exercises.name: Snap-Down
instructions: Stand tall on your toes with both arms reaching overhead.
Pull your arms down fast and let your feet leave the floor slightly.
Land on both feet at once with hips back, knees bent and chest over your knees.
Hold the landing position for two seconds, then stand and reset.
exercises.formCue: Snap down and freeze.
exercises.commonMistakes: Knees caving inward or landing stiff and loud.
exercises.beginnerModification: Skip the hop and simply drop quickly from tall into the landing position.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the landing position at low impact before any real jumping.

source.name: NSCA, Plyometric Implementation: Jump Landing Positions

exercises.name: Drop Landing
instructions: Stand on a low box, about 15 to 30 cm high.
Step off the edge without jumping up.
Land on both feet together, hips back, knees bent and in line with your toes.
Hold the landing for two seconds before stepping back up.
exercises.formCue: Step off, land quiet, stick it.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jumping up off the box, or letting the knees collapse inward on contact.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lower step, or go back to the snap-down.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the ability to absorb force from a height before rebound jumps are added.

source.name: NSCA, Plyometric Implementation: Jump Landing Positions

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hop and Stick
instructions: Balance on one leg with a soft knee.
Hop forward a short distance and land on the same leg.
Absorb the landing with hip and knee bent, knee over the middle of the foot.
Hold still for two seconds, then reset and repeat before switching legs.
exercises.formCue: Small hop, quiet landing, hold.
exercises.commonMistakes: Hopping too far, wobbling at the knee, or letting the hip drop on landing.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hop from two feet and land on one, or shorten the hop to a few centimetres.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Most sport landings and cuts happen on one leg, so control has to be trained on one leg.

source.name: NSCA, Plyometric Implementation: Jump Landing Positions

exercises.name: Hurdle Hop
instructions: Line up low hurdles about a metre apart and stand facing the first one.
Jump off both feet over the first hurdle, pulling the toes up in the air.
Land on both feet at the same time and rebound straight into the next jump.
Keep ground contacts short and the torso tall through the full row, then walk back.
exercises.formCue: Both feet together. Bounce, do not sink.
exercises.commonMistakes: Sinking deep into each landing, or landing one foot after the other.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use mini hurdles or lines on the floor and pause to reset between jumps.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Repeated rebounds train the quick, springy ground contact used in sprinting and jumping.

source.name: ISBS Conference Proceedings, Kinetic Analysis of Horizontal Plyometric Exercise Intensity

exercises.name: Alternate Leg Push-Off
instructions: Place one foot flat on a low box with the other foot on the floor.
Drive through the box foot and swing your arms to jump straight up.
Switch legs in the air so the other foot lands on the box.
Land softly with hips back and knees bent, then go again.
exercises.formCue: Drive up through the box foot.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pushing mostly off the floor foot, or landing heavily with a locked knee.
exercises.beginnerModification: Pause and reset between jumps, or use a lower step.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It develops single-leg drive in the same alternating rhythm as running.

exercises.name: Forward Hurdle Run
instructions: Line up mini hurdles roughly a stride apart and start in a staggered stance.
Run through with one foot landing between each pair of hurdles.
Lift each knee to about hip height and swing the opposite arm from the shoulder.
Stay tall with your trunk braced until you are past the last hurdle.
exercises.formCue: Knee up, toe up, stay tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning back or looking down, which shortens the knee lift.
exercises.beginnerModification: Walk or march over the hurdles first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It grooves knee lift, rhythm and upright posture for faster running.

exercises.name: Lateral Bound to Shot-Put Throw
instructions: Stand side-on to a wall, a few metres away, holding a light medicine ball at your chest.
Bound sideways away from the wall and land on the outside leg, loading the hip.
Push back off that leg, rotate your hips and trunk toward the wall.
Finish by punching the ball from the back shoulder into the wall, then collect it and reset.
exercises.formCue: Load the hip, turn, then throw.
exercises.commonMistakes: Throwing with the arm only, or losing balance on the landing before the throw.
exercises.beginnerModification: Remove the bound and throw from a split stance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It links a sideways push off the ground to a rotational throw, as in striking and throwing sports.

source.name: NSCA, Strength Training for Lacrosse (Human Kinetics excerpt)

exercises.name: Plant and Cut
instructions: Jog four or five steps in a straight line.
Plant on the outside foot with the knee bent and in line with the toes.
Push off that foot to change direction diagonally.
Accelerate for five to seven quick steps, slow down, and repeat off the other foot.
exercises.formCue: Plant under the hip, knee over toes, go.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the planted knee buckle inward, or cutting with an upright trunk.
exercises.beginnerModification: Walk into the plant and make the angle of the cut shallow.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It rehearses the cutting step with good knee position at a controlled speed.

exercises.name: Quick Forward-Backward Run
instructions: Set a line of cones about 5 metres apart.
Run forward quickly two cones.
Run backward one cone with hips and knees slightly bent and small quick steps.
Keep repeating two forward, one back until the end of the line, then jog back.
exercises.formCue: Small fast steps, hips low going back.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing upright and leaning back while backpedalling.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it at a jog and shorten the cone spacing.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains quick transitions between forward running and backpedalling.

exercises.name: Squat with Toe Raise
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips.
Sit back slowly until your knees are bent to about 90 degrees, keeping them in line with your toes.
Stand up a little faster than you went down.
Once your legs are straight, rise onto your toes, then lower the heels and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Slow down, knees out, finish tall on the toes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Knees drifting inward on the way down.
exercises.beginnerModification: Squat to a shallower depth and hold a support for the toe raise.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It pairs knee-control practice with calf strength in one simple warm-up move.

exercises.name: Running Hip Out
instructions: Jog easily in a straight line.
Every few steps, pause and lift one knee forward to hip height.
Rotate that knee out to the side, then put the foot down.
Jog on and repeat with the other leg.
exercises.formCue: Knee up, open the gate.
exercises.commonMistakes: Twisting the trunk instead of moving at the hip.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it walking with a hand on a wall for balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It opens the hips and wakes up single-leg balance before faster running.

exercises.name: Running Hip In
instructions: Jog easily in a straight line.
Every few steps, pause and lift one knee out to the side at hip height.
Rotate that knee inward to the front, then put the foot down.
Jog on and repeat with the other leg.
exercises.formCue: Knee out, close the gate.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning the body away from the lifted leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it walking with a hand on a wall for balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It prepares the inner hip and groin for cutting and kicking.

exercises.name: Partner Mirror Drill
instructions: Set two cones about 5 metres apart and face your partner between them.
One athlete leads, shuffling left and right between the cones and changing direction at random.
The other athlete mirrors every move, staying square and directly opposite.
Work for about 10 seconds, rest, then swap roles.
exercises.formCue: Watch the hips, stay low, stay square.
exercises.commonMistakes: Crossing the feet or guessing instead of reacting.
exercises.beginnerModification: Have the leader move at half speed with clearer changes of direction.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Reacting to another person is closer to real sport than any pre-planned cone pattern.

source.name: National Association of Speed and Explosion

exercises.name: Ball Drop Reaction
instructions: Stand in an athletic stance a few metres from a partner who holds a tennis ball at shoulder height.
The partner drops the ball without warning.
Sprint and catch the ball before it bounces a second time.
Walk back and reset, and increase the distance as you get faster.
exercises.formCue: Eyes on the ball, first step low.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing tall while waiting, or reaching with the hands instead of moving the feet.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start closer to the partner.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains a fast first step in response to something you see, not a planned start.

source.name: NSCA, 5 Reaction Drills to Build Quickness

exercises.name: Single-Leg Squat Touchdown
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, hip stabilisers, ankle stabilisers
instructions: Stand on one leg with the other foot hovering just in front or to the side.
Brace your trunk and sit back into a single-leg squat.
Lower until the toes of the free leg lightly touch the floor.
Drive through the standing foot to return to the top, and finish all reps before switching.
exercises.formCue: Touch like the floor is hot. Weight stays on the standing leg.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing knee collapsing inward, or putting real weight through the touching foot.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold a support with one hand and squat to a shallower depth.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds single-leg strength and knee control without needing any load.

exercises.name: Kneeling Wood Chop
exercises.equipment: Cable machine or band with high anchor
instructions: Set a cable at its highest position and kneel side-on to it with the inside leg forward and the outside knee down.
Grip the rope with both hands, reaching up toward the anchor.
Pull the rope diagonally across your body down to the outside hip.
Keep the torso tall and hips still, pause, and return under control.
exercises.formCue: Tall spine, hips quiet, arms draw the line.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending or twisting from the lower back, or letting the hips swing.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light band and shorten the range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The kneeling stance takes the legs out so the trunk has to control the diagonal pull.

exercises.name: Kneeling Hay Baler
exercises.equipment: Cable machine or band with low anchor
instructions: Set a cable at its lowest position and kneel side-on to it with the outside leg forward and the inside knee down.
Grip the rope with both hands beside the inside hip.
Pull the rope up to your chest, then press it up and across in front of the far shoulder.
Pause for a second at the top with your torso still, then lower slowly.
exercises.formCue: Pull to the chest, press across, body stays still.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning away from the machine or shrugging the load up with the arms only.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter load, or the medicine-ball version.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A low-to-high diagonal pull trains the trunk to pass force upward, as in throwing and swinging.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Medicine Ball Hay Baler
instructions: Kneel with one foot forward and the other knee on the floor.
Hold a medicine ball in both hands beside the hip of the back leg.
Turn your trunk and shoulders to sweep the ball across your body and over the opposite shoulder.
Lower it back along the same path, and finish all reps before switching sides.
exercises.formCue: Eyes follow the ball. Hips face forward.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swinging the arms without turning the trunk, or wobbling at the hips.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter ball or no ball at all.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is a simple entry to diagonal trunk rotation with a stable base.

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge Wood Chop
exercises.equipment: Cable machine or band at shoulder height
instructions: Set a cable at shoulder height and stand side-on to it holding the handle in both hands near the inside shoulder.
Step sideways away from the machine into a lateral lunge.
As the foot lands, keep your arms long and rotate to bring the handle down toward the lunging leg.
Push off that foot and rotate back to the start.
exercises.formCue: Step, sit, chop. One smooth move.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the back to reach down, or letting the lunging knee cave in.
exercises.beginnerModification: Learn the lateral lunge and the standing chop separately first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It ties a sideways step to trunk rotation, the way cutting and reaching happen in sport.

exercises.name: Anti-Rotation Reverse Lunge
exercises.equipment: Cable machine or band at chest height
instructions: Set a cable at chest height and stand side-on to it with feet hip-width apart.
Hold the handle in both hands and press your arms straight out in front of your chest.
Step the leg nearest the machine back into a lunge, lowering the knee toward the floor.
Keep the hands in front of your breastbone the whole time, then push through the front foot to stand.
exercises.formCue: Hands stay on the centre line.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the cable turn the shoulders, or leaning toward the machine.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the press-out standing still first, then add a shallow lunge.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the trunk to resist twisting while the legs move, which is how the core works in running and cutting.

exercises.name: High-Bar Back Squat
instructions: Set the bar on top of the traps, grip as narrow as is comfortable, and pull the shoulder blades together.
Unrack, step back into your stance, take a big breath into the belly, and brace all the way around the trunk.
Bend the knees and hips together and sit straight down, keeping the torso fairly upright and the weight over the middle of the foot.
Go as deep as you can hold position, then drive up with the chest and hips rising at the same speed.
exercises.formCue: Sit down between your heels, chest tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hips shoot up first out of the bottom, or losing the brace and folding forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Squat to a box at parallel height with an empty bar, or use a goblet squat until the upright position feels natural.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The upright, deep position builds the quads and carries straight over to front squats and the Olympic lifts.

exercises.name: Low-Bar Back Squat
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, quads, hamstrings, adductors, spinal erectors
instructions: Set the bar a few centimetres below the top of the traps, across the rear shoulders, and squeeze the upper back tight to make a shelf.
Unrack, take two short steps back, breathe in, and brace hard.
Push the hips back as the knees bend and let the torso lean forward enough to keep the bar over the middle of the foot.
Lower until the hip crease drops just below the top of the knee.
Drive the hips and shoulders up together until you stand fully locked out.
exercises.formCue: Bar over midfoot, the whole way down and up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bar rolling down the back because the upper back is loose, or cutting depth as the load gets heavy.
exercises.beginnerModification: Learn the bar position with an empty bar and squat to a box set just below parallel.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the bar position most powerlifters use because it lets the hips do more of the work.

exercises.name: Pause Squat
instructions: Set up and descend exactly as you would for your normal back squat.
Stop dead at the bottom and hold for two to three seconds with the trunk braced hard.
Stay still during the hold with no bouncing or rocking.
Drive straight up as fast as you can and stand fully before the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Stay tight in the hole, then explode.
exercises.commonMistakes: Cutting the pause short, or relaxing the trunk at the bottom and losing position.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter load with a one-second pause, or pause a goblet squat first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Removing the bounce builds strength and control in the hardest part of the squat.

exercises.name: Pin Squat
exercises.equipment: Barbell, power rack with safety pins
instructions: Set the rack pins at the squat depth you want to train.
Lower under control until the bar settles completely on the pins.
Keep your position over the middle of the foot and brace the trunk again while the pins hold the weight.
Drive the bar off the pins and accelerate all the way to standing.
Let every rep come to a full stop on the pins before the next one.
exercises.formCue: Dead stop, get tight, then drive.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing the bar off the pins, or relaxing so much on the pins that your position is lost.
exercises.beginnerModification: Set the pins a little higher and use a light load until you can settle and restart without shifting.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Starting from a dead stop teaches you to produce force with no rebound at your weakest depth.

exercises.name: Box Squat
exercises.equipment: Barbell, squat rack, box or bench
instructions: Place a sturdy box behind you at about parallel height and unrack the bar on your upper back.
Sit the hips back and down under control, keeping the shins close to vertical.
Settle onto the box lightly while staying braced, without dropping or rocking.
Drive through the whole foot and stand up until hips and knees are locked.
exercises.formCue: Sit back softly, stay tight on the box.
exercises.commonMistakes: Crashing onto the box, or relaxing the trunk while seated and rocking forward to get up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a higher box and a goblet hold, then lower the box as control improves.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The box gives the same depth every rep and loads the hips hard from a controlled stop.

exercises.name: Safety Bar Squat
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, upper back, spinal erectors
instructions: Duck under the bar so the pad sits across the shoulders with the yoke around the neck, and hold the handles.
Unrack, step back, set your stance, and brace.
Bend the hips and knees and squat until the thighs are just past parallel, keeping the chest up against the forward pull of the bar.
Drive back up by extending the hips and knees until you are standing tall.
exercises.formCue: Chest up, do not let the bar fold you.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the upper back round forward, or pulling the handles down so the bar tips.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start light and squat to a box until you can hold the upright position.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the squat hard while asking far less of the shoulders, elbows, and wrists.

exercises.name: Zercher Squat
instructions: Set the bar in the rack just below elbow height and hook it in the crooks of your elbows.
Keep the elbows close together, pull the bar into your body, stand it up, and step back.
Brace and squat down between the knees as deep as you can with a straight back.
Drive up through the whole foot, keeping the chest tall and the bar tight to the body.
exercises.formCue: Hug the bar in and stay tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the back round as the bar pulls forward, or going heavy before the elbows have adapted.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a goblet squat, or wrap the bar in a pad and start with light loads.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The front-loaded position builds the trunk and upper back along with the legs.

exercises.name: One-and-a-Quarter Squat
instructions: Squat down under control to your full depth.
Without bouncing, rise only to just below parallel while keeping the legs and glutes tight.
Sink back to the bottom again.
Stand all the way up to finish one rep.
exercises.formCue: Down, quarter up, down, stand.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom, or coming up too high on the quarter rep.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do the same pattern with a goblet squat or an empty bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The extra trip through the bottom builds leg strength and control where squats are usually lost.

exercises.name: Paused Bench Press
instructions: Lie back, pinch the shoulder blades together and down, set a slight arch, and plant the feet.
Unrack and lower the bar under control to the lower chest.
Hold the bar still on the chest for a full second while staying tight.
Press up and slightly back toward the shoulders until the elbows lock.
exercises.formCue: Touch, stay tight, press.
exercises.commonMistakes: Relaxing on the chest so the bar sinks, or lifting the hips off the bench to start the press.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter load with a short count, or pause a dumbbell bench press.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A motionless pause is how the bench is judged in competition and it builds honest strength off the chest.

exercises.name: Larsen Press
instructions: Set up as you would for your normal bench press with the shoulder blades pinched back and down.
Unrack the bar, then straighten the legs and hold the feet just off the floor.
Lower the bar under control to the lower chest.
Press back to lockout while the legs stay off the floor and the body stays still on the bench.
exercises.formCue: Legs out, upper back locked into the bench.
exercises.commonMistakes: Wobbling on the bench because the upper back is loose, or loading it like a normal bench press.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bench with the knees bent and feet resting on the bench before taking the legs out straight.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Taking leg drive away makes the chest, shoulders, and triceps do all the pressing.

exercises.name: Floor Press
instructions: Lie on the floor under a bar set low in the rack, knees bent, and take an overhand grip.
Unrack and hold the bar over the lower chest with the arms straight.
Lower until the backs of the upper arms rest fully on the floor.
Pause briefly, then press back up to lockout.
exercises.formCue: Arms settle on the floor, then press.
exercises.commonMistakes: Slamming the elbows into the floor, or bouncing off it to start the press.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use dumbbells on the floor so each arm can settle at its own pace.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The shortened range builds lockout strength with little stress at the bottom of the press.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Set the bench to a low incline, lie back, and grip the bar slightly wider than the shoulders.
Unrack and bring the bar over the upper chest with the arms straight.
Lower under control to the upper chest.
Press up until the arms are fully extended.
exercises.formCue: Bar to the upper chest, elbows under the bar.
exercises.commonMistakes: Setting the bench too steep so it turns into a shoulder press, or bouncing the bar off the chest.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the incline dumbbell press with a light load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the upper chest and shoulders and supports both the bench press and the overhead press.

exercises.name: Board Press
instructions: Lie on the bench and have a partner hold a board on your chest, or strap one in place.
Take your bench grip and unrack the bar.
Lower under control until the bar touches the board while the upper body stays tight.
Press back to lockout with a controlled, fast drive.
exercises.formCue: Touch the board, do not sink into it.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the bar crash into the board, or relaxing so the board shifts.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the floor press, which shortens the range without a partner.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The shortened range lets you train the top half of the press with heavier loads.

exercises.name: Deficit Deadlift
instructions: Stand on a plate or low platform with the loaded bar over the middle of the feet.
Bend down and grip the bar, set the back flat, and pull the slack out of the bar.
Push the floor away and lift by extending the knees and hips together.
Stand fully upright, then lower the bar under control along the legs.
exercises.formCue: Stay over the bar and push the floor away.
exercises.commonMistakes: Using a platform so tall the lower back rounds, or letting the hips rise before the bar moves.
exercises.beginnerModification: Pull from the floor, or use a very small deficit with a light load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The longer pull builds strength in the first part of the lift off the floor.

exercises.name: Pause Deadlift
instructions: Set up with the bar over the middle of the foot, grip it, breathe in, and brace.
Lift the bar a few centimetres off the floor and stop.
Hold that position for one to three seconds with the bar close and the back flat.
Finish the pull to a full stand, then lower the bar under control.
exercises.formCue: Hold your position, bar against the legs.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the bar drift forward during the hold, or pausing so briefly it does not count.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light load and a one-second pause until you can hold still.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The hold teaches a strong, balanced position at the point where many deadlifts go wrong.

exercises.name: Stiff-Leg Deadlift
instructions: Stand tall holding the bar with an overhand grip, feet about hip width.
Keep the knees nearly straight and the back flat, and bend at the hips to lower the bar.
Stop when the hamstrings are tight and before the lower back starts to round.
Extend the hips to stand back up.
exercises.formCue: Hips back, back flat, feel the hamstrings.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach further, or bending the knees until it becomes a regular deadlift.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the Romanian deadlift with a soft knee bend and a shorter range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It loads the hamstrings at long length, which supports every pull from the floor.

exercises.name: Good Morning
instructions: Set the bar on your back as you would for a back squat and brace the trunk.
Unlock the knees slightly and push the hips back, lowering the chest under control.
Keep the back flat and the weight over the whole foot as far down as you can hold position.
Drive the hips forward to stand back up.
exercises.formCue: Hips back, back stays set.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the back soften at the bottom, or turning it into a squat by bending the knees too much.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practice the hinge with a dowel or empty bar, or use a back extension.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the back and hip strength that keeps squats and pulls from folding forward.

exercises.name: Seated Good Morning
instructions: Straddle a bench with the bar on your back as for a back squat, knees bent and feet flat in front of you.
Set the back tight and flat.
Bend forward at the hips as far as you can without the back softening.
Return to upright by extending the hips, keeping the back set the whole time.
exercises.formCue: Long spine, fold at the hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the back to get lower, or loading it like a squat.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use an empty bar or a dowel and a shorter range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the back to hold its position with light loads and little stress on the legs.

exercises.name: Pendlay Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, mid and upper back, rear delts, biceps
instructions: Stand over the bar, hinge at the hips with the knees bent until the trunk is close to horizontal, and take a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Brace the trunk the way you would for a pull from the floor.
Row the bar to the abdomen and squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower the bar until it rests on the floor, then reset before the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Chest down, pull to the belt, back to the floor.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing up with each rep so the hips do the work, or not letting the bar settle on the floor.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower the load, or use a chest-supported row to learn the pull without holding the hinge.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Each rep starts from a dead stop, so the upper back does the work instead of momentum.

exercises.name: Yoke Walk
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, trunk, upper back, calves
instructions: Set the crossbar just below shoulder height and stand under it with the bar across the upper traps, as in a high-bar squat.
Press the hands out against the uprights, take a big breath and brace.
Stand the yoke up with a narrow to medium stance and let it settle before you move.
Walk with short, quick steps, eyes forward and the feet close to the midline.
Stop, bend the knees and set the yoke down under control.
exercises.formCue: Short fast steps, eyes on the finish.
exercises.commonMistakes: Taking long strides so the yoke swings, or looking down and folding forward under the bar.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with the empty frame or a load you could squat for many reps and cover a short distance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the trunk and hips to stay rigid under a heavy load while moving.

exercises.name: Farmer's Walk (Handles)
exercises.musclesWorked: Grip, traps, upper back, trunk, glutes
instructions: Stand between the two loaded handles and squat down to grip both in the middle.
Lift both at the same time with the legs, keeping a flat back, and stand tall with arms straight.
Walk with short, quick steps, chest up and shoulders back.
Finish the full distance, then lower both handles together by bending the knees.
exercises.formCue: Stand tall, quick feet, crush the handles.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning far forward to chase speed, or shrugging the shoulders up so they tire early.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use dumbbells or kettlebells and a shorter distance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Long handles let you carry far more than dumbbells, which builds grip and back endurance fast.

exercises.name: Zercher Carry
exercises.musclesWorked: Abs, obliques, upper back, biceps, glutes
instructions: Take the bar from a rack set at waist height into the crooks of the elbows.
Clasp the hands or make fists in front of the chest and keep the elbows close to the ribs.
Stand tall, brace and walk slowly with an upright torso.
Return the bar to the rack or lower it to blocks under control.
exercises.formCue: Elbows in, chest tall, slow steps.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the upper back round over the bar, or rushing so the load swings.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hug a light sandbag or medicine ball in the same position.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A load held in front makes the trunk and upper back fight to stay upright with every step.

exercises.name: Bottoms-Up Carry
instructions: Hold a light kettlebell by the handle with the bell pointing up.
Keep the upper arm level with the floor in front of you and the wrist straight.
Squeeze the handle and walk slowly with the torso upright.
Switch hands after each length.
exercises.formCue: Straight wrist, crush the handle.
exercises.commonMistakes: Going too heavy so the bell tips, or letting the wrist bend back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the position standing still before you walk with it.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The unstable bell makes the grip and the small shoulder muscles steady the load.

exercises.name: Sandbag Bear Hug Carry
exercises.musclesWorked: Upper back, biceps, abs, glutes, quads
instructions: Straddle the bag with a wide stance and grab around its body, not the handles.
Pull it up to the lap, then re-grip and stand with the bag high on the chest.
Wrap both arms around it and squeeze it into the torso.
Walk with steady steps and short breaths, then lower the bag to the floor with bent knees.
exercises.formCue: Bag high, squeeze it tight.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the bag slide down to the belly, or leaning back too far to prop it up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter bag and shorter distances, resting the bag on a bench between trips.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A shifting load you have to hug teaches bracing and breathing under pressure.

exercises.name: Sandbag Over Bar
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, upper back, biceps, quads
instructions: Stand close to the bar with the bag between wide feet and grip around the body of the bag.
Lift it to the lap with a flat back and sit it on the thighs.
Re-grip over the top of the bag and pull it high on the chest.
Drive the hips and legs up fast and roll the bag over the bar.
Walk around and repeat from the other side.
exercises.formCue: Lap it, hug it high, hips through.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing too far from the bar, or trying to lift the bag slowly with the arms.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light bag and a waist-high target such as a box.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains a full pick from the floor to chest height with an object that will not stay still.

exercises.name: Atlas Stone Over Bar
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, spinal erectors, upper back, biceps, forearms
instructions: Straddle the stone with feet about shoulder-width apart and reach the hands as far under it as you can.
Squeeze the stone with the arms and stand until you can sit it on the lap.
Sit back with the stone on the thighs and re-grip over the top, chest pressed against it.
Drive the hips up and forward and roll the stone up the chest.
Push it over the bar and step back as it drops.
exercises.formCue: Squeeze, lap, hips through.
exercises.commonMistakes: Trying to curl the stone up with the arms, or standing too far from the bar.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the same lift with a sandbag or a light stone and a low bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the classic strongman test of picking an awkward object off the ground and getting it high.

exercises.name: Atlas Stone to Shoulder
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, spinal erectors, upper back, biceps
instructions: Straddle the stone, squeeze it between the forearms and lift it to the lap.
Sit back, re-grip with the arms over the top and pull the stone into the chest.
Stand up fast, extending the hips and knees and rolling the stone up the torso.
Roll it onto one shoulder and stand tall with it under control.
Drop it forward onto a mat and step clear.
exercises.formCue: Lap, stand fast, roll to the shoulder.
exercises.commonMistakes: Stalling at the chest because the hips did not drive, or losing balance with the stone on the shoulder.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a sandbag to shoulder until the lap and hip drive are consistent.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Finishing on the shoulder demands a stronger, higher hip drive than loading over a bar.

exercises.name: Atlas Stone Platform Load
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, spinal erectors, upper back, forearms
instructions: Stand a foot or so from the platform with the stone between the feet.
Wrap the arms around the stone and lift it to the lap with the chest up.
Squeeze the knees in to hold the stone, lean back slightly and re-grip over the top.
Extend the hips hard, roll the stone up the body and place it on the platform.
exercises.formCue: Roll it up your body, do not press it.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding hard through the lift without bracing, or trying to press the stone up with the arms.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light stone or sandbag and a platform at waist height.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Placing the stone on a platform adds control at the top, the way stones are loaded in competition.

exercises.name: Log Clean and Press
exercises.musclesWorked: Shoulders, triceps, upper back, glutes, quads, trunk
instructions: Stand close to the log with feet about hip-width apart and grip the neutral handles.
Pull the log to the lap with a flat back and sit down with it on the thighs.
Drive the hips through and roll the log up the body to the top of the chest with the elbows high.
Dip the knees a little, drive with the legs and press the log overhead.
Lock the elbows with the head through, then lower to the chest and down to the lap.
exercises.formCue: Roll it high, dip, drive, head through.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pressing before the legs finish their drive, or leaning far back under the log.
exercises.beginnerModification: Learn with an empty log, or press it from a rack before adding the clean.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The thick, neutral-grip log builds overhead strength from the ground up in one lift.

exercises.name: Log Press (From Rack)
exercises.musclesWorked: Shoulders, triceps, upper chest, quads, trunk
instructions: Take the log from a rack so it rests on the upper chest with the elbows up and a neutral grip.
Brace and dip the knees a few centimetres with the torso upright.
Drive up with the legs and press the log overhead in one motion.
Finish with the elbows locked, the shoulders shrugged up and the head through, then lower to the chest.
exercises.formCue: Short dip, hard drive, lock it out.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dipping forward onto the toes, or resting the log too low so the elbows drop.
exercises.beginnerModification: Press it strictly with no leg drive at a light load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Skipping the clean lets you train the press itself with more volume.

exercises.name: Axle Clean and Press
exercises.musclesWorked: Shoulders, triceps, forearms, upper back, glutes, quads
instructions: Grip the thick bar a little wider than shoulder width with the feet about hip-width apart.
Pull from the floor with a flat back and drive the hips to bring the bar to the shoulders.
Settle the bar across the front of the shoulders and re-set a full grip.
Dip slightly, drive with the legs and press to a full lockout with the head through.
exercises.formCue: Reset your grip, then dip and drive.
exercises.commonMistakes: Gripping too narrow on the thick bar, or pressing with the bar drifting forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a standard barbell, or press the axle from a rack to skip the clean.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The thick bar does not spin, so it builds grip and a strong, honest pull to the shoulders.

exercises.name: Tire Flip
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, quads, back, chest, shoulders
instructions: Crouch close to the tire with feet about hip-width apart, the chest and shoulders against it and the hands under the edge.
Keep the back flat and the arms long, and drive forward and up through the legs.
As the tire passes the hips, step in and turn the hands over to a pushing position.
Push the tire over with both arms and follow it forward.
exercises.formCue: Chest on the tire, drive through it, not up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing too far away and lifting it like a deadlift with a round back, or curling it with the arms.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter tire, or train the same pattern with a sled push and a trap bar deadlift.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the hips, knees and ankles to extend together while pushing forward.

exercises.name: Harness Sled Drag
instructions: Attach the sled to a chest or waist harness and walk forward until the strap is tight.
Lean forward from the ankles with a straight line from head to back heel.
Drive each foot back into the ground with powerful, full steps.
Keep the trunk braced and the lean steady until the distance is done.
exercises.formCue: Lean in, push the ground behind you.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending at the waist instead of leaning as one piece, or taking short, choppy steps that stall the sled.
exercises.beginnerModification: Load the sled lightly and walk it rather than driving hard.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A heavy forward drag builds horizontal leg drive with very little impact.

source.name: Sports Medicine - Open (systematic review of strongman exercises)

exercises.name: Keg Carry
exercises.musclesWorked: Upper back, biceps, abs, glutes, quads
instructions: Tip the keg, grip the rim at one end and the base at the other, and lift it to the lap.
Stand and hug it high against the chest, or roll it onto one shoulder.
Brace and walk with quick, even steps, keeping the torso upright.
Lower it back to the lap and then to the floor with bent knees.
exercises.formCue: Keep it high and close.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the keg slip low so the back rounds, or twisting to one side under a shouldered keg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Carry an empty or lightly filled keg, or use a sandbag.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A rigid, bulky load that you cannot grip well forces the whole trunk to hold it in place.

source.name: Sports Medicine - Open (systematic review of strongman exercises)

exercises.name: Mountain Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Feet, calves, quads, glutes, deep core, postural muscles
instructions: Stand with your big toes close and heels slightly apart, or feet hip-width if that feels steadier.
Lift and spread your toes, set them down, and balance your weight evenly across both feet.
Firm your thighs without locking the knees and stack hips over ankles and shoulders over hips.
Let your arms hang with palms forward, level your chin, and breathe slowly for the full hold.
exercises.formCue: Ears over shoulders, shoulders over hips, hips over ankles.
exercises.commonMistakes: Locking the knees back and letting the ribs flare forward so the lower back arches.
exercises.beginnerModification: Stand with feet hip-width apart, or with your back lightly against a wall to feel the stacked line.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the stacked, balanced stance every other standing pose is built from.

exercises.name: Standing Forward Fold
instructions: Stand tall with hands on your hips and feet hip-width apart.
Hinge forward from the hips, keeping the front of your torso long as you lower.
Rest your hands on the floor, on blocks, or on your shins and let your head hang heavy.
Keep a soft bend in the knees and shift a little weight toward the balls of your feet.
Come up by bending the knees and rising with a long back.
exercises.formCue: Fold from the hips, not the waist.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding hard through the lower back to reach the floor, or locking the knees and pulling on the hamstrings.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bend the knees generously and rest your hands on blocks or a chair seat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It lengthens the whole back of the body and is the linking position in most flows.

exercises.name: Half Lift
instructions: Start in a standing forward fold with feet hip-width apart.
Place your fingertips on the floor, on blocks, or on your shins.
Breathe in and lift your chest until your back is flat and roughly level with the floor.
Reach the crown of your head forward, keep the back of your neck long, then fold again on the breath out.
exercises.formCue: Flat back, long neck, chest forward.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the upper back, or cranking the head up and pinching the neck.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bend the knees slightly and put your hands on your shins or thighs so the back can flatten.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains a clean hip hinge with a long spine, which carries into every forward bend and lift.

exercises.name: Chaturanga (Plank to Low Plank)
instructions: Set a strong plank with shoulders over wrists and legs firm.
Shift forward a little so your shoulders move just ahead of your wrists.
Bend your elbows straight back along your ribs and lower in one piece.
Stop when your upper arms are about level with the floor and elbows sit over wrists.
Hold for a breath, then press back up or move on to your next pose.
exercises.formCue: Elbows hug the ribs, body moves as one board.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping the shoulders below elbow height, or letting the hips sag or pike.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower your knees to the floor first and keep the same straight line from knees to head.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the pressing strength and shoulder control that keep flowing sequences safe.

exercises.name: Upward-Facing Dog
exercises.musclesWorked: Spinal erectors, glutes, triceps, chest, hip flexors
instructions: Lie face down with legs hip-width apart and hands on the floor beside your lower ribs.
Press the tops of your feet into the floor so your thighs switch on.
Breathe in, straighten your arms, and lift your chest and thighs off the floor.
Stack wrists under shoulders, draw your shoulders back, and keep your neck in line with your upper back.
Hold for a few breaths, then lower down or lift the hips to Downward Dog.
exercises.formCue: Thighs off the floor, chest pulls forward and up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Hanging in the shoulders with them up by the ears, or sagging into the lower back with relaxed legs.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the thighs and hips on the floor and bend the elbows for Cobra Pose.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It opens the chest and front of the hips while strengthening the arms and back.

exercises.name: Warrior One
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, hip flexors, calves, shoulders
instructions: Step one foot forward between your hands and bend that knee over the ankle.
Turn your back heel down so the back foot angles about 45 degrees.
Press the back thigh straight and firm the outer edge of the back foot into the floor.
Rise up, turn your chest toward the front, and reach both arms overhead.
Hold for five to ten breaths, then switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Back leg strong, front knee tracks over the ankle.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the front knee cave inward, or dumping into the lower back as the arms go up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the stance, take the feet wider side to side, and keep hands on hips.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds leg strength and opens the hip of the back leg in one hold.

exercises.name: Triangle Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Hamstrings, inner thighs, obliques, glutes, shoulders
instructions: Stand with feet wide, front foot turned out and back foot turned slightly in.
Reach your arms out level with your shoulders and keep both legs straight but not locked.
Reach forward over the front leg, then tip from the hip and lower your front hand to your shin, a block, or the floor.
Stack the top arm over the bottom arm and open your chest to the side.
Hold for five breaths, press through the feet to rise, and switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Long on both sides of the waist.
exercises.commonMistakes: Collapsing the bottom side of the torso to reach the floor, or locking the front knee.
exercises.beginnerModification: Rest your bottom hand on a block or high on the shin and keep a small bend in the front knee.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It stretches the hamstrings and inner thighs while teaching the legs to hold a steady base.

exercises.name: Extended Side Angle
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, inner thighs, obliques, shoulders
instructions: Start in a wide stance with the front foot turned out and arms reaching out to the sides.
Bend the front knee toward 90 degrees, keeping it over the ankle.
Lean over the front leg and place your forearm on the thigh or your hand outside the front foot.
Sweep the top arm over your ear so your body makes one line from back heel to fingertips.
Hold for 30 to 60 seconds, then rise and change sides.
exercises.formCue: One long line from back heel to top fingertips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the front knee drift inward, or sinking all the weight onto the bottom arm.
exercises.beginnerModification: Rest the forearm lightly on the front thigh, or put the bottom hand on a block.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the legs while lengthening the whole side of the body.

exercises.name: Half Moon Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, outer hips, hamstrings, ankles, obliques
instructions: From Triangle Pose, bend the front knee and look down at the floor.
Place your bottom hand a little ahead of the front foot, under the shoulder, on the floor or a block.
Shift your weight onto the front leg and lift the back leg until it is level with your hip.
Straighten the standing leg without locking it and turn your chest open to the side.
Reach the top arm up, hold for a few breaths, then step back down with control.
exercises.formCue: Flex the lifted foot and push it into an imaginary wall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Locking the standing knee, or letting the top hip roll forward so the chest faces the floor.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a tall block under the bottom hand and practise with your back near a wall.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains single-leg balance and outer-hip strength at the same time.

exercises.name: Tree Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, outer hips, calves, feet, deep core
instructions: Stand in Mountain Pose and shift your weight onto one foot.
Place the sole of the other foot on the inner calf or inner thigh of the standing leg, never on the knee.
Press foot and leg into each other and keep your hips level and facing forward.
Bring your hands together at your chest, or reach them overhead once you are steady.
Fix your eyes on one point, hold, then change sides.
exercises.formCue: Foot into leg, leg into foot.
exercises.commonMistakes: Resting the foot against the side of the knee, or hiking the hip of the lifted leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the toes of the lifted foot on the floor with the heel on the ankle, or stand next to a wall.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds ankle and hip stability and the focus needed for every balance.

exercises.name: Eagle Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, outer hips, upper back, shoulders
instructions: Stand tall, bend both knees, and shift your weight onto one leg.
Cross the other thigh over the standing thigh and hook the foot behind the calf if you can.
Reach your arms forward, cross one elbow over the other, and wrap the forearms so the palms meet.
Lift your elbows to shoulder height, sit a little lower, and keep your chest upright.
Hold for about five breaths, unwind, and repeat on the other side.
exercises.formCue: Sit low, lift the elbows, squeeze everything to the midline.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing up tall out of the squat, or tipping the chest forward to stay balanced.
exercises.beginnerModification: Cross the legs and rest the top toes on the floor like a kickstand, and hold opposite shoulders with the arms.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It challenges balance while stretching the upper back and outer hips.

exercises.name: Bridge Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, spinal erectors, chest, hip flexors
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet hip-width apart, close to your hips.
Rest your arms by your sides with palms down.
Breathe in, press through your feet, and lift your hips.
Keep your thighs parallel, and if it is comfortable, clasp your hands under you and roll the shoulders in.
Hold for several breaths, then lower your spine slowly to the floor.
exercises.formCue: Press the heels down and keep the knees pointing straight ahead.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the knees splay out, or flattening and pressing the back of the neck into the floor.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift only part way, or rest your hips on a block for a supported version.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It opens the chest and hips while strengthening the whole back of the body.

exercises.name: Boat Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Abdominals, hip flexors, spinal erectors, quads
instructions: Sit with knees bent, feet on the floor, and hands behind your thighs.
Lean back a little with a long spine until you balance just behind your sitting bones.
Lift your feet so your shins are level with the floor.
Reach your arms forward beside your legs, and straighten the legs only if your back stays long.
Hold for 10 to 20 seconds, building toward a minute, then lower with control.
exercises.formCue: Chest lifted, lower back long.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back and sinking the chest once the legs go up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the knees bent and hold the backs of your thighs, or keep the toes on the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds deep abdominal and hip flexor strength with an upright spine.

exercises.name: Low Lunge
instructions: From Downward Dog or hands and knees, step one foot forward between your hands.
Lower the back knee to the floor and rest the top of the back foot down.
Keep the front knee over the ankle and slide the back knee away until you feel the front of that hip stretch.
Lift your chest and reach your arms overhead, or keep hands on your hips.
Hold for up to a minute, then switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Tailbone down, front of the back hip opens.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to lift the chest, or letting the front knee slide far past the toes.
exercises.beginnerModification: Pad the back knee with a folded blanket and keep your hands on blocks or on the front thigh.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It opens the hip flexors and quads that tighten up from sitting.

exercises.name: Lizard Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Hip flexors, inner thighs, hamstrings, glutes
instructions: From a low lunge, walk the front foot toward the outer edge of the mat.
Bring both hands to the floor inside the front foot.
Stay on your hands, or lower your forearms to the floor or to blocks.
Keep the back knee down for an easier hold, or lift it and press the heel back for more load.
Keep your chest reaching forward, hold for five slow breaths, then change sides.
exercises.formCue: Chest forward, hips level.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the upper back to get the elbows down, or letting the front knee collapse inward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the back knee on a pad and stay up on your hands or on blocks.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It reaches the deep hip and inner-thigh range that lunges and squats depend on.

exercises.name: Half Splits
instructions: Start in a low lunge with the back knee on the floor and hands framing the front foot.
Shift your hips back until they sit over the back knee.
Straighten the front leg and flex the foot so the toes point up.
Keep your hips square and walk your hands forward with a long spine.
Hold for five to ten breaths, then switch legs.
exercises.formCue: Lead with the chest, not the forehead.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the spine to chase the shin, or letting the hips drift back past the knee.
exercises.beginnerModification: Put blocks under your hands and keep a small bend in the front knee.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It isolates one hamstring at a time without loading the lower back.

exercises.name: Seated Forward Fold
instructions: Sit with both legs straight in front of you and your feet flexed.
Breathe in and sit tall through the crown of your head.
Breathe out and hinge forward from the hips, keeping the spine long.
Walk your hands forward as far as is comfortable, holding your shins, feet, or a strap.
Lengthen a little on each breath in, ease forward on each breath out, and hold for one to three minutes.
exercises.formCue: Reach the chest toward the toes, not the head toward the knees.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling hard with the arms and rounding the back to get lower.
exercises.beginnerModification: Sit on a folded blanket, bend the knees, and loop a strap around the feet.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It gives the hamstrings and back a long, calm stretch that suits the end of a session.

exercises.name: Bound Angle Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Inner thighs, groin, outer hips, spinal erectors
instructions: Sit tall, bend your knees, and bring the soles of your feet together.
Draw your heels toward your pelvis only as far as is comfortable.
Hold your ankles or feet and let your knees fall out to the sides.
Lift through your chest and keep your pelvis upright rather than slumped.
Stay for one to five minutes, then lift the knees with your hands and stretch the legs out.
exercises.formCue: Sit tall and let the thighs release on their own.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pushing the knees down with the hands or elbows, or slumping through the lower back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Sit on a folded blanket and rest blocks or cushions under each thigh.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It opens the inner thighs and hips while training an upright seated posture.

exercises.name: Happy Baby
exercises.musclesWorked: Inner thighs, glutes, hamstrings, lower back
instructions: Lie on your back and draw both knees toward your chest.
Hold the outer edges of your feet, or your shins or the backs of your thighs.
Open your knees a little wider than your torso and bring them toward your armpits.
Stack each ankle over its knee so the shins point straight up.
Press your feet gently up into your hands as you draw down, and hold for several slow breaths.
exercises.formCue: Tailbone heavy, shoulders soft.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting the head and shoulders, or curling the tailbone far off the floor to reach the feet.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold behind the thighs, or do one leg at a time with the other foot on the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It releases the inner hips and lower back with no load on the spine.

exercises.name: Legs Up the Wall
instructions: Sit sideways next to a wall with one hip close to it.
Lower onto your side, roll onto your back, and swing your legs up the wall.
Shuffle your hips toward the wall until your legs rest comfortably; they do not have to touch it.
Rest your arms by your sides with palms up and let your legs relax.
Breathe slowly for five to ten minutes, then bend your knees, roll to one side, and pause before sitting up.
exercises.formCue: Let the wall hold your legs.
exercises.commonMistakes: Forcing the hips tight to the wall so the hamstrings pull and the lower back lifts.
exercises.beginnerModification: Move your hips further from the wall, bend the knees, or rest your calves on a chair seat instead.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is a simple, fully supported position for winding down after training.

exercises.name: Corpse Pose
instructions: Lie on your back with legs straight and feet hip-width apart or wider, letting the feet fall out.
Rest your arms a little away from your sides with the palms up.
Lengthen the back of your neck and let your body feel heavy on the floor.
Soften your jaw and face, close your eyes, and let your breath slow down on its own.
Stay for at least five minutes, then roll to one side before you sit up.
exercises.formCue: Nothing to hold, nothing to fix.
exercises.commonMistakes: Skipping it, or lying there while planning the rest of the day.
exercises.beginnerModification: Put a rolled blanket under your knees and a thin cushion under your head.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It gives the body time to settle so the work of the session can sink in.

exercises.name: Garland Pose (Deep Squat Hold)
exercises.musclesWorked: Ankles, calves, inner thighs, glutes, lower back
instructions: Stand with feet a little wider than your hips and toes turned out slightly.
Bend your knees and lower your hips all the way down between your heels.
Bring your palms together and press your elbows gently against your inner knees.
Lift your chest and lengthen your spine while the knees track over the toes.
Hold for 30 to 60 seconds, then press through the feet to stand.
exercises.formCue: Heels heavy, chest tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the heels float with no support, or collapsing the chest and rounding the back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Put a folded blanket under your heels, sit on a low block, or hold a door frame for balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It restores the ankle and hip range that a comfortable full squat needs.

exercises.name: Sun Salutation A
exercises.musclesWorked: Shoulders, chest, triceps, core, hamstrings, hip flexors
instructions: Stand in Mountain Pose, breathe in and sweep your arms overhead, then breathe out and fold forward.
Breathe in to a Half Lift, then breathe out, step back to plank, and lower through Chaturanga.
Breathe in to Upward-Facing Dog, then breathe out and lift your hips to Downward Dog.
Hold Downward Dog for three to five breaths, then step or walk your feet to your hands.
Breathe in to a Half Lift, breathe out to fold, then rise with arms overhead and return to Mountain Pose.
exercises.formCue: One breath, one movement.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rushing ahead of the breath, and letting the hips sag in the plank and lowering phase.
exercises.beginnerModification: Drop the knees for the lowering phase and swap Upward-Facing Dog for Cobra Pose.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It warms the whole body and links breath to movement in under a minute per round.

exercises.name: Hip Controlled Articular Rotation
exercises.musclesWorked: Hip flexors, glutes, deep hip rotators, obliques
instructions: Stand tall beside a wall or chair, hold it lightly, and brace your trunk so the pelvis stays still.
Lift one knee straight up in front of you as high as you can without leaning back.
Open the knee out to the side, then turn the thigh inward so the foot swings out and back behind you.
Lower the knee under your hip, then reverse the whole circle back to the start.
Move slowly enough that each circle takes several seconds, and stay inside a pain-free range.
exercises.formCue: Biggest circle you can make with nothing else moving.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swinging the leg with momentum, or tilting and twisting the pelvis to fake a bigger circle.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it on hands and knees, where the floor steadies the trunk, and make a smaller circle.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It takes the hip through its full active range so you keep the motion you already own.

exercises.name: Shoulder Controlled Articular Rotation
exercises.musclesWorked: Rotator cuff, deltoids, upper back, serratus
instructions: Stand tall with ribs down, one arm straight by your side, and the other hand in a light fist.
Raise the working arm forward and up, thumb leading, until it is beside your ear.
At the top, turn the arm inward so the palm faces out and continue reaching back and down behind you.
Finish with the back of the hand near your hip, then reverse the path to the start.
Move slowly, keep the torso still, and stay inside a pain-free range.
exercises.formCue: Slow circle, quiet ribs.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching the back or leaning the torso to get the arm further, and rushing through the stiff part.
exercises.beginnerModification: Stand side-on to a wall an arm's length away and trace a smaller circle beside it.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the shoulder through its full active range before pressing, pulling, or hanging.

exercises.name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Drill
exercises.musclesWorked: Calves, soleus, Achilles tendon, ankle joint
instructions: Face a wall in a short split stance or half kneel with your front toes a few centimetres from it.
Keep the front foot pointing straight ahead and the heel flat on the floor.
Drive the front knee forward over the middle toes until it touches the wall or the heel wants to lift.
Ease back and repeat for slow reps, moving the foot further from the wall only if the heel stays down.
Switch sides and compare the two ankles.
exercises.formCue: Heel glued down, knee over the middle toes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the heel peel up, or letting the arch collapse and the knee dive inward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with the toes almost touching the wall and hold the wall for balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Better ankle bend lets the knees travel forward so squats and lunges sit deeper and feel steadier.

exercises.name: Foam Roller Thoracic Extension
instructions: Sit on the floor with knees bent and place a foam roller across your mid-back, below the shoulder blades.
Support your head with your hands and keep your elbows pointing forward and up.
Keep your hips on the floor and your ribs down, then lean back gently over the roller.
Pause for a breath, curl back up, and repeat a few times.
Shift the roller a little higher and repeat, staying on the upper and middle back only.
exercises.formCue: Hips down, ribs down, bend from the upper back.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting the hips or flaring the ribs so the lower back arches instead of the upper back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a rolled towel instead of a roller and take a smaller range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It restores upper-back extension, which overhead reaching and good posture both need.
